   101	// the fixed tables use absolute coords and would fall off a smaller pitch.
   102	// The UI toggle (settings → experimental) can still turn it OFF for A/B, and
   103	// probes can force-OFF with EMERGENT_POS=0.
   104	let _emergentPos: boolean | null = null; // null = use the default (ON)
   105	export function setEmergentPos(on: boolean): void {
   106	  _emergentPos = on;
   107	}
   108	export function emergentPosOn(): boolean {
   109	  if (_emergentPos !== null) return _emergentPos; // explicit UI / probe override
   110	  // typeof guard: `process` is undefined in the browser bundle — never throw.
   111	  if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.env && process.env.EMERGENT_POS === '0') return false;
   112	  return true; // DEFAULT ON
   113	}
   114	
   115	/** How far up/down the pitch each tactical mode pushes the block. */
   116	const MODE_SHIFT: Record<TeamMode, number> = {
   117	  Attack: 10,
   118	  BuildUp: 4,
   119	  CounterAttack: 8,
   120	  Press: 6,
   121	  Defend: -8,
   122	  ResetShape: 0,
   123	};
   124	
   125	/**
   126	 * World-space formation target for a player. `hasBall` decides whether width
   127	 * (attackingWidth) or compactness (defensiveCompactness) shapes the block.
   128	 */
   129	export function formationSpot(p: Player, team: Team, ball: Ball, hasBall: boolean, opp?: Team): V2 {
   130	  // EMERGENT POSITIONING FIELD (Phase B1, toggle — the user's #1 emergence
   131	  // ask: shape must grow from role + genes + live state, not a hand-authored
   132	  // MENU). Behind a flag so it A/Bs cleanly against the fixed tables
   133	  // (positioning-shape.ts) before it can replace them. OFF = today's behavior.
   134	  if (emergentPosOn()) return emergentStation(p, team, ball, hasBall, opp);
   135	  const g = team.genome;
   136	  const base = hasBall
   137	    ? ATTACK_FORMATIONS[team.style.formationAtk][p.index]
   138	    : DEFEND_FORMATIONS[team.style.formationDef][p.index];
   139	
   140	  // Block slides toward the ball along x (local coords), capped at ±10m.
   141	  const ballLocalX = team.localX(ball.pos.x);
   142	  const slide = clamp(ballLocalX * 0.3, -10, 10);
   143	
   144	  // formationDepth: 0 = sit 6m deeper, 1 = push 6m higher.
   145	  const depth = (g.formationDepth - 0.5) * 12;
   146	
   147	  // PRESSING BUYS ITS RISK (Phase 83, the goal-inflation fix): a pressing
   148	  // side's defensive block steps UP with its press gene — outfielders only,
   149	  // defending phase only. Before this, line height was formationDepth's
   150	  // alone, so evolution could chase-press from a deep couch: turnovers with
   151	  // ZERO space conceded behind — the free lunch that rode pressIntensity to
   152	  // 0.88 and the league to 6-7 goals (phase-82 anatomy). Now the line you
   153	  // press with is the line the through-ball/route-one/chip channels attack.
   154	  const pressUp = hasBall || p.role === 'GK' ? 0 : (g.pressIntensity - 0.5) * 8;
   155	
   156	  let x = base.x + slide + depth + pressUp + MODE_SHIFT[team.mode];
   157	
   158	  // Rest defence (Phase 31): the DF slot NEVER joins the siege. With the
   159	  // ball deep in the opponent half, slide (+10) + Attack shift (+10) used
   160	  // to push even the last outfielder past halfway — the attacking team had
   161	  // literally nobody covering, so every turnover was an uncontested
   162	  // breakaway. That hole is what let a 5v6 side out-score its own
   163	  // full-strength baseline once the open-run economy paid honestly
   164	  // (counters were ALL open runs). One cover man keeps counters real —
   165	  // beatable by pace or a dragged block, never free.
   166	  // −12, not −5: a cover man AT halfway is already beaten by the time a
   167	  // counter carrier enters the open-run zone (28m out) — he has to start
   168	  // goal-side of the race, near his base spot, to ever contest it.
   169	  if (p.index === 1 && p.role !== 'GK') {
   170	    if (hasBall) {
   171	      // Rest-defense depth is now the SWEEPER gene's possession face
   172	      // (Phase 88): 0.5 = the old hardcoded −12 exactly; the full libero
   173	      // (1) holds −16 even mid-siege, the bold stopper (0) dares −8.
   174	      x = Math.min(x, -8 - (g.coverBias ?? 0.5) * 8);
   175	    } else {
   176	      // THE SWEEPER (Phase 88, school #2 — catenaccio): the DF slot sits
   177	      // off his own line by the gene — behind it (libero: the man who
   178	      // meets whatever beats the first wave, at the price of playing
   179	      // everyone onside) or ahead of it (stopper: early interceptions,
   180	      // gambling the space behind). 0.5 = today's flat line.
   181	      x -= ((g.coverBias ?? 0.5) - 0.5) * 8;
   182	    }
   183	  }
   184	
   185	  // Width: stretch when we have the ball, squeeze when we don't. The
   186	  // in-possession floor is 1.0 (Phase 27.1) — an attacking shape should
   187	  // never be narrower than its base lanes.
   188	  let widthMul = hasBall
   189	    ? 1.0 + g.attackingWidth * 0.55 // 1.0 .. 1.55
   190	    : 1.15 - g.defensiveCompactness * 0.6; // 1.15 .. 0.55
   191	  // Zonal shape stays HONEST-WIDE (Phase 30.4): a zone defence covers
   192	  // width by definition — it may not also collapse into the central
   193	  // corridor, or its parked bodies dead-lane the entire pitch (measured:
   194	  // zonal sides conceded 3.6 shots/match vs man's 8 — the league's shot
   195	  // volume collapsed with half the clubs zonal).
   196	  if (!hasBall && team.style.scheme === 'zonal') widthMul = Math.max(widthMul, 0.95);
   197	  let y = base.y * widthMul;
   198	
   199	  // Compact teams also drag their block a little toward the ball's y.
   200	  if (!hasBall) y += (ball.pos.y - y * team.attackDir) * team.attackDir * g.defensiveCompactness * 0.25;
   201	
   202	  // Weak-side far-post pull (Phase 31): when the attack is deep AND wide,
   203	  // the far winger leaves the touchline and attacks the back post — the
   204	  // overload that punishes a ball-side defensive shift, and the second
   205	  // body a cutback or deep cross finds. The strong-side winger keeps the
   206	  // width; the pull releases as soon as the ball comes back central.
   207	  if (
   208	    hasBall && p.role === 'WG' && ballLocalX > HALF_L - 20 &&
   209	    Math.abs(ball.pos.y) > 12 && Math.sign(y) !== Math.sign(ball.pos.y)
   210	  ) {
   211	    y *= 0.3;
   212	  }
   213	
   214	  if (p.role === 'GK') {
   215	    // Keepers hold a narrow band in front of goal regardless of mode.
   216	    x = clamp(base.x + (g.keeperAggression - 0.5) * 4, -HALF_L + 1, -HALF_L + 11);
   217	    y = clamp(ball.pos.y * 0.25, -GOAL_WIDTH / 2, GOAL_WIDTH / 2);
   218	    return v2(x * team.attackDir, y);
   219	  }
   220	
   221	  x = clamp(x, -HALF_L + 3, HALF_L - 7);
   222	  y = clamp(y, -HALF_W + 2, HALF_W - 2);
   223	  return v2(x * team.attackDir, y);
   224	}
   225	
   226	/**
   227	 * EMERGENT POSITIONING FIELD (Phase B1-a). Replaces the fixed formation TABLE
   228	 * with a ROLE-anchored field: a role gives a coarse depth+lane TENDENCY (a
   229	 * dimension, like an attribute — not a hand-drawn shape), and the actual
   230	 * station grows from that + the live game state, weighted by GENES. So the
   231	 * team's SHAPE and "style" emerge from gene weights, not from us picking
   232	 * wide-212 vs low-32. B1-a lands the structural swap + a REAL, gene-weighted
   233	 * strong/weak-side shift (the B0 probe found the old ~2m drag was token). The
   234	 * anti-clump / space-value terms (kill the bus box-crowd, no clumping) are
   235	 * B1-b. Opponent-relative positioning is B2. Same sensible modifiers as the
   236	 * table path (slide/depth/press/rest-defence/width) so shape stays sane.
   237	 */
   238	function emergentStation(p: Player, team: Team, ball: Ball, hasBall: boolean, opp?: Team): V2 {
   239	  const g = team.genome;
   240	  // Role → coarse (depth fraction of HALF_L, lane fraction of HALF_W). WGs take
   241	  // a side from their slot (L=3, R=4); everyone else holds a central lane.
   242	  const laneSign = p.index === 3 ? -1 : p.index === 4 ? 1 : 0;
   243	  let depthFrac: number;
   244	  let laneFrac: number;
   245	  switch (p.role) {
   246	    case 'GK': depthFrac = -0.91; laneFrac = 0; break;
   247	    case 'DF': depthFrac = -0.45; laneFrac = 0; break;
   248	    case 'MF': depthFrac = -0.12; laneFrac = laneSign * 0.12; break;
   249	    case 'WG': depthFrac = 0.05; laneFrac = laneSign * 0.6; break;
   250	    default: depthFrac = 0.12; laneFrac = 0; break; // ST
   251	  }
   252	
   253	  const ballLocalX = team.localX(ball.pos.x);
   254	  const slide = clamp(ballLocalX * 0.3, -10, 10);
   255	  const depth = (g.formationDepth - 0.5) * 12;
   256	  const pressUp = hasBall || p.role === 'GK' ? 0 : (g.pressIntensity - 0.5) * 8;
   257	  let x = depthFrac * HALF_L + slide + depth + pressUp + MODE_SHIFT[team.mode];
   258	
   259	  // Rest defence — the DF slot never joins the siege (same as the table path).
   260	  if (p.index === 1 && p.role !== 'GK') {
   261	    if (hasBall) x = Math.min(x, -8 - (g.coverBias ?? 0.5) * 8);
   262	    else x -= ((g.coverBias ?? 0.5) - 0.5) * 8;
   263	  }
   264	
   265	  // Width: stretch in possession, squeeze out of it.
   266	  let widthMul = hasBall ? 1.0 + g.attackingWidth * 0.55 : 1.15 - g.defensiveCompactness * 0.6;
   267	  if (!hasBall && team.style.scheme === 'zonal') widthMul = Math.max(widthMul, 0.95);
   268	  let y = laneFrac * HALF_W * widthMul;
   269	
   270	  // ⭐ STRONG / WEAK SIDE (B1-a, the real thing): the block slides toward the
   271	  // BALL'S y — overload the ball side in attack, protect it in defence —
   272	  // weighted by width (attack) / compactness (defence). The B0 probe measured
   273	  // the old drag at only ~2m and gene-flat; this is a genuine, selectable
   274	  // ball-side shift, so a team that commits to it gets a real strong side and
   275	  // leaves a weak side (which width/switches then punish — emergent).
   276	  // TRANSLATE the block ball-side (add a common offset) — do NOT converge each
   277	  // man onto ball.y (that collapses the lateral spread; the first B1-a cut did,
   278	  // halving spreadY). The whole shape slides over, keeping its width.
   279	  const ballSideShift = hasBall ? 0.18 + g.attackingWidth * 0.22 : 0.18 + g.defensiveCompactness * 0.25;
   280	  y += ball.pos.y * ballSideShift;
   281	
   282	  // ⭐ B2: the block tracks the OPPONENT's push, not just the ball (the user's
   283	  // "阵型也不会随着对面的移动而移动"). The defensive spine (DF/MF) holds a line
   284	  // just goal-side of the opponents' advanced players — step UP when they sit
   285	  // deep, DROP when they push. A modest convergence, so the block MOVES WITH
   286	  // the opponent line while keeping its own depth structure. Only when we have
   287	  // an opponent reference (executor/marking path); attack + supportSpot skip it.
   288	  if (!hasBall && opp && (p.role === 'DF' || p.role === 'MF')) {
   289	    const adv = opp.players
   290	      .filter((o) => o.role !== 'GK' && !o.sentOff)
   291	      .map((o) => team.localX(o.pos.x))
   292	      .sort((a, b) => a - b);
   293	    if (adv.length >= 2) {
   294	      const holdLine = adv[1] - 3; // goal-side of their 2nd-deepest attacker
   295	      x += (holdLine - x) * 0.14;
   296	    }
   297	  }
   298	
   299	  // ⭐ B1-b: ANTI-CLUMP + position by VALUE (the user's "一堆人挤自家禁区,防守
   300	  // 帮助 0" / "别扎堆"). Stations REPEL each other, so bodies SPREAD to cover
   301	  // space instead of piling into the same zone — the emergent alternative to a
   302	  // fixed lattice AND to the bus box-crowd. Computed in the local-x / world-y
   303	  // frame (x is local, y unflipped). Plus a box-crowd relief: with no ball
   304	  // threat to our box, nobody buries INSIDE it — hold the useful edge.
   305	  // Defensive THREAT = how close the ball is to OUR goal (0 at/above halfway,
   306	  // ~1 deep in our third). Spread when there's no threat (cover space, no
   307	  // bus-crowd); COMPACT the last line under threat (B-continued — the first
   308	  // B1-b spread even the back line → clean chances → goals-warming inflated
   309	  // to overperf 2.1×; solidity restored here).
   310	  const threat = clamp((-team.localX(ball.pos.x) - 8) / 26, 0, 1);
   311	  if (p.role !== 'GK') {
   312	    let rx = 0;
   313	    let ry = 0;
   314	    for (const q of team.players) {
   315	      if (q === p || q.role === 'GK' || q.sentOff) continue;
   316	      const dxL = x - team.localX(q.pos.x);
   317	      const dyL = y - q.pos.y;
   318	      const d = Math.hypot(dxL, dyL);
   319	      if (d < 9 && d > 1e-3) {
   320	        const f = (9 - d) / 9;
   321	        rx += (dxL / d) * f;
   322	        ry += (dyL / d) * f;
   323	      }
   324	    }
   325	    const spread = 2.6 * (1 - threat * 0.7); // don't spread the last line under threat
   326	    x += clamp(rx * spread, -7, 7);
   327	    y += clamp(ry * spread, -7, 7);
   328	    // no useless burying in our own box when the ball isn't threatening it
   329	    if (team.localX(ball.pos.x) > -20 && x < -HALF_L + BOX_DEPTH) x = -HALF_L + BOX_DEPTH + 2;
   330	    // SOLIDITY under threat: the back/mid block collapses goal-ward + central
   331	    // as the ball bears down, so the last line stays compact and denies the
   332	    // clean chance (the ST stays high as the outlet).
   333	    if (!hasBall && p.role !== 'ST' && threat > 0) {
   334	      const kk = threat * (0.3 + g.defensiveCompactness * 0.5);
   335	      x += (-HALF_L + 11 - x) * kk * 0.45;
   336	      y += (0 - y) * kk * 0.3;
   337	    }
   338	  }
   339	
   340	  if (p.role === 'GK') {
   341	    x = clamp(-HALF_L + 4 + (g.keeperAggression - 0.5) * 4, -HALF_L + 1, -HALF_L + 11);
   342	    y = clamp(ball.pos.y * 0.25, -GOAL_WIDTH / 2, GOAL_WIDTH / 2);
   343	    return v2(x * team.attackDir, y);
   344	  }
   345	  x = clamp(x, -HALF_L + 3, HALF_L - 7);
   346	  y = clamp(y, -HALF_W + 2, HALF_W - 2);
   347	  return v2(x * team.attackDir, y);
   348	}
   349	
   350	/**
   351	 * Free-kick wall slots (Phase 32): shoulder-to-shoulder on the ball–goal
   352	 * line at the law clearance (9.15m), 0.7m apart, centered. Shared by the
   353	 * executor (routing), the referee's wall-wait gate and the flight solver —
   354	 * one geometry, so nothing fights and nobody strikes past a half-built
   355	 * wall standing in the climb's header band.
   356	 */
   357	export function fkWallSlots(from: V2, goal: V2, n: number): V2[] {
   358	  const dx = goal.x - from.x;
   359	  const dy = goal.y - from.y;
   360	  const dl = Math.max(Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy), 1e-6);
   361	  const ux = dx / dl;
   362	  const uy = dy / dl;
   363	  const cx = from.x + ux * (CORNER_CLEARANCE + 0.15);
   364	  const cy = from.y + uy * (CORNER_CLEARANCE + 0.15);
   365	  const out: V2[] = [];
   366	  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
   367	    // 1.1m spacing: anything under PLAYER_MIN_DIST (1.05) gets shoved
   368	    // apart by resolveOverlaps every frame — the wall equilibrated 1.4m
   369	    // OFF its slots, standing exactly in the climb's header band.
   370	    const off = (i - (n - 1) / 2) * 1.1;
   371	    out.push(v2(cx - uy * off, cy + ux * off));
   372	  }
   373	  return out;
   374	}
   375	
   376	/**
   377	 * Corner routine geometry (Phase 31), in world coordinates for the taking
   378	 * team. `attackDir` is the taker's attacking direction, `cornerY` the sign
   379	 * of the corner flag's y. The KEY zone is what the routine's openness is
   380	 * judged on; the CRASH spots are where the three licensed box-crashers
   381	 * attack (primary / secondary / rebound), ordered by aerial rank.
   382	 */
   383	export function cornerKeyZone(routine: CornerRoutine, attackDir: 1 | -1, cornerY: number): V2 {
   384	  const gx = attackDir * HALF_L;
   385	  const s = cornerY >= 0 ? 1 : -1;
   386	  switch (routine) {
   387	    case 'nearPost':
   388	      return v2(gx - attackDir * 4.5, s * 2.8);
   389	    case 'farPost':
   390	      return v2(gx - attackDir * 5.5, -s * 3.2);
   390	      return v2(gx - attackDir * 5.5, -s * 3.2);
   391	    case 'short':
   392	      return v2(gx - attackDir * 9, s * (HALF_W - 6));
   393	    case 'arcCutback':
   394	      return v2(gx - attackDir * 16, s * 3);
   395	  }
   396	}
   397	
   398	export function cornerCrashSpots(
   399	  routine: CornerRoutine | undefined, attackDir: 1 | -1, cornerY: number,
   400	): [V2, V2, V2] {
   401	  const gx = attackDir * HALF_L;
   402	  const s = cornerY >= 0 ? 1 : -1;
   403	  const b = (dx: number, y: number): V2 => v2(gx - attackDir * dx, y);
   404	  switch (routine) {
   405	    case 'nearPost':
   406	      // Overload the front zone: the flick wins the race, the others eat
   407	      // the flick-on and the spill.
   408	      return [b(4.5, s * 2.8), b(7, -s * 1), b(11, s * 0.5)];
   409	    case 'farPost':
   410	      // The back-post crash: primary attacks the far stick with a run.
   411	      return [b(5.5, -s * 3.2), b(6, s * 1.5), b(11, 0)];
   412	    case 'arcCutback':
   413	      // Crashers pin the box DEEP so the arc stays empty for the arriver.
   414	      return [b(4.5, s * 2.5), b(5.5, -s * 2.5), b(7.5, 0)];
   415	    case 'short':
   416	    default:
   417	      // Default milling (and the short routine's box picture): posts + spot.
   418	      return [b(5, s * 2.5), b(6, -s * 2.5), b(11, 0)];
   419	  }
   420	}
   421	
   422	/**
   423	 * Is the team settled into its ATTACKING shape? (Phase 30 step 3 — the
   424	 * keeper waits for this before releasing a goal kick or a held ball, so
   425	 * distributions find SET receivers instead of gifting scrambles.) At least
   426	 * three outfielders within `radius` of their attacking spots — or every
   427	 * outfielder the team still has, when send-offs leave fewer than three.
   428	 * Pure sim-state (invariant 3): positions vs spot tables, no clocks.
   429	 */
   430	export function shapeReady(team: Team, ball: Ball, radius = 6): boolean {
   431	  let settled = 0;
   432	  let outfield = 0;
   433	  for (const p of team.players) {
   434	    if (p.role === 'GK' || p.sentOff) continue;
   435	    outfield++;
   436	    const spot = formationSpot(p, team, ball, true);
   437	    const dx = p.pos.x - spot.x;
   438	    const dy = p.pos.y - spot.y;
   439	    if (dx * dx + dy * dy < radius * radius) settled++;
   440	  }
   441	  return settled >= Math.min(3, outfield);
   442	}
   443	
   444	/**
   445	 * The opponents' last defensive line, in `team`-local x (bigger = deeper
   446	 * toward their goal). GK excluded — beating the keeper is the striker's job.
   447	 */
   448	export function defenderLineLocalX(team: Team, opponents: Player[]): number {
   449	  let line = -HALF_L;
   450	  for (const o of opponents) {
   451	    if (o.role === 'GK' || o.sentOff) continue;
   452	    const lx = team.localX(o.pos.x);
   453	    if (lx > line) line = lx;
   454	  }
   455	  return line;
   456	}
   457	
   458	/**
   459	 * The OFFSIDE line in `team`-local x (Phase 29): the second-last opponent
   460	 * COUNTING the keeper (the real law — usually the last outfield defender,
   461	 * because the keeper is the last man), or the ball itself if it's deeper,
   462	 * floored at halfway (you cannot be offside in your own half). An attacker
   463	 * ahead of this line when a teammate strikes the ball is in an offside
   464	 * position; level is onside (callers add their own epsilon).
   465	 */
   466	export function offsideLineLocalX(team: Team, opponents: Player[], ballLocalX: number): number {
   467	  let last = -HALF_L;
   468	  let secondLast = -HALF_L;
   469	  for (const o of opponents) {
   470	    if (o.sentOff) continue;
   471	    const lx = team.localX(o.pos.x);
   472	    if (lx > last) {
   473	      secondLast = last;
   474	      last = lx;
   475	    } else if (lx > secondLast) {
   476	      secondLast = lx;
   477	    }
   478	  }
   479	  return Math.max(secondLast, ballLocalX, 0);
   480	}
   481	
   482	/**
   483	 * Where an assigned runner sprints: past the last defender's shoulder,
   484	 * angling into the channel toward goal. Clamped short of the keeper's box so
   485	 * runs stretch the defence without parking on the goal line. The target aims
   486	 * BEYOND the line on purpose — while a teammate still carries the ball the
   487	 * executor holds the run at the offside line (Phase 29), and the instant the
   488	 * kick is struck the clamp releases and this target is the burst in behind.
   489	 */
   490	export function runTarget(p: Player, team: Team, opponents: Player[]): V2 {
   491	  const line = defenderLineLocalX(team, opponents);
   492	  const myX = team.localX(p.pos.x);
   493	  const targetLocalX = clamp(Math.max(line + 7, myX + 5), myX + 3, HALF_L - 9);
   494	  // Narrow toward the goal mouth as the run goes deeper, keeping the lane.
   495	  // The poacher (Phase 39) attacks the POST CHANNEL (|y|≈3.5, his wing's
   496	  // post) — the tap-in zone. NOT the center: a first cut narrowed him to
   497	  // ×0.35 and his runs ended on the keeper's chest (fm 21, the goal-pull
   498	  // lesson — conversion went DOWN and the finishing invariant test flagged
   499	  // it).
   500	  const y = p.traits.includes('poacher')
   501	    ? Math.sign(p.pos.y || 1) * 3.5
   502	    : clamp(p.pos.y * 0.6, -HALF_W + 4, HALF_W - 4);
   503	  return v2(targetLocalX * team.attackDir, y);
   504	}
   505	
   506	/**
   507	 * Where a through ball should MEET a runner (Phase 29). A runner already in
   508	 * stride is led by their velocity, like any pass. But a runner HELD at the
   509	 * offside line hovers with near-zero velocity — leading by velocity would
   510	 * put the ball at their feet ON the line, exactly the ball the line exists
   511	 * to kill. The pass anticipates the break instead: it projects the burst
   512	 * along the run target at the runner's top speed, and the runner breaks the
   513	 * instant the kick releases the onside hold. Judgment stays honest — the
   514	 * flag is judged on where the runner STANDS at the kick, not the aim point.
   515	 */
   516	export function runBurstPoint(p: Player, team: Team, opponents: Player[], flight: number): V2 {
   517	  const speed = Math.hypot(p.vel.x, p.vel.y);
   518	  if (speed > 3) {
   519	    return v2(p.pos.x + p.vel.x * flight * 1.6, p.pos.y + p.vel.y * flight * 1.6);
   520	  }

   522	  const dx = rt.x - p.pos.x;
   523	  const dy = rt.y - p.pos.y;
   524	  const d = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1;
   525	  const burst = Math.min(d, p.topSpeed * flight * 1.1);
   526	  return v2(p.pos.x + (dx / d) * burst, p.pos.y + (dy / d) * burst);
   527	}

   533	 *
   534	 * Lane-pulled but radius-bounded (Phase 30.5): the old sign()-based nudge
   535	 * kept every supporter within ~5m of the ball's y, so all three off-ball
   536	 * attackers formed one narrow column ahead of the carrier — dragging their
   537	 * markers into the same corridor, walling off every forward lane
   538	 * (interceptions ran 33/match) and pulling wingers off the flank. Pulling
   539	 * y toward the lane spreads support into a fan: near-central options stay
   540	 * short, the ball-side winger becomes a REAL wide outlet. The lateral pull
   541	 * is capped at ~0.9× the support radius on purpose — a first cut anchored
   542	 * y fully to the lane, which parked "support" 30m from the carrier: no
   543	 * short options left, neutral-genome attacks starved (mirror goals 1.47 →
   544	 * 0.93), and the 5v6 sanity invariant inverted (probe-shorthand).
   545	 */
   546	export function supportSpot(p: Player, team: Team, ball: Ball): V2 {
   547	  const g = team.genome;
   548	  // 10..18m: close enough for a give-and-go, far enough that the carrier
   549	  // isn't mobbed by their own teammates (Phase 19 spacing pass, widened in
   550	  // Phase 27.1 — the crowd complaint was real).
   551	  const radius = 10 + g.supportDistance * 8;
   552	  const aheadBias = team.mode === 'CounterAttack' || team.mode === 'Attack' ? 0.75 : 0.35;

   554	  const lane = formationSpot(p, team, ball, true);
   555	  const maxLat = radius * 0.9;
   556	  const latPull = clamp((lane.y - ball.pos.y) * 0.75, -maxLat, maxLat);
   557	  return v2(
   558	    clamp(ball.pos.x + team.attackDir * radius * aheadBias, -HALF_L + 2, HALF_L - 2),
   559	    clamp(ball.pos.y + latPull, -HALF_W + 2, HALF_W - 2),
   560	  );
   561	}

   245	## 5.5 The arrival hypothesis, reality-calibrated (commander amendment,
   246	2026-07-27, user-ratified — supersedes the "price the landing" framing)
   247	
   248	Real box attack happens BEFORE the kick, and C4's own chain measured the
   249	same thing (T2: presence without pre-aim moved nothing; the corner
   250	machinery works because it stages pre-kick). The P5+/C4-handshake
   251	hypothesis is therefore posed as:
   252	
   253	* **Evidence read, pre-kick**: the eye reads observable carrier context
   254	  (teammate wide + high + body set to deliver — external evidence only,
   255	  intent privacy holds) and prices the box ZONES ahead of the kick. The
   256	  last-half-second landing re-route is already banked dormant (C4) and
   257	  is the correction, never the mechanism.
   258	* **Division of labour EMERGES**: near/far/spot splits are never
   259	  hand-assigned — they fall out of don't-crowd (an occupied zone prices
   260	  lower in the next man's eye) plus per-player gene/attr differences.
   261	  A4's doctrine, when it opens, sharpens the split as a shared PRIOR
   262	  (latency/coordination), never revealing hidden truth.

   265	  offside canary stays HARD on this hypothesis forever.
   266	* **Wasted runs are the honest price**: evidence-driven anticipation

   271	  per ruling #34.3.

   226	/**
   227	 * EMERGENT POSITIONING FIELD (Phase B1-a). Replaces the fixed formation TABLE
   228	 * with a ROLE-anchored field: a role gives a coarse depth+lane TENDENCY (a
   229	 * dimension, like an attribute — not a hand-drawn shape), and the actual
   230	 * station grows from that + the live game state, weighted by GENES. So the
   231	 * team's SHAPE and "style" emerge from gene weights, not from us picking
   232	 * wide-212 vs low-32. B1-a lands the structural swap + a REAL, gene-weighted
   233	 * strong/weak-side shift (the B0 probe found the old ~2m drag was token). The
   234	 * anti-clump / space-value terms (kill the bus box-crowd, no clumping) are
   235	 * B1-b. Opponent-relative positioning is B2. Same sensible modifiers as the
   236	 * table path (slide/depth/press/rest-defence/width) so shape stays sane.
   237	 */
   238	function emergentStation(p: Player, team: Team, ball: Ball, hasBall: boolean, opp?: Team): V2 {

   241	  // a side from their slot (L=3, R=4); everyone else holds a central lane.
   242	  const laneSign = p.index === 3 ? -1 : p.index === 4 ? 1 : 0;
   243	  let depthFrac: number;
   244	  let laneFrac: number;
   245	  switch (p.role) {
   246	    case 'GK': depthFrac = -0.91; laneFrac = 0; break;
   247	    case 'DF': depthFrac = -0.45; laneFrac = 0; break;
   248	    case 'MF': depthFrac = -0.12; laneFrac = laneSign * 0.12; break;
   249	    case 'WG': depthFrac = 0.05; laneFrac = laneSign * 0.6; break;
   250	    default: depthFrac = 0.12; laneFrac = 0; break; // ST
   251	  }
   252	
   253	  const ballLocalX = team.localX(ball.pos.x);
   254	  const slide = clamp(ballLocalX * 0.3, -10, 10);
   255	  const depth = (g.formationDepth - 0.5) * 12;
   256	  const pressUp = hasBall || p.role === 'GK' ? 0 : (g.pressIntensity - 0.5) * 8;
   257	  let x = depthFrac * HALF_L + slide + depth + pressUp + MODE_SHIFT[team.mode];
   258	
   259	  // Rest defence — the DF slot never joins the siege (same as the table path).
   260	  if (p.index === 1 && p.role !== 'GK') {
   261	    if (hasBall) x = Math.min(x, -8 - (g.coverBias ?? 0.5) * 8);
   262	    else x -= ((g.coverBias ?? 0.5) - 0.5) * 8;
   263	  }
   264	
   265	  // Width: stretch in possession, squeeze out of it.
   266	  let widthMul = hasBall ? 1.0 + g.attackingWidth * 0.55 : 1.15 - g.defensiveCompactness * 0.6;

   268	  let y = laneFrac * HALF_W * widthMul;
   269	
   270	  // ⭐ STRONG / WEAK SIDE (B1-a, the real thing): the block slides toward the
   271	  // BALL'S y — overload the ball side in attack, protect it in defence —
   272	  // weighted by width (attack) / compactness (defence). The B0 probe measured
   273	  // the old drag at only ~2m and gene-flat; this is a genuine, selectable
   274	  // ball-side shift, so a team that commits to it gets a real strong side and
   275	  // leaves a weak side (which width/switches then punish — emergent).
   276	  // TRANSLATE the block ball-side (add a common offset) — do NOT converge each
   277	  // man onto ball.y (that collapses the lateral spread; the first B1-a cut did,
   278	  // halving spreadY). The whole shape slides over, keeping its width.
   279	  const ballSideShift = hasBall ? 0.18 + g.attackingWidth * 0.22 : 0.18 + g.defensiveCompactness * 0.25;

   281	
   282	  // ⭐ B2: the block tracks the OPPONENT's push, not just the ball (the user's
   283	  // "阵型也不会随着对面的移动而移动"). The defensive spine (DF/MF) holds a line
   284	  // just goal-side of the opponents' advanced players — step UP when they sit
   285	  // deep, DROP when they push. A modest convergence, so the block MOVES WITH
   286	  // the opponent line while keeping its own depth structure. Only when we have
   287	  // an opponent reference (executor/marking path); attack + supportSpot skip it.
   288	  if (!hasBall && opp && (p.role === 'DF' || p.role === 'MF')) {
   289	    const adv = opp.players
   290	      .filter((o) => o.role !== 'GK' && !o.sentOff)
   291	      .map((o) => team.localX(o.pos.x))

   294	      const holdLine = adv[1] - 3; // goal-side of their 2nd-deepest attacker
   295	      x += (holdLine - x) * 0.14;

   297	  }
   298	
   299	  // ⭐ B1-b: ANTI-CLUMP + position by VALUE (the user's "一堆人挤自家禁区,防守
   300	  // 帮助 0" / "别扎堆"). Stations REPEL each other, so bodies SPREAD to cover
   301	  // space instead of piling into the same zone — the emergent alternative to a
   302	  // fixed lattice AND to the bus box-crowd. Computed in the local-x / world-y
   303	  // frame (x is local, y unflipped). Plus a box-crowd relief: with no ball
   304	  // threat to our box, nobody buries INSIDE it — hold the useful edge.
   305	  // Defensive THREAT = how close the ball is to OUR goal (0 at/above halfway,
   306	  // ~1 deep in our third). Spread when there's no threat (cover space, no

   340	  if (p.role === 'GK') {

   534	 * Lane-pulled but radius-bounded (Phase 30.5): the old sign()-based nudge

   536	 * attackers formed one narrow column ahead of the carrier — dragging their

   539	 * y toward the lane spreads support into a fan: near-central options stay

   543	 * short options left, neutral-genome attacks starved (mirror goals 1.47 →
   544	 * 0.93), and the 5v6 sanity invariant inverted (probe-shorthand).

   546	export function supportSpot(p: Player, team: Team, ball: Ball): V2 {
   547	  const g = team.genome;
   548	  // 10..18m: close enough for a give-and-go, far enough that the carrier
   549	  // isn't mobbed by their own teammates (Phase 19 spacing pass, widened in
   550	  // Phase 27.1 — the crowd complaint was real).
   551	  const radius = 10 + g.supportDistance * 8;

   556	  const latPull = clamp((lane.y - ball.pos.y) * 0.75, -maxLat, maxLat);

   559	    clamp(ball.pos.y + latPull, -HALF_W + 2, HALF_W - 2),
   560	  );
   561	}

  1003	  // brain tick of the moment dying and he falls through to positioning,

  1018	  // rush-anatomy A/B measured the extended charge at GA +1.3-1.8 vs the

    36	  /** How far away support runs position themselves from the carrier. */

    46	  /**

    56	  /**

    62	   * exactly; 1 = the tinkerer who slams the panic button early and hard.
    63	   * Neither is a virtue: the chase concedes counters, the deep shut-down

    65	   */

     1	# C5 T1 — The waiting census (fork-and-force hold-k vs act-now)
     2	
     3	Status: **PRE-REGISTERED 2026-07-27 — everything below is frozen before any
     4	implementation and before any data.** Drafted by the autonomous session under
     5	the C5 design contract ([`C5-TIME-DIMENSION.md`](C5-TIME-DIMENSION.md) §3 T1,

     8	
     9	Date: 2026-07-27
    10	
    11	## 1. What T1 is for, and what it must refuse to do
    12	
    13	The design contract's stage line: *"THE WAITING CENSUS — fork-and-force, C3R
    14	floor discipline + the attainable-population check ex ante, #20 cluster
    15	semantics, table SHA'd as data, zero src. Time-signature instruments DEFINED
    16	here."*
    17	
    18	T0/T0R built the capability and proved it is real, graded and losable. T1
    19	answers the only question that can price it: **what does a second of waiting
    20	buy or cost, on the same outcome axis the pass options are already priced on?**
    21	
    22	Three refusals are structural, and they are the reason this stage exists at all:
    23	
    24	1. **No forward-looking term is invented.** Q2 binds: the world pays for
    25	   waiting, the census merely reads the exchange rate. Nothing in T1 writes a
    26	   bonus for "a run is maturing" or "pressure is being drawn"; those effects, if
    27	   they are real, arrive through the NEXT decision's genuinely better menu and
    28	   therefore land inside the measured outcome by themselves.
    29	2. **The exchange rate is REPORTED, never gated.** T1's gates are
    30	   instrument-quality gates. A census that gated on "waiting pays" would be an
    31	   experiment with a preferred answer, and Q2 says in advance what to do if the
    32	   answer is no: *"if today's world pays little for patience, the table says so
    33	   honestly; road B enriches the world and re-censuses"*. §8 pre-lays the
    34	   exhaustive readings so no narrative can be chosen after the numbers.
    35	3. **A2b may not be cited here.** The commander's binding interpretation (T0
    36	   §6, C5 §6.5) reserves the free-option question for this table and T3's
    37	   dominance ceiling. T1 is where the comparison is finally made on an OUTCOME
    38	   axis rather than a retention axis — the thing T0's 12.31% baseline could not
    39	   do (§6.3 of T0R).
    40	
    41	## 2. Staging, frozen
    42	
    43	| item | value | why this and not something else |

    45	| build block | seeds **850,000+** | fresh; 840,000 (T0R) and 830,000 (the diagnostic) have both been seen |
    46	| held-out block | seeds **860,000+** | disjoint; C3R discipline — the block that builds may not also validate |

The pair never arms alone (E4-PREP-2's closed mode list) |

    54	
    55	### 2.1 What a decision moment is (frozen predicate)
    56	
    57	A tick qualifies when **all** hold:
    58	
    59	* `match.phase === 'playing'`;
    60	* `ball.owner` is non-null, not a GK, not sent off;
    61	* the tick is a **brain-decision tick for that owner** (`AI_INTERVAL` 0.15 s,
    62	  `Match.ts:717`) — the census samples where the argmax actually happens, not
    63	  between decisions, because T0 §6.5 banked that action labels drift inside the
    64	  0.15 s gap;
    65	* at least **30 ticks** since the last sampled moment in this match, so
    66	  successive trials are not one possession counted repeatedly (T0R's spacing,
    67	  verbatim);
    68	* the per-match cap of 80 is not yet reached.
    69	
    70	## 3. The arms
    71	
    72	Four arms, all forked with `cloneSimulationState` from the **same pre-step
    73	state**, so the comparison is paired by construction:
    74	
    75	```text
    76	A0  ACT-NOW    the untouched fork — whatever the brain does, which per the
    77	               Phase-0 map is pass / carry / shoot and never a hold.
    78	               "act-now includes the carry" (C5 §6.5) is the whole point.
    79	A1  HOLD-30    forcedHold for 30 ticks  (0.5 s), then free
    80	A2  HOLD-60    forcedHold for 60 ticks  (1.0 s), then free
    81	A3  HOLD-90    forcedHold for 90 ticks  (1.5 s), then free
    82	```
    83	
    84	The ladder is 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 s: the top rung is T0R's own measured window, so
    85	its survival and tackle-loss numbers are the banked prior for what the holder
    86	is risking; the two lower rungs exist because the exchange rate is a *curve*
    87	and a single k cannot tell a cost that grows from one that switches on.
    88	
    89	After `untilTick` the brain decides normally. Nothing else is forced anywhere,
    90	in any arm.
    91	
    92	## 4. The outcome axis, frozen
    93	
    94	**The attacking team takes a shot within 240 ticks OF THE DECISION MOMENT.**
    95	
    96	* `teams[owner.side].stats.shots` strictly increases inside the window —
    97	  E5d's instrument, unchanged, so the numbers are comparable to the committed
    98	  attempt tables.
    99	* **The horizon origin is the DECISION MOMENT in every arm, not the release.**
   100	  This is the load-bearing choice of the whole stage and it is made here, in
   101	  advance, with its consequence stated: a hold arm spends k of its own 240
   102	  ticks holding. That is not a handicap to be corrected — it *is* the price of
   103	  waiting, and moving the origin to the release would hand the hold arms free
   104	  time and manufacture the result Q2 forbids assuming. A release-origin twin is
   105	  computed and **reported** (§8.3) precisely so the difference between the two
   106	  conventions is visible rather than hidden.
   107	* Every window is simulated to its end whatever happens to the ball —
   108	  E5d's attempt convention, no adjudication conditioning, no
   109	  clean-reception gate.
   110	* Windows are truncated only by `phase !== 'playing'` ending the match; a
   111	  restart inside the window does not stop the clock (both arms alike).
   112	
   113	**The concession twin** — the opponent takes a shot within the same window — is
   114	computed on the same rows and reported beside it. Waiting has two failure modes
   115	and a one-sided axis would only see one of them.
   116	
   117	## 5. Context keying and the coverage ladder
   118	
   119	Cell = **pressure band × staleTime band × support band** (27 cells), all read
   120	from the pre-fork state:
   121	
   122	| feature | cuts | provenance |
   123	| --- | --- | --- |
   124	| pressure | `pressureAt(owner.pos, opponents)`, cuts **0.15 / 0.45** | T0R's frozen bands, verbatim — same instrument, same world, banked shares 20.6 / 13.6 / 65.8% |
   125	| staleTime | `teams[side].staleTime`, cuts **3 s / 8 s** | **code-derived, not invented**: `stagnation = clamp01((staleTime − 3)/5)` (`PlayerBrain.ts:191`) is exactly flat below 3 and saturated at 8. Q3 keeps stagnation legacy-only; this stage uses its ramp only as an honest place to cut a feature |
   126	| support | count of own non-GK, non-sent-off players in E0's **6–30 m** window; **terciles of the realised distribution**, declared as a rule now and reported as numbers after | the window is banked (E0/E2a); the cuts are not invented ex nihilo, they are computed by a frozen rule — T0R's tercile precedent |
   127	
   128	**Frozen fall-down ladder**, floor **300 rows per arm per bucket**:
   129	
   130	```text
   131	(pressure × stale × support)  →  (pressure × stale)  →  pressure  →  marginal
   132	```
   133	
   134	Under-filled buckets take the next rung and are **REPORTED, never merged after
   135	seeing results** (E5d C1's rule, verbatim).
   136	
   137	⚠️ **Only the pressure-row level is GATED for coverage**, and that is the #24
   138	lesson applied honestly rather than performed: the joint 27-cell occupancy is
   139	**not** derivable ex ante from anything banked, so inventing a per-cell floor
   140	would repeat E5g's P2 in its worse form — a number I made up. The pressure-row
   141	floor, by contrast, IS derivable (§7.2). Cell-level occupancy is a coverage
   142	report, and the ladder is what makes the table usable at T2 regardless of how
   143	the occupancy falls.
   144	
   145	## 6. Gates
   146	
   147	### 6.1 X-series — identity and harness (any failure ⇒ FAIL)
   148	
   149	| gate | predicate |
   150	| --- | --- |
   151	| **X1** | `npm run fingerprint` returns `57b0bdab389122af5e4cacd75c4e13020b8ff248a413a7fcd71cc6215ba4c673`, unchanged |
   152	| **X2** | **zero `src/**` changes**, audited by diff. T1 measures the capability T0 built; it adds none |
   153	| **X3** | two `runExperiment()` calls byte-identical; SHA-256 emitted |
   154	| **X4** | **the seam is inert** (E2a-2's X5, in this stage's shape): with `c5Hold` armed and `forcedHold` set to an ALREADY-EXPIRED `untilTick`, the fork's world signature over the full 240-tick horizon is byte-identical to the untouched fork, on 3 seeds. The A0 arm is that untouched fork, so this pins that arming the seam is not itself the intervention |
   155	| **X5** | **the seam BITES**: for k = 90, the hold arm's world signature differs from A0's inside the horizon in **≥ 90%** of moments. Derived, not hoped: the untouched menu provably contains no hold (Phase-0 map), so divergence is expected at essentially every moment; below 90% the intervention is not reaching the world |
   156	
   157	### 6.2 C — coverage
   158	
   159	```text
   160	C1  build block:     6,000 moments,  >= 60 clusters
   161	C2  held-out block:  2,500 moments,  >= 30 clusters
   162	C3  every PRESSURE ROW carries >= 300 rows per arm, in BOTH blocks
   163	```
   164	
   165	### 6.3 H — held-out calibration (the interval test that makes it an instrument)
   166	
   167	Per arm, comparing the build block's table to the held-out block's:
   168	
   169	```text
   170	H1  | shotRate_build − shotRate_heldout |  <=  2.0pp   on the marginal
   171	H2  | shotRate_build − shotRate_heldout |  <=  5.0pp   on each gated pressure row
   172	```
   173	
   174	E5d's C2 tolerances, verbatim, on the same outcome axis at the same base rate.
   175	A table that does not reproduce on a disjoint block cannot price anything at
   176	T2, so this is the one substantive gate T1 carries — and it is a property of
   177	the instrument, not of the hypothesis.
   178	
   179	### 6.4 What is deliberately NOT gated, and why
   180	
   181	* **The exchange rate itself** (§1 refusal 2, §8).
   182	* **Discrimination across cells.** E5d gated it because E5a had already
   183	  established that its keying discriminates; here there is no such prior, so a
   184	  discrimination floor would be a number nobody powered — exactly what killed
   185	  T0's A3. It is reported in full.
   186	
   187	## 7. Power and attainability, derived ex ante
   188	
   189	### 7.1 The marginal
   190	
   191	Base rate from the banked attempt table: shot-within-240 ≈ **7%**, so
   192	σ² ≈ 0.065. Treating the arms as INDEPENDENT (conservative — they are paired by
   193	construction, which can only shrink the interval):
   194	
   195	```text
   196	SE(difference) = sqrt(2 · 0.065 / n)
   197	n = 6,000  ⇒  SE = 0.466pp  ⇒  MDE at 80% / α = 0.05 = 2.8 · SE = 1.30pp
   198	with a 1.5× cluster-variance inflation:      SE ≈ 0.57pp  ⇒  MDE ≈ 1.60pp
   199	```
   200	
   201	So the build block resolves a **1.6pp** exchange rate on the marginal. That is
   202	the resolution being bought, stated as a number before the run so that a
   203	smaller measured effect is read as *unresolved*, not as *zero* (#20).
   204	
   205	### 7.2 Attainability — checked, not assumed (#24)
   206	
   207	* **Moments are budget-bound, not population-bound.** A decision moment is any
   208	  ball-owner decision tick; T0R harvested 12,000 such trials from 76 clusters
   209	  at a 30-tick spacing. With the 80-per-match cap, 6,000 moments needs ≈ **75
   210	  matches** and 2,500 needs ≈ **32** — both comfortably inside a block walk,
   211	  and both floors therefore reachable by construction. This is the opposite of
   212	  E5g's P2 and the check is written down rather than implied.
   213	* **C3's 300-per-row floor is derivable from banked data**: T0R's realised band
   214	  shares were 20.6 / 13.6 / 65.8%, so the smallest pressure row holds ≈ **814**
   215	  rows in the build block (2.7× the floor) and ≈ **339** in the held-out block
   216	  (1.1× — thin by design, which is why H2 gates only rows meeting the floor in
   217	  BOTH blocks).
   218	
   219	### 7.2b ⚠️ DISCLOSED BEFORE THE RUN: the realised base rate is ~3× the assumed one
   220	
   221	A sizing smoke (60 moments, no gate read) puts the act-now shot rate at
   222	**≈21%**, not the ≈7% §7.1 took from the attempt table's marginal. The two are
   223	different populations and I should have seen it while writing §7.1: the attempt
   224	table asks *"did a shot follow this PASS to this target"*, while T1 asks *"did a
   225	shot follow this POSSESSION MOMENT" — a moment that includes carries, shots and
   226	every other thing the argmax can do. A quarter of a 4-second window near the
   227	ball produces a shot far more often than one particular pass does.
   228	
   229	Two consequences, both recorded rather than repaired:
   230	
   231	* **The marginal resolution is worse than §7.1 claimed.** At p ≈ 0.21,
   232	  σ² ≈ 0.166, so the unpaired SE at n = 6,000 is 0.74pp and the MDE is **2.1pp**
   233	  (≈2.5pp with cluster inflation) rather than 1.6pp. The primary estimator is
   234	  PAIRED, which cuts this substantially, but by how much is a property of the
   235	  data and will be reported as an achieved interval rather than claimed here.
   236	* **H1's 2.0pp tolerance is tighter than it looked**: against a build/held-out
   237	  difference SE of ≈0.95pp it is **2.1σ**, not the ≈3σ E5d's tolerance
   238	  represented at its own base rate. So H1 may fire on noise, and if it does that
   239	  is a gate I mis-sized, not a table that failed to reproduce.
   240	
   241	**Nothing is changed**: not the budget, not the tolerance, not the axis. Moving
   242	either after seeing a base rate is the re-powering-after-sight the discipline
   243	forbids, and #19's answer to a gate that looks wrong after the fact is to report
   244	the FAIL, not to redraw it. The numbers above exist so that whatever fires can
   245	be read for what it is.
   246	
   247	### 7.3 No staging pin is available, and that is stated
   248	
   249	#18 asks a stage to pin against banked integers wherever a staging is reused.
   250	T1 reuses none: fresh blocks, a new population (decision moments, not pass
   251	moments), a new arm set. There is nothing honest to pin against, so **X4/X5
   252	carry that weight instead** — one proving the seam changes nothing when
   253	inactive, the other proving it changes the world when active.
   254	
   255	## 8. The exchange rate — pre-laid, exhaustive, reported
   256	
   257	For each k, the primary statistic is the **paired per-moment difference**,
   258	`mean(shot_holdk − shot_actnow)`, with a 95% cluster bootstrap over match
   259	seeds. Read under #20's semantics — an interval straddling zero is
   260	INCONCLUSIVE, never "no effect".
   261	
   262	### 8.1 The three readings, fixed now
   263	
   264	```text
   265	(a) NEGATIVE and resolved       waiting costs shots at this k. The table
   266	                                prices a real cost; T2's chooser will pick a
   267	                                hold only where the cost is repaid, and the
   268	                                honest headline is that today's world charges
   269	                                for patience.
   270	(b) INDISTINGUISHABLE           at 1.6pp resolution the world neither pays nor
   271	                                charges. Q2's registered outcome: the table
   272	                                says so, C5 continues on feel/realism grounds
   273	                                (§1 of the design contract already registered
   274	                                C5 as a feel slice, not an overlap repair),
   275	                                and road B's enrichment re-censuses (#26.5).
   276	(c) POSITIVE and resolved       waiting pays in the CURRENT world. The most
   277	                                surprising of the three and the one to
   278	                                distrust first: it would mean the live argmax
   279	                                is leaving value on the table every 0.15 s,
   280	                                and it returns to the commander with the
   281	                                concession twin and the per-k curve beside it
   282	                                before anything is built on it.
   283	```
   284	
   285	None of the three is a FAIL. All three are C5-relevant, and which one occurs
   286	does not change T1's verdict — only what T2 is allowed to assume.
   287	
   288	### 8.2 The shape questions, reported
   289	
   290	Monotonicity in k (a growing cost vs a switch); the curve per pressure band
   291	(T0R found protection concentrates where a tackler is in range — the same
   292	shape would be a coherence check, not a gate); the concession twin per k; the
   293	per-cell table in full; the loss-cause split of held balls that never got to
   294	release; and the **paired-vs-unpaired** estimator side by side, so the pairing
   295	premium is visible rather than claimed.
   296	
   297	### 8.3 The release-origin twin
   298	
   299	The same statistic with each hold arm's 240-tick window starting at RELEASE
   300	instead of at the decision moment. **Reported, never gated, and never
   301	substituted for the primary** — it answers "was the ball better when he finally
   302	played it", which is a different question from "was waiting worth it", and
   303	keeping both visible is what stops the second question being quietly answered
   304	with the first.
   305	
   306	## 9. Time-signature instruments — DEFINED here (the tempo census)
   307	
   308	The design contract puts the tempo census on this stage; the user's 1.1–1.2×
   309	anchor has been waiting for a measurement. These are computed on **whole
   310	matches, unforked**, over the build block, in **two worlds** — flags-off legacy
   311	(what the user actually plays) and the VALUE arm (what the census is keyed on)
   312	— and reported as a paired baseline that every later C5/C7 stage re-reports.
   313	
   314	```text
   315	TS1  passes per minute        stats.passes / (possessionTime in minutes), per team
   316	TS2  one-touch share          stats.oneTouch / stats.passes, per team
   317	TS3  ownership-spell duration a maximal run of consecutive 'playing' ticks with
   318	                              the same ball.owner; mean / median / p90 seconds
   319	TS4  time-to-release          TS3 restricted to spells ENDING in a kick by that
   320	                              owner, split from spells ending in a loss —
   321	                              the two have different meanings and E5a's lesson
   322	                              is that one number with two meanings is a defect
   323	TS5  decisions per possession ticks-with-an-owner / AI_INTERVAL ticks — how many
   324	                              times the argmax is re-run before the ball leaves
   325	```
   326	
   327	They are **instruments, not gates, at this stage**: nobody has yet established
   328	what a right tempo number is, and inventing one now would be the same error as
   329	T0's A3. Their job is to exist, be frozen in definition, and give T3/T4 a
   330	before/after that the user's feel can be compared against.

   362	
   363	**Only the act-now arm missed, and only on the marginal.** All three HOLD arms
   364	reproduce across disjoint blocks at 1.56 / 0.06 / 0.87pp, and every one of the
   365	twelve gated pressure rows is inside H2's 5.0pp. The act-now level moved
   366	31.35% → 28.36%, and the movement is concentrated in the top pressure band
   367	(31.71% → 27.72%, 4.0pp), which is also where two thirds of the moments live.
   368

   370	realised base rate**, and it fired at ≈3.1σ of the naive interval — i.e. right
   371	at the edge where a mis-sized tolerance and a real block difference are not
   372	distinguishable by this design. With the match seed as the cluster unit and
   373	**32 held-out clusters**, "how shot-heavy a match is" is a cluster-level
   374	property, and the marginal is the statistic most exposed to it; the per-row
   375	comparison at a tolerance that respects that passes everywhere.
   376	
   377	**I am not relaxing it.** §12 says H may not be relaxed after sight and the
   378	tolerances were inherited whole precisely so they could not be argued about

   388	
   389	| k | waiting's cost | 95% CI | concession twin | release-origin twin |

   397	
   398	**In today's world, waiting is expensive at both ends and the cost grows with
   399	every tick held.** Half a second costs 7.6pp of shot probability and buys 1.5pp
   400	of extra concession; a second and a half costs 16.1pp and concedes 3.6pp. Every
   401	interval is far from zero — this is not the 1.6pp-resolution question §7.1
   402	worried about, it is an effect ten times the resolution.

   405	ball" is measurable, and it is false: re-anchoring the window at the RELEASE
   406	still leaves waiting **−6.53 / −10.20 / −12.40pp**. The ball is not better when
   407	it finally goes; it is simply later. The twin is reported, never substituted —
   408	but the direction it points is the same one.
   409	
   410	**By pressure band** (k=90): free **−10.53pp**, mid **−18.87pp**, pressed
   411	**−16.77pp**. Waiting costs least when nobody is near you, which is coherent
   412	without anyone designing it in, and matches T0R's shape — the world only
   413	charges for time when there is someone to charge you.

   420	### 11.3 What this does and does not say
   421	
   422	**Registered in advance and honoured now**: reading (a) is not a FAIL and not a
   423	refutation of C5. What it establishes is narrower and sharper —
   424	
   425	* **A T2 chooser priced from this table would essentially never hold.** That is
   426	  the single most consequential thing T1 hands forward, and it is a design fact
   427	  the commander needs before T2 is drafted, not after.
   428	* **Part of the cost is mechanical by construction, and that was the design.**
   429	  A held tick is a tick removed from the same 240-tick window, and §4 fixed the
   430	  horizon at the decision moment precisely so that time cost would be counted
   431	  rather than hidden. So the honest claim is *"on this axis, in this world, a
   432	  held tick is a spent tick and nothing currently pays it back"* — **not**
   433	  "patience has no value in football".
   434	* **Q2 anticipated this exact outcome**: *"if today's world pays little for
   435	  patience, the table says so honestly; road B enriches the world and
   436	  re-censuses (#26.5)."* The world that would pay for waiting — a maturing run
   437	  that is worth waiting for, a press that can be drawn and beaten, a receiver
   438	  repertoire — is the world road B is building. This table is the before.
   439	* **It is the fourth independent arrow at the same seat, pointing the other
   440	  way.** E4r1, the user's round-2 anchor, E5f/E5g and now T1 all agree that the
   441	  substrate does not currently reward waiting; the first three read it as a
   442	  missing capability, and T1 says the capability alone would not be selected.

   484	## 12. Stop rules
   485	
   486	* **Any X gate fails ⇒ FAIL.** X4 failing means the census measured the seam,
   487	  not the world; X5 failing means it measured nothing.

   121	## 4. Design invariants — the Phase-0 map's six questions, ruled
   122	
   123	* **Q1 — Hold is a CANDIDATE, never a modifier.** The measured gap IS the
   124	  missing option; a modifier hides the choice from measurement and from
   125	  selection, and a candidate is an observable external state — opponents
   126	  see shielding, never intention (the 内心/外显/推断 model holds).
   127	* **Q2 — the WORLD pays for waiting; the census prices it.** No
   128	  forward-looking bonus term is invented anywhere. Waiting's real
   129	  benefits (runs maturing, pressure drawn, percepts refreshing under
   130	  pull semantics) flow through the NEXT decision's genuinely better
   131	  menu; the census measures the net exchange rate on the same outcome
   132	  axis the pass prices use — the E2b-0 move applied to time. If today's
   133	  world pays little for patience, the table says so honestly; road B
   134	  enriches the world and re-censuses (#26.5).
   135	* **Q3 — stagnation stays legacy-only.** In the measured seat, time's
   136	  price comes from the census (staleTime is a census feature, so any
   137	  real decay is IN the table); the hand-penalty is neither copied into
   138	  the value seat nor removed from the legacy one.
   139	* **Q4 — a NEW generalized Hold; legacy HoldUp untouched.** Shield-hold
   140	  is the v1 action. "Look around" is not a separate action in v1 —
   141	  that is seat 2's future consumer. The `layingOff` synergy (`281/326`)
   142	  is a named natural consumer, later.
   143	* **Q5 — C7 shares the contract, not the stages** (§2 above).
   144	* **Q6 — NO FREE TIME (I1, the hard invariant).** Every held tick must
   145	  be attackable: pressure closes, poke/tackle windows open against the
   146	  shield (priced by both sides' attrs), stamina drains. A Hold that
   147	  cannot be lost is the ×1.3 subsidy in a new costume (E5h) and C1-A2's
   148	  free option. T3 carries an explicit pre-registered hold-dominance
   149	  ceiling; a world where holding never loses the ball stops the queue.

    39	band 1                 0.394                  0.433
    40	band 2                 0.386                  0.421
    41	```
    42	
    43	There is no skew to confound with. **The explanation I labelled was wrong**, and
    44	the diagnostic that ruling #27.3 authorized is what says so.
    45	
    46	### 2.2 ⭐ The real finding: the substrate grades a held ball by DRIBBLING, and
    47	strength reads backwards
    48	
    49	Tackle-loss by attr tercile, **within** each pressure band:
    50	
    51	| band | by **strength** (bottom / mid / top) | Δ | by **dribbling** (bottom / mid / top) | Δ |
    52	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    53	| 0 | 2.39 / 4.26 / 3.64% | **+1.24pp** | 4.07 / 3.55 / 2.70% | **−1.38pp** |
    54	| 1 | 13.00 / 15.29 / 15.33% | **+2.33pp** | 16.82 / 14.86 / 12.37% | **−4.45pp** |
    55	| 2 | 20.74 / 22.77 / 24.36% | **+3.63pp** | 25.57 / 20.43 / 21.87% | **−3.70pp** |
    56	
    57	**Stronger holders are tackled MORE, in every band. More technical holders are
    58	tackled LESS, in every band.** Neither is a band artefact — §2.1 killed that.
    59	
    60	### 2.3 And the code said so first, which is why A3R is derivable ex ante
    61	
    62	Ruling #27.3 asks A3R to gate "where the substrate says the gradient should
    63	live". `mechanics.ts:1780–1793`, the standing challenge that resolves a held
    64	ball, prices the carrier's protection as:
    65	
    66	```text
    67	− owner.attrs.dribbling · 0.18      ← dominant
    68	− owner.attrs.strength  · 0.10
    69	− owner.attrs.pace · drive · 0.16   ← drive ≈ 0 during a hold: OFF by construction
    70	```
    71	
    72	and the slide path (`1626`) prices `− dribbling · 0.10` and no strength at all.
    73	
    74	**So `dribbling` carries nearly twice strength's weight in the one formula that
    75	resolves a held ball, and the pace term — which would have been the largest —
    76	is switched off by holding still.** T0's A3 gated on `strength`: the third
    77	term, at half the weight, in a formula it never read. That is the defect,
    78	derivable from the code without any data, and the diagnostic merely confirms
    79	its sign.
    80	
    81	⚠️ Labelled, untested, and **not** pursued: the natural reason strength reads
    82	*reversed* rather than merely weak is that squad generation likely trades
    83	physical against technical attributes, making strength terciles partly inverse
    84	dribbling terciles. A3R does not depend on this being true — the code, not the
    85	correlation, is what selects the attr — so it is recorded and left alone.
    86	
    87	## 3. Gates
    88	
    89	Judged on a **FRESH seed block, 840,000+**, budget **12,000 forced holds**. The
    90	frozen block above has been seen, so it may derive power and may not judge —
    91	C3R's discipline, verbatim.
    92	
    93	| gate | claim | predicate |
    94	| --- | --- | --- |
    95	| **A2aR** | the world grades a held ball by pressure, on the channel pressure drives | **tackle-loss strictly increasing** across the three frozen bands, each consecutive step's 95% cluster-bootstrap CI on the difference entirely **> 0** |
    96	| **A3R** | the hold is attr-graded, stratified by construction | the **band-weighted within-stratum** gradient of tackle-loss by **dribbling** tercile (top − bottom) has its 95% cluster-bootstrap CI entirely **< 0** (protective) |
    97	| **A1** (transfer) | the shield is a body position | far-side ≥ **90%** of held ticks |
    98	| **A2b** (transfer) | I1's ceiling | top-band survival < **0.90** |
    99	| **A2c** (transfer) | holding costs legs | stamina/s > 0 and rising across bands |
   100	| **D** | determinism | two runs byte-identical, SHA emitted |
   101	
   102	### 3.1 Power, derived from the frozen rates (#19), stated not assumed
   103	
   104	- **A2aR** — the smallest step is band 1 → 2, 14.59% → 22.60% = 8.0pp. At the
   105	  observed band n's its naive SE is ≈ 1.09pp, i.e. **≈ 7σ**. Enormously
   106	  powered; **the frozen band cuts therefore stand** (ruling #27.2's condition
   107	  for re-deriving them is not met).
   108	- **A3R** — the band-weighted gradient on the frozen data is
   109	  `(2064·−1.38 + 1357·−4.45 + 6579·−3.70)/10000 = **−3.32pp**`, with an overall
   110	  SE ≈ 0.94pp at n ≈ 3,330 per tercile — **≈ 3.5σ** already. Detecting −3.32pp
   111	  at 80% / α = 0.05 needs `SE ≤ 3.32/2.8 = 1.19pp` ⇒ **n ≥ 6,400**; the 12,000
   112	  budget carries a **1.9× margin** for cluster inflation.
   113	- **Attainability**: a forced hold is stageable at any ball-owner tick, so both
   114	  floors are budget-bound, not population-bound (the #24 check, as at T0).
   115	
   116	### 3.2 Why A3R gates on a CI and not on a magnitude
   117	
   118	A magnitude floor is what killed A3: a number chosen without checking what the
   119	data could resolve. #20's CI semantics answer the question that matters —
   120	*is the substrate's grading real* — and the magnitude is **reported beside it**
   121	so a real-but-tiny gradient can be seen for what it is rather than passed or
   122	failed by a threshold nobody powered.
   123	
   124	## 4. Stop rules
   125	
   126	- **A2aR fails** ⇒ the world does not grade a held ball by pressure even on the
   127	  tackle channel. That is a substrate finding, not a gate defect, and it
   128	  returns to the commander.
   129	- **A3R fails** ⇒ ruling #27.3's own words apply: *"a decorative attr term in
   130	  tackle resolution, a VISION §1 dead-attr candidate"* — an undifferentiated
   131	  option is decoration (C1-A2), and this is **a C5 blocker until the substrate
   132	  grades holding by something**. Returns to the commander.
   133	- **Any transferred gate fails** ⇒ the transfer was not real; FAIL and return.
   134	- No third redraw of these two gates without a ruling.
   135	
   136	## 5. What T0R does not do
   137	
   138	- No `src/**` change: the capability built at T0 is what is being measured.
   139	- No re-judging of run 1, whose FAIL is history.
   140	- No new gate on anything but the two redrawn objects and the four transfers.
   141	- On **PASS**, ruling #27.5 lets T1 (the waiting census) pre-register without a
   142	  new ruling; C4 T0 runs after T0R lands either way (one experiment in flight).
   143	
   144	## 6. Result — RUN 2026-07-27: **PASS, every gate**
   145	
   146	SHA `495faec0…f503`, twice byte-identical. **12,000 forced holds over 76
   147	clusters, fresh block 840,000+.** Zero `src/**` this stage.
   148	
   149	| gate | result | |
   150	| --- | --- | --- |
   151	| **A2aR** tackle-loss strictly increasing, each step's CI > 0 | **4.52% → 17.72% → 23.76%**; steps **+13.20pp** CI [11.11, 15.32] and **+6.04pp** CI [4.02, 8.08] | ✅ |
   152	| **A3R** band-weighted dribbling gradient, CI < 0 | **−2.76pp**, CI **[−5.14, −0.49]** | ✅ |
   153	| **A1** transfer, far-side ≥ 90% | **95.81%** | ✅ |
   154	| **A2b** transfer, top-band survival < 0.90 | **67.57%** | ✅ |
   155	| **A2c** transfer, stamina rising | 0.00095 → 0.00384 → 0.00631 /s | ✅ |
   156	| coverage / determinism | 12,000 trials; two runs byte-identical | ✅ |
   157	
   158	### 6.1 What the redraw actually bought
   159	
   160	**A2aR is not a marginal pass.** Measured on the channel pressure drives, the
   161	world grades a held ball hard: the tackle-loss rate more than **quintuples**
   162	from the free band to the pressed one, and both steps clear zero by 5σ and 4σ.
   163	The object was wrong at T0, not the world — and the same underlying run said so
   164	in a report column.
   165	
   166	**A3R passes and its per-band shape is coherent:**
   167	
   168	| band | bottom / mid / top dribbling | Δ |
   169	| --- | --- | --- |
   170	| 0 (free) | 5.02 / 4.29 / 4.23% | −0.79pp |
   171	| 1 | 19.26 / 15.99 / 18.12% | −1.14pp |
   172	| 2 (pressed) | 25.32 / 24.40 / 21.59% | **−3.73pp** |
   173	
   174	The protection concentrates exactly where it should: **technique buys almost
   175	nothing when nobody is near you, and 3.7pp when you are pressed.** Nobody
   176	designed that shape into the gate — it falls out of the tackle formula being
   177	consulted only when a tackler is in range.
   178	
   179	⚠️ **Honest about the margin**: A3R's CI upper bound is **−0.49pp**, close to
   180	zero, and the point estimate (−2.76pp) is smaller than the frozen block's
   181	−3.32pp. It passes; it does not pass with room. A future stage that leans hard
   182	on this gradient should re-power rather than inherit it.
   183	
   184	### 6.2 ⭐ The strength channel, reported for comparison — and it is unstable
   185	
   186	Run alongside A3R with the identical stratified estimator:
   187	
   188	```text
   189	frozen block (830,000), within-band strength Δ:  +1.24 / +2.33 / +3.63 pp
   190	fresh  block (840,000), band-weighted strength:  −2.27 pp, CI [−4.69, +0.19]
   191	```
   192	
   193	**The sign flips between blocks and the fresh-block interval straddles zero.**
   194	Under #20's semantics that is INCONCLUSIVE — and it is exactly what a
   195	noise-dominated weak term looks like. The code predicted it before either run:
   196	`strength` carries **×0.10** against `dribbling`'s **×0.18** in the only
   197	formula that resolves a held ball, with the ×0.16 pace term switched off by
   198	standing still.
   199	
   200	So the lesson generalises past this gate: **gate where the substrate says the
   201	gradient lives, and the code will tell you before the data does.** T0's A3
   202	picked the third-largest term and got a reading that reversed between two
   203	blocks of the same world.
   204	
   205	### 6.3 Carried forward unchanged
   206	
   207	Hold survival overall 70.23%; the dribble baseline arm 10.83% — **still not
   208	comparable**, for the reason banked at T0 and re-affirmed by ruling #27.4: the
   209	baseline counts a completed pass as not-survived. Every comparative value
   210	question lives on T1's outcome axis.
   211	
   212	### 6.4 Disposition
   213	
   214	**PASS ⇒ ruling #27.5 applies**: T1 (the waiting census) pre-registers without
   215	a new ruling, and C4 T0 runs after this lands (one experiment in flight).
   216	Nothing shipped — both flags stay default OFF with zero live callers, the
   217	preview cannot reach them, and the fingerprint is untouched because this stage
   218	wrote no `src/**` at all.
