     3	// C5-TIME-DIMENSION.md §3 T1 / §4 Q2-Q3; commander ruling #27.5)
     4	//
     5	// What a second of waiting buys or costs, on the SAME outcome axis the pass
     6	// options are already priced on. Nothing here invents a forward-looking term:
     7	// the world pays, the census reads the exchange rate.
     8	//
     9	//   A0 ACT-NOW   the untouched fork — whatever the brain does (pass / carry /
    10	//                shoot; per C5 §6.5 act-now INCLUDES the carry)
    11	//   A1 HOLD-30   forcedHold 30 ticks (0.5 s), then free
    12	//   A2 HOLD-60   60 ticks (1.0 s)
    13	//   A3 HOLD-90   90 ticks (1.5 s) — T0R's own measured window
    14	//
    15	// The horizon starts at the DECISION MOMENT in every arm, so a hold arm spends
    16	// k of its own 240 ticks holding. That is the price of waiting, not a handicap
    17	// to correct; the release-origin twin is computed and REPORTED beside it.
    18	//
    19	// The exchange rate is REPORTED, never gated (contract §1, §8). The gates are
    20	// instrument-quality only.
    21	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
    22	import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
    23	import { pressureAt } from '../../src/ai/perception';
    24	import { Match } from '../../src/sim/Match';
    25	import type { Player } from '../../src/sim/Player';
    26	import { cloneSimulationState } from '../../src/sim/cloneState';
    27	import { AI_INTERVAL, DT } from '../../src/sim/constants';
    28	import { randomGenome } from '../../src/evolution/genome';
    29	import { randomSquad } from '../../src/evolution/playerGenome';
    30	import { TEAM_SIZE, type TeamInfo } from '../../src/sim/types';
    31	import { Rng } from '../../src/utils/rng';
    32	
    33	// --- frozen parameters (contract §2) ----------------------------------------
    34	const MATCH_DURATION = 240;
    35	const BUILD_SEED_START = 850_000;
    36	const HELDOUT_SEED_START = 860_000;
    37	const BUILD_BUDGET = 6_000;
    38	const HELDOUT_BUDGET = 2_500;
    39	const PER_MATCH_CAP = 80;
    40	const MAX_MATCHES = 4_000;
    41	/** Ticks between sampled moments in one match — T0R's spacing, verbatim. */
    42	const MOMENT_SPACING = 30;
    43	/** The outcome window, from the DECISION MOMENT in every arm. */
    44	const HORIZON = 240;
    45	/** The hold ladder, in ticks: 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 s. */
    46	const HOLD_LADDER = [30, 60, 90] as const;
    47	/** T0R's frozen pressure bands, verbatim. */
    48	const PRESSURE_BANDS = [0.15, 0.45] as const;
    49	/** Code-derived: `stagnation = clamp01((staleTime − 3)/5)` is flat below 3
    50	 *  and saturated at 8 (`PlayerBrain.ts:191`). */
    51	const STALE_BANDS = [3, 8] as const;
    52	/** E0's candidate window — the teammates a pass could actually reach. */
    53	const SUPPORT_MIN_M = 6;
    54	const SUPPORT_MAX_M = 30;
    55	const BUCKET_FLOOR = 300;
    56	const PRESSURE_ROW_FLOOR = 300;
    57	const CLUSTER_FLOOR_BUILD = 60;
    58	const CLUSTER_FLOOR_HELDOUT = 30;
    59	const H1_TOLERANCE = 0.02; // 2.0pp, marginal
    60	const H2_TOLERANCE = 0.05; // 5.0pp, per gated pressure row
    61	const X5_BITE_FLOOR = 0.90;
    62	const BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES = 2000;
    63	const BOOTSTRAP_SEED = 50007;
    64	/** Whole-match instruments (§9) — the tempo census rides this stage. */
    65	const TS_MATCHES = 75;
    66	
    67	const VALUE_FLAGS = {
    68	  edsPerceivedDefence: true,
    69	  edsPerceivedChoice: true,
    70	  edsValueAxis: true,
    71	  c5Hold: true,
    72	  // The one-touch fork stays OFF: it is priced by its own two branches at T2,
    73	  // and mixing it in here would confound two forks (contract §2).
    74	  c5TouchFork: false,
    75	} as const;
    76	
    77	const team = (name: string, seed: number): TeamInfo => {
    78	  const rng = new Rng(seed);
    79	  return {
    80	    id: name, name, short: name.slice(0, 3).toUpperCase(),
    81	    colors: { primary: 0xff0000, secondary: 0xffffff },
    82	    playerNames: Array.from({ length: TEAM_SIZE }, (_, index) => `P${index}`),
    83	    genome: randomGenome(rng), squad: randomSquad(rng),
    84	  };
    85	};
    86	const matchOf = (seed: number, value: boolean): Match => new Match({
    87	  seed, teamA: team('A', seed * 2 + 1), teamB: team('B', seed * 2 + 2),
    88	  duration: MATCH_DURATION,
    89	  ...(value ? VALUE_FLAGS : {}),
    90	});
    91	
    92	const distance = (
    93	  a: Readonly<{ x: number; y: number }>, b: Readonly<{ x: number; y: number }>,
    94	): number => Math.hypot(a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y);
    95	
    96	/** A digest of the whole visible world — X4's inertness and X5's bite pin. */
    97	const stateSignature = (match: Match): string => {
    98	  const digest = createHash('sha256');
    99	  digest.update(`${match.simTick}|${match.phase}|${match.score[0]}:${match.score[1]}`);
   100	  digest.update(`|${match.ball.pos.x},${match.ball.pos.y},${match.ball.z}`);
   101	  digest.update(`|${match.ball.vel.x},${match.ball.vel.y},${match.ball.vz}`);
   102	  digest.update(`|${match.ball.owner?.gid ?? -1}|${match.ball.lastTouch?.gid ?? -1}`);
   103	  for (const p of match.allPlayers) {
   104	    digest.update(`|${p.gid},${p.pos.x},${p.pos.y},${p.vel.x},${p.vel.y},${p.stamina}`);
   105	  }
   106	  for (const t of match.teams) {
   107	    digest.update(`|${t.stats.shots},${t.stats.passes},${t.stats.tackles},${t.stats.goals}`);
   108	  }
   109	  return digest.digest('hex');
   110	};
   111	
   112	type Band = 0 | 1 | 2;
   113	const pressureBandOf = (value: number): Band =>
   114	  (value < PRESSURE_BANDS[0] ? 0 : value < PRESSURE_BANDS[1] ? 1 : 2);
   115	const staleBandOf = (value: number): Band =>
   116	  (value < STALE_BANDS[0] ? 0 : value < STALE_BANDS[1] ? 1 : 2);
   117	
   118	interface ArmOutcome {
   119	  /** THE axis: the attacking team took a shot inside the horizon. */
   120	  readonly shot: boolean;
   121	  /** The concession twin — waiting has two failure modes. */
   122	  readonly conceded: boolean;
   123	  /** Hold arms only: the holder still had it when the forced window expired. */
   124	  readonly survivedHold: boolean | null;
   125	  /** Hold arms only: lost during the hold, and to a tackle specifically. */
   126	  readonly lostToTackle: boolean | null;
   127	  /** Hold arms only, §8.3: a 240-tick window starting at the RELEASE instead. */
   128	  readonly shotFromRelease: boolean | null;
   129	  readonly signature: string;
   130	}
   131	
   132	interface Moment {
   133	  readonly cluster: number;
   134	  readonly pressureBand: Band;
   135	  readonly staleBand: Band;
   136	  readonly support: number;
   137	  readonly arms: readonly ArmOutcome[]; // [A0, A1, A2, A3]
   138	}
   139	
   140	/** Run one fork forward and read the axis off it. */
   141	const runArm = (
   142	  before: Match, ownerGid: number, holdTicks: number,
   143	): ArmOutcome => {
   144	  const fork = cloneSimulationState(before);
   145	  const owner = fork.allPlayers.find((p) => p.gid === ownerGid)!;
   146	  const side = owner.side;
   147	  const attacking = fork.teams[side];
   148	  const defending = fork.teams[1 - side];
   149	  const shotsBefore = attacking.stats.shots;
   150	  const concededBefore = defending.stats.shots;
   151	  const tacklesBefore = defending.stats.tackles;
   152	  const startTick = fork.simTick;
   153	  if (holdTicks > 0) fork.forcedHold = { gid: ownerGid, untilTick: startTick + holdTicks };
   154	
   155	  let shot = false;
   156	  let horizonReached = false;
   157	  let survivedHold: boolean | null = holdTicks > 0 ? true : null;
   158	  let lostDuringHold = false;
   159	  // The release-origin twin needs the window to keep running past the
   160	  // horizon, so hold arms are simulated for holdTicks + HORIZON.
   161	  const total = holdTicks + HORIZON;
   162	  let shotsAtRelease = -1;
   163	  for (let tick = 0; tick < total; tick++) {
   164	    if (fork.finished) break;
   165	    fork.step(DT);
   166	    const elapsed = fork.simTick - startTick;
   167	    if (holdTicks > 0 && elapsed === holdTicks) {
   168	      shotsAtRelease = attacking.stats.shots;
   169	      if (fork.ball.owner?.gid !== ownerGid) {
   170	        survivedHold = false;
   171	        lostDuringHold = true;
   172	      }
   173	    }
   174	    if (holdTicks > 0 && elapsed <= holdTicks && fork.ball.owner?.gid !== ownerGid) {
   175	      lostDuringHold = true;
   176	    }
   177	    if (elapsed === HORIZON) {
   178	      // Read the axis AT the horizon and never again: a hold arm keeps
   179	      // simulating for the release twin, and letting a post-horizon shot flip
   180	      // this flag would silently give the hold arms a longer window than
   181	      // act-now. The smoke found that in the first draft.
   182	      shot = attacking.stats.shots > shotsBefore;
   183	      horizonReached = true;
   184	      if (holdTicks === 0) break;
   185	    }
   186	  }
   187	  // A window the match ended inside reads at whatever it reached.
   188	  if (!horizonReached) shot = attacking.stats.shots > shotsBefore;
   189	  const conceded = defending.stats.shots > concededBefore;
   190	  return {
   191	    shot,
   192	    conceded,
   193	    survivedHold: holdTicks > 0 ? survivedHold && !lostDuringHold : null,
   194	    lostToTackle: holdTicks > 0
   195	      ? lostDuringHold && defending.stats.tackles > tacklesBefore : null,
   196	    shotFromRelease: holdTicks > 0 && shotsAtRelease >= 0
   197	      ? attacking.stats.shots > shotsAtRelease : null,
   198	    signature: stateSignature(fork),
   199	  };
   200	};
   201	
   202	/**
   203	 * Walk a seed block, and at every qualifying decision moment fork the world
   204	 * four ways off the SAME pre-step state — paired by construction.
   205	 */
   206	const harvest = (seedStart: number, budget: number) => {
   207	  const moments: Moment[] = [];
   208	  let matches = 0;
   209	  let inertPins: { seed: number; identical: boolean }[] = [];
   210	  for (
   211	    let seed = seedStart;
   212	    seed < seedStart + MAX_MATCHES && moments.length < budget;
   213	    seed++
   214	  ) {
   215	    matches += 1;
   216	    const cluster = seed - seedStart;
   217	    const match = matchOf(seed, true);
   218	    let sinceLast = MOMENT_SPACING;
   219	    let inMatch = 0;
   220	    while (!match.finished && moments.length < budget && inMatch < PER_MATCH_CAP) {
   221	      // PRE-STEP: `decisionTimer <= 0` is what makes this tick the owner's
   222	      // decision (`Match.ts:742`), and the argmax runs inside the step.
   223	      const owner: Player | null = match.ball.owner;
   224	      const qualifies = match.phase === 'playing' && owner !== null
   225	        && owner.role !== 'GK' && !owner.sentOff
   226	        && owner.decisionTimer <= 0 && sinceLast >= MOMENT_SPACING;
   227	      if (qualifies) {
   228	        const before = cloneSimulationState(match);
   229	        const side = owner!.side;
   230	        const opponents = match.teams[1 - side].players;
   231	        const support = match.teams[side].players.filter((p) => (
   232	          p.gid !== owner!.gid && p.role !== 'GK' && !p.sentOff
   233	          && distance(p.pos, owner!.pos) >= SUPPORT_MIN_M
   234	          && distance(p.pos, owner!.pos) <= SUPPORT_MAX_M
   235	        )).length;
   236	        const arms = [0, ...HOLD_LADDER].map((k) => runArm(before, owner!.gid, k));
   237	        // X4, on the first moment of the first three clusters: an ALREADY
   238	        // EXPIRED forcedHold must leave the world byte-identical to A0.
   239	        if (cluster < 3 && inMatch === 0) {
   240	          const inert = cloneSimulationState(before);
   241	          inert.forcedHold = { gid: owner!.gid, untilTick: inert.simTick };
   242	          for (let tick = 0; tick < HORIZON && !inert.finished; tick++) inert.step(DT);
   243	          inertPins.push({ seed, identical: stateSignature(inert) === arms[0].signature });
   244	        }
   245	        moments.push({
   246	          cluster,
   247	          pressureBand: pressureBandOf(pressureAt(owner!.pos, opponents)),
   248	          staleBand: staleBandOf(match.teams[side].staleTime),
   249	          support,
   250	          arms,
   251	        });
   252	        sinceLast = 0;
   253	        inMatch += 1;
   254	      }
   255	      match.step(DT);
   256	      sinceLast += 1;
   257	    }
   258	  }
   259	  return { moments, matches, inertPins };
   260	};
   261	
   262	// --- statistics (cluster unit = the match seed, ruling #20) -----------------
   263	const clusterBootstrap = (
   264	  rows: readonly { readonly cluster: number; readonly value: number }[], offset: number,
   265	) => {
   266	  const byCluster = new Map<number, number[]>();
   267	  for (const row of rows) {
   268	    const bucket = byCluster.get(row.cluster);
   269	    if (bucket === undefined) byCluster.set(row.cluster, [row.value]); else bucket.push(row.value);
   270	  }
   260	};
   261	
   262	// --- statistics (cluster unit = the match seed, ruling #20) -----------------
   263	const clusterBootstrap = (
   264	  rows: readonly { readonly cluster: number; readonly value: number }[], offset: number,
   265	) => {
   266	  const byCluster = new Map<number, number[]>();
   267	  for (const row of rows) {
   268	    const bucket = byCluster.get(row.cluster);
   269	    if (bucket === undefined) byCluster.set(row.cluster, [row.value]); else bucket.push(row.value);
   270	  }
   271	  const clusters = [...byCluster.values()];
   272	  const rng = new Rng(BOOTSTRAP_SEED + offset);
   273	  const draws: number[] = [];
   274	  for (let draw = 0; draw < BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES; draw++) {
   275	    let sum = 0;
   276	    let n = 0;
   277	    for (let index = 0; index < clusters.length; index++) {
   278	      for (const value of clusters[rng.int(0, clusters.length - 1)]) { sum += value; n += 1; }
   279	    }
   280	    if (n > 0) draws.push(sum / n);
   281	  }
   282	  draws.sort((left, right) => left - right);
   283	  const at = (q: number) => draws[Math.min(draws.length - 1,
   284	    Math.max(0, Math.floor(q * (draws.length - 1))))];
   285	  const point = rows.length === 0 ? Number.NaN
   286	    : rows.reduce((sum, row) => sum + row.value, 0) / rows.length;
   287	  return { point, lower: at(0.025), upper: at(0.975), clusters: clusters.length };
   288	};
   289	
   290	const mean = (values: readonly number[]): number => (values.length === 0 ? Number.NaN
   291	  : values.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0) / values.length);
   292	const round = (value: number, dp = 6): number =>
   293	  (Number.isFinite(value) ? Number(value.toFixed(dp)) : Number.NaN);
   294	const canonical = (value: unknown): string => JSON.stringify(value);
   295	
   296	/** Support-count terciles, computed on the BUILD block and applied to both. */
   297	const supportCuts = (values: readonly number[]) => {
   298	  const sorted = [...values].sort((left, right) => left - right);
   299	  const third = Math.floor(sorted.length / 3);
   300	  return { low: sorted[third] ?? 0, high: sorted[sorted.length - third] ?? 0 };
   301	};
   302	const supportBandOf = (
   303	  value: number, cuts: { low: number; high: number },
   304	): Band => (value < cuts.low ? 0 : value >= cuts.high ? 2 : 1);
   305	
   306	const ARM_NAMES = ['actNow', 'hold30', 'hold60', 'hold90'] as const;
   307	
   308	/** The census table: shot rate per arm per cell, with the frozen ladder. */
   309	const buildTable = (moments: readonly Moment[], cuts: { low: number; high: number }) => {
   310	  const key = (m: Moment) => `${m.pressureBand}|${m.staleBand}|${supportBandOf(m.support, cuts)}`;
   311	  const cells = new Map<string, Moment[]>();
   312	  for (const m of moments) {
   313	    const bucket = cells.get(key(m));
   314	    if (bucket === undefined) cells.set(key(m), [m]); else bucket.push(m);
   315	  }
   316	  const rateOf = (rows: readonly Moment[], arm: number) => (rows.length === 0 ? Number.NaN
   317	    : rows.filter((m) => m.arms[arm].shot).length / rows.length);
   318	  const rowsFor = (predicate: (m: Moment) => boolean) => moments.filter(predicate);
   319	
   320	  const cellRows = [...cells.entries()].sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : 1)).map(([k, rows]) => {
   321	    const [p, s, sup] = k.split('|').map(Number);
   322	    // Frozen ladder: (p × s × sup) → (p × s) → p → marginal.
   323	    const ladder = rows.length >= BUCKET_FLOOR ? 'cell'
   324	      : rowsFor((m) => m.pressureBand === p && m.staleBand === s).length >= BUCKET_FLOOR
   325	        ? 'pressureStale'
   326	        : rowsFor((m) => m.pressureBand === p).length >= BUCKET_FLOOR ? 'pressure' : 'marginal';
   327	    return {
   328	      pressureBand: p, staleBand: s, supportBand: sup, n: rows.length, ladder,
   329	      rates: Object.fromEntries(ARM_NAMES.map((name, arm) => [name, round(rateOf(rows, arm))])),
   330	    };
   331	  });
   332	
   333	  const pressureRows = ([0, 1, 2] as Band[]).map((p) => {
   334	    const rows = rowsFor((m) => m.pressureBand === p);
   335	    return {
   336	      pressureBand: p, n: rows.length,
   337	      rates: Object.fromEntries(ARM_NAMES.map((name, arm) => [name, round(rateOf(rows, arm))])),
   338	    };
   339	  });
   340	
   341	  return {
   342	    cells: cellRows,
   343	    pressureRows,
   344	    marginal: {
   345	      n: moments.length,
   346	      rates: Object.fromEntries(
   347	        ARM_NAMES.map((name, arm) => [name, round(rateOf(moments, arm))]),
   348	      ) as Record<typeof ARM_NAMES[number], number>,
   349	    },
   350	  };
   351	};
   352	
   353	const describeBlock = (
   354	  moments: readonly Moment[], matches: number, cuts: { low: number; high: number },
   355	) => {
   356	  const table = buildTable(moments, cuts);
   357	  const clusters = new Set(moments.map((m) => m.cluster)).size;
   358	  return { matches, clusters, moments: moments.length, table };
   359	};
   360	
   361	const runExperiment = () => {
   362	  const build = harvest(BUILD_SEED_START, BUILD_BUDGET);
   363	  const heldout = harvest(HELDOUT_SEED_START, HELDOUT_BUDGET);
   364	  const cuts = supportCuts(build.moments.map((m) => m.support));
   365	
   366	  const buildBlock = describeBlock(build.moments, build.matches, cuts);
   367	  const heldoutBlock = describeBlock(heldout.moments, heldout.matches, cuts);
   368	
   369	  // --- §8: the exchange rate, PAIRED per moment, reported never gated -------
   370	  const exchange = HOLD_LADDER.map((k, index) => {
   371	    const arm = index + 1;
   372	    const paired = clusterBootstrap(build.moments.map((m) => ({
   373	      cluster: m.cluster,
   374	      value: (m.arms[arm].shot ? 1 : 0) - (m.arms[0].shot ? 1 : 0),
   375	    })), index);
   376	    const unpairedHold = clusterBootstrap(build.moments.map((m) => ({
   377	      cluster: m.cluster, value: m.arms[arm].shot ? 1 : 0,
   378	    })), 10 + index);
   379	    const unpairedNow = clusterBootstrap(build.moments.map((m) => ({
   380	      cluster: m.cluster, value: m.arms[0].shot ? 1 : 0,
   381	    })), 20 + index);
   382	    const concession = clusterBootstrap(build.moments.map((m) => ({
   383	      cluster: m.cluster,
   384	      value: (m.arms[arm].conceded ? 1 : 0) - (m.arms[0].conceded ? 1 : 0),
   385	    })), 30 + index);
   386	    const byPressure = ([0, 1, 2] as Band[]).map((p) => {
   387	      const rows = build.moments.filter((m) => m.pressureBand === p);
   388	      return {
   389	        pressureBand: p, n: rows.length,
   390	        delta: round(mean(rows.map((m) => (m.arms[arm].shot ? 1 : 0) - (m.arms[0].shot ? 1 : 0)))),
   391	      };
   392	    });
   393	    // §8.3 the release-origin twin — only defined where the hold reached its
   394	    // own release, and never substituted for the primary.
   395	    const released = build.moments.filter((m) => m.arms[arm].shotFromRelease !== null);
   396	    const releaseTwin = clusterBootstrap(released.map((m) => ({
   397	      cluster: m.cluster,
   398	      value: (m.arms[arm].shotFromRelease ? 1 : 0) - (m.arms[0].shot ? 1 : 0),
   399	    })), 40 + index);
   400	    return {
   401	      holdTicks: k,
   402	      paired: {
   403	        point: round(paired.point), lower: round(paired.lower), upper: round(paired.upper),
   404	      },
   405	      unpaired: {
   406	        hold: round(unpairedHold.point), actNow: round(unpairedNow.point),
   407	        delta: round(unpairedHold.point - unpairedNow.point),
   408	        holdCi: [round(unpairedHold.lower), round(unpairedHold.upper)],
   409	      },
   410	      concessionTwin: {
   411	        point: round(concession.point),
   412	        lower: round(concession.lower),
   413	        upper: round(concession.upper),
   414	      },
   415	      byPressure,
   416	      releaseTwin: {
   417	        n: released.length,
   418	        point: round(releaseTwin.point),
   419	        lower: round(releaseTwin.lower),
   420	        upper: round(releaseTwin.upper),
   421	      },
   422	      holdAnatomy: {
   423	        survived: round(mean(build.moments.map((m) => (m.arms[arm].survivedHold ? 1 : 0)))),
   424	        lostToTackle: round(mean(build.moments.map((m) => (m.arms[arm].lostToTackle ? 1 : 0)))),
   425	      },
   426	    };
   427	  });
   428	
   429	  // --- gates ----------------------------------------------------------------
   430	  const x4 = build.inertPins.length > 0 && build.inertPins.every((pin) => pin.identical);
   431	  const bite = mean(build.moments.map((m) => (m.arms[3].signature !== m.arms[0].signature ? 1 : 0)));
   432	  const x5 = bite >= X5_BITE_FLOOR;
   433	
   434	  const rowFloorOk = (block: ReturnType<typeof describeBlock>) =>
   435	    block.table.pressureRows.every((row) => row.n >= PRESSURE_ROW_FLOOR);
   436	
   437	  const h1 = ARM_NAMES.map((name) => ({
   438	    arm: name,
   439	    delta: round(Math.abs(
   440	      buildBlock.table.marginal.rates[name] - heldoutBlock.table.marginal.rates[name],
   441	    )),
   442	  }));
   443	  const h2 = ([0, 1, 2] as Band[]).flatMap((p) => {
   444	    const b = buildBlock.table.pressureRows[p];
   445	    const h = heldoutBlock.table.pressureRows[p];

     1	# C4 T1-FLIGHT — the ball gets up
     2	
     3	Status: **PRE-REGISTERED 2026-07-27 — everything below is frozen before any
     4	implementation and before any data.** C4 v1's first stage under **commander
     5	ruling #30.3** and the design contract's
     6	[§5.5 re-aim amendment](C4-AERIAL-ARRIVAL.md). Autonomous mode, one experiment
     7	in flight. Nothing here may be tuned after first sight of results.
     8	
     9	Date: 2026-07-27
    10	
    11	## 1. What T1-FLIGHT is
    12	
    13	T0b closed C2 with residual zero and named the seat: **H0 height-preempted
    14	56.78%** — the ball was never inside the outfield header band when it arrived,
    15	so no contest could occur whoever was standing there. Its deliveries peak at a
    16	median **1.00–1.06 m** against a **1.35 m** floor. #30.2's banked sentence:
    17	*nobody is absent — the aerial game fails by a third of a metre of flight and
    18	half a metre of arrival.*
    19	
    20	T1-FLIGHT makes the ball get up. **Aim geometry is untouched** (Q1's surviving
    21	half), the mechanism is derived from the code in §2 below, and every guard is
    22	carried: I2 HARD, the §2 band, the behavioural suite, the #20 battery and
    23	co-evolution.
    24	
    25	## 2. The mechanism, derived from the code before any data (#30.3)
    26	
    27	### 2.1 The arithmetic
    28	
    29	`performCross` (`mechanics.ts:552-595`) delegates the flight to
    30	`loftKick(match, crosser, spot, 0.5, 0.038, 0.7, 1.7, 1.1, spin)`
    31	(`mechanics.ts:512-544`), which computes
    32	
    33	```text
    34	T  = clamp(tBase + dEff·tPerM, tMin, tMax)   = clamp(0.5 + dEff·0.038, 0.7, 1.7)
    35	kickBall(..., speed = dEff / T, loft = GRAVITY·T/2)
    36	```
    37	
    38	That is a plain ballistic launch: apex at `T/2`, and
    39	
    40	```text
    41	peak = vz² / 2g = (gT/2)² / 2g = g·T² / 8 = 1.22625 · T²      (GRAVITY 9.81, constants.ts:176)
    42	```
    43	
    44	Setting `peak ≥ HEADER_MIN_HEIGHT` (1.35 m, `constants.ts:186`):
    45	
    46	```text
    47	T    ≥ √(8 · 1.35 / 9.81)      = 1.04925 s
    48	dEff ≥ (1.04925 − 0.5) / 0.038 = 14.454 m
    49	```
    50	
    51	⭐ **A cross whose effective range is under ~14.5 m cannot reach header height.
    52	That is arithmetic, not tuning.** At the current `tMin` of 0.7 s the apex is
    53	**0.601 m**; at `tMax` 1.7 s it is 3.544 m.
    54	
    55	### 2.2 The prediction this makes about T0b's own numbers
    56	
    57	Inverting `peak = 1.22625·T²` on the measured medians, **registered here as an
    58	ex-ante prediction the run will check**:
    59	
    60	```text
    61	H0 (peak 1.00–1.06 m)  ⇒ T ≈ 0.903–0.930 s ⇒ dEff ≈ 10.6–11.3 m
    62	BAL crosses (2.19–2.26) ⇒ T ≈ 1.337–1.358 s ⇒ dEff ≈ 22.0–22.6 m
    63	```
    64	
    65	⭐⭐ **If that holds, the archetype gap is a DISTANCE gap, not a flight-law
    66	gap**: CROSS-archetype deliveries (60–62% headable) are struck from ~11 m and
    67	BAL's (76–84%) from ~22 m, through one shared law. The flight curve is not
    68	broken; it is *a function of distance only*, and a short cross therefore cannot
    69	be lofted. **F3 measures this and it is REPORTED, not gated** — if it holds it
    70	is a finding the commander needs, because it says the cross TRIGGER's distance
    71	is a second seat that neither the aim nor the flight owns.
    72	
    73	### 2.3 The intervention
    74	
    75	**Flag `c4Flight` (`MatchConfig`, default `EDS_BUNDLE_ARMED` = false).** In
    76	`performCross` **only** — no other `loftKick` caller is touched — the flight
    77	time gains a floor at the apex that clears the band:
    78	
    79	```text
    80	T_HEAD = √(8 · HEADER_MIN_HEIGHT / GRAVITY)     // 1.04925 s, DERIVED
    81	tMin:  0.7  →  T_HEAD          (crosses only, flag on)
    82	```
    83	
    84	**One derived constant and no free parameter.** The value is not chosen; it is
    85	the solution of `peak(T) = HEADER_MIN_HEIGHT`, and it is written in the code as
    86	that expression, not as a literal.
    87	
    88	Everything the change carries with it is automatic, and is **reported, never
    89	tuned**:
    90	
    91	* **horizontal speed falls** to `dEff/T` on short crosses (a 10 m delivery:
    92	  11.4 → 9.5 m/s);
    93	* **hang time rises** (10 m: 0.88 → 1.049 s) — and that gives the DEFENCE the
    94	  same extra time it gives the attack. An honest symmetric cost, not a
    95	  subsidy;
    96	* **the Magnus pre-compensation** `−spin·T/2` scales with T, so the closed-form
    97	  landing invariance the comment at `mechanics.ts:539-542` describes still
    98	  holds.
    99	
   100	**Why technique does not scale the floor.** Getting a cross airborne is not the
   101	hard part of crossing; putting it in the right place is — and that half is
   102	*already* technique-priced through `loftKick`'s existing noise and range-error
   103	channels (`1.3 − passing·0.55`, `1.25 − passing·0.5`, `orientationNoiseMul`,
   104	`orientationPowerMul`). Adding a second technique term to the capability would
   105	price the same attribute twice, which is exactly the double-pay hazard #28.5
   106	registered for `attacking = 0.3`.
   107	
   108	### 2.4 ⚠️ The one interpretive call, surfaced for the commander to reverse
   109	
   110	`performCross` leads the target's run by `target.vel × flight0 ×
   111	CROSS_LEAD_FRAC` where `flight0 = clamp(0.5 + d·0.038, 0.7, 1.7)` — **the same
   112	law**, used as the crosser's estimate of his own flight time. So "aim
   113	untouched" has two readings:
   114	
   115	* **literal** — leave `flight0` alone. The aim NUMBER is unchanged, and the aim
   116	  RULE ("lead the run by a meetable fraction of the flight") silently becomes
   117	  wrong: on short crosses the true flight is now longer than the estimate, so
   118	  every running target is systematically under-led.
   119	* **rule-preserving** — `flight0` takes the same floor. The aim number moves,
   120	  by at most `CROSS_LEAD_MAX` 3.5 m and only for moving targets, and the rule
   121	  keeps meaning what it says.
   122	
   123	**PRIMARY = rule-preserving**, because #30 protected Q1's surviving half, and
   124	Q1's surviving half is the *rule* (lead/pull/curl are well built), not a stale
   125	input to it. A lead computed from a flight time the ball no longer has is not
   126	the aim geometry being preserved; it is the aim geometry being broken by
   127	omission.
   128	
   129	**The literal variant runs as a REPORTED Phase-A arm** so the choice is
   130	measured rather than argued, and **this is flagged as the single place I
   131	interpreted the ruling** — the commander can reverse it before the run at no
   132	cost.

   165	```text

   171	⚠️ **AMENDED BEFORE THE RUN, in its own commit.** As first frozen, F1 tested
   172	the *sampled* `maxZ` against 1.35 m and F2 asked for 1e-6. Both are
   173	**unpassable by construction**: the floor puts a short cross's apex at exactly
   174	1.35 m, and a parabola read at tick boundaries under-reads its apex by up to
   175	`g·(dt/2)²/2 = 3.4e-4 m`, so the sampled value can sit just below the very
   176	threshold the mechanism guarantees. F1 now reads the LAUNCH (`vz`, exact and
   177	sampling-free); F2's tolerance is **3× the analytic sampling bound**. The
   178	`maxZ`-based headable share is reported alongside for continuity with T0R's

   180	not a gate.

   182	**F1 is tautological by construction, and that is exactly why it is a FIRES
   183	gate and not a payoff.** It proves the mechanism reached the world; it proves

   193	   parabola.** `Match.stepBall` is semi-implicit Euler (`z += vz·dt;
   194	   vz -= g·dt`), whose discrete apex sits ≈`vz·dt/2` ABOVE the continuous
   195	   `vz²/(2g)` — **measured at 0.053 m**, which is 50× the tick-sampling bound
   196	   F2's tolerance was derived against. The probe now replays the recurrence, so

   374	### 7.1 The FAIL is my gate, again, and I am not re-scoping it
   375	
   376	F2 is a **max over 5,547 records with a 1e-3 tolerance**. It fired on exactly
   377	one delivery, whose measured peak (2.661 m) is 1.02 m ABOVE the apex its launch
   378	capture implies (1.639 m) — the ball rose higher than the kick that was
   379	recorded. Diagnosed read-only: it is a delivery **re-struck by the same player
   380	inside its own window**, so `lastTouch` never changes, the `maxZ` guard never
   381	trips, and the capture's apex and the observed peak describe two different
   382	kicks. Its class is `C3def`, `band = 40`, no touch registered.
   383	
   384	**A max-statistic over thousands of records at a tight tolerance is a
   385	coupon-collector gate** — it asks that no single record anywhere be
   386	pathological, which is a different claim from "the arithmetic reached the
   387	world". That is a gate-design defect I own, and it is the **second time in this
   388	stage** my own instrument has fired rather than the world (the first, F1/F2's
   389	sampling forms, was caught before the run; this one was not).
   390	
   391	**It is not re-scoped after sight** (§8), and the honest verdict stands: the
   392	stage FAILED. What the commander needs alongside it is that the arithmetic is
   393	verified on **5,546 of 5,547** crosses at error exactly **0**, and F1 — the
   394	launch-side statement of the same claim, evaluated on all 5,466 valid launches
   395	— passes at **100.00%**.

    17	## 1. What T2-ARRIVAL is
    18	
    19	T1-FLIGHT fixed the height and **enlarged** the arrival gap: H3
    20	(*the ball crossed head height with nobody at head height*) went from
    21	11.74% to **22.90% of all crosses**, and the nearest body got **farther**,
    22	2.08 → 2.39 m. Deliveries that were previously un-headable by construction
    23	now arrive headable and find nobody there.
    24	
    25	T2 is that half-metre, and nothing else. Not the contest (1.35 m stays,
    26	Q3), not the delivery (healthy, Q1, and now also flight-corrected), not
    27	conversion (a ceiling, never a target, Q5).
    28	
    29	## 2. The mechanism, derived from the code before any data (#30.3)
    30	
    31	### 2.1 ⚠️ One of the three authorized components is ALREADY IN THE ENGINE
    32	
    33	The contract's §2 describes the post-kick landing re-route as something to
    34	build. **It exists in open play, and has since Phase 63** —
    35	`actionExecutor.ts:159–166`:
    36	
    37	```ts
    38	if (p.action.type === 'ReceivePass' && ball.owner === null && ball.z > CONTROL_MAX_HEIGHT) {
    39	  const { x: lx, y: ly } = ballLanding(ball);
    40	  const vl = Math.hypot(ball.vel.x, ball.vel.y) || 1;
    41	  target = { x: lx - (ball.vel.x / vl) * 2.5, y: ly - (ball.vel.y / vl) * 2.5 };
    42	}
    43	```
    44	
    45	Its own comment says it is *"the 31.9 corner principle in open play"*:
    46	attack the DESCENT 2.5 m upstream, not the drop. `ballLanding`
    47	(`perception.ts:97–112`) is the one shared projector, Magnus-corrected and
    48	exact.
    49	
    50	**So the re-route is not missing. It is granted to exactly one body — the
    51	registered pass target** (`registerPass` → `match.pendingPass` → the
    52	`ReceivePass` candidate at `PlayerBrain.ts:1105–1107`, live for 3.5 s,
    53	longer than any cross flight). This re-shapes T2's mechanism from *"add a
    54	re-route"* to *"widen who is eligible for the one that already works"* —
    55	still Q2's safe half, still post-kick, still observable physics. **Flagged
    56	as a correction to the contract's own premise; the commander can reverse
    57	the framing before the run at no cost.**
    58	
    59	### 2.2 ⭐⭐⭐ And the real defect is that the box EMPTIES during the flight
    60	
    61	`PlayerBrain.ts:1144`, the gate on every licensed attacking run:
    62	
    63	```ts
    64	if ((team.runners.has(p.index) || arriving) &&
    65	    (carrier ? carrier !== p : match.phase === 'restart' || crashLive)) {
    66	```
    67	
    68	Read the false branch. The instant a cross leaves the boot in open play,
    69	`ball.owner === null`, `match.phase === 'playing'`, and `crashLive` is
    70	false (`team.cornerCrash` is set for corners only, `Match.ts:2208–2214`).
    71	**Every runner and the arriver lose their `MakeRun` candidate.**
    72	`SupportBallCarrier` also requires a carrier (`1128`), so what is left is
    73	`MoveToFormationSpot` (`1172–1176`). With a decision cadence of ~0.3–0.5 s
    74	inside a ~1.1 s flight, most of them re-decide once or twice mid-air.
    75	
    76	Upstream, the license itself dies too: `assignRunners` clears
    77	`team.arriver = null` every tick (`TeamBrain.ts:113–114`) and re-sets it
    78	only while the ball is *in the wide attacking channel*
    79	(`ballLocalX > HALF_L − 21 && |ballPos.y| > 10`, `211`) — which a ball
    80	flying into the box has left.
    81	
    82	**This is Phase 31.9's bug, still present in open play.** The engine has
    83	already been patched for it twice, in the same shape, with the reasons
    84	in-comment: `team.cornerCrash` for corners (*"the licenses died HERE and
    85	the crashers turned back toward their formation spots before the ball was
    86	struck"*) and the overlap license at `TeamBrain.ts:114–117` (*"the kick
    87	clears `ball.owner`, and a license torn up at that instant strands the
    88	runner — and the arriving ball — mid-flight"*).
    89	
    90	And it explains H3 exactly: the ball needs ~1.1 s to reach the header
    91	band, and for most of that second every attacking body except the
    92	registered target is running **away from the box**.
    93	
    94	### 2.3 The intervention, therefore: the open-play analogue of `cornerCrash`
    95	
    96	Two nested flags, both default OFF, crosses only:
    97	
    98	**`c4Arrival` — the license survives the delivery.** `performCross` snapshots
    99	the already-licensed bodies (`team.runners` + `team.arriver`, exactly as
   100	`Match.ts:2210–2213` snapshots them at the corner hand-off) into a
   101	`team.crossFlight` record, and `PlayerBrain.ts:1144`'s `crashLive` clause is
   102	generalized to accept it. **No new license, no new count, no new scorer** —
   103	whoever the engine had already sent forward simply does not turn around
   104	mid-air.
   105	
   106	*Duration, derived not chosen*: `until = simTime + ballLanding(ball).t` read
   107	at the kick — the license lasts exactly the flight and not a tick longer.
   108	(The corner's 2.8 s carries hand-off slack open play does not have.)
   109	It also ends early the moment the ball is owned again.
   110	
   111	*Scope, derived*: armed only when `team.cornerCrash === null`, so a corner
   112	delivery keeps its own machinery and can never be double-licensed.
   113	
   114	**`c4ArrivalReroute` — the closest licensed body gets the re-route that
   115	already works.** While the license is live and the ball is above
   116	`CONTROL_MAX_HEIGHT`, the licensed body closest to `ballLanding` targets the
   117	meet point `landing − flightDir·2.5` — the **same formula** as
   118	`actionExecutor.ts:164–166` and as the corner branch at `320`/`344`. The
   119	others keep their existing routing untouched, exactly as the corner branch
   120	leaves its non-closest crashers on their structure spots for the knockdown.
   121	
   122	Nesting is forced: without the license there is no `MakeRun` to re-route, so
   123	the ladder OFF → license → license+re-route is the only decomposition
   124	available, and it is the one the arms below run.
   125	
   126	### 2.4 What this deliberately does NOT do
   127	
   128	* **Nothing pre-kick.** The arriver keeps the 16 m arc until the ball is
   129	  struck. That is Q2's forbidden half (it needs the delivery moment, which
   130	  open play knows only through evidence or doctrine), it is what revert 2
   131	  broke, and the arc is a *measured* channel in its own right
   132	  (`cutback-anatomy`: 20% → shot).
   133	* **Therefore the offside exposure is structurally bounded**, not merely
   134	  gated: the flag is judged at the kick (`offsideAtKick`, `mechanics.ts:234`)
   135	  and every body this stage moves starts moving *after* it. Revert 2's blast
   136	  came from bodies crashing *before* the delivery. The canary in §4.6 is
   137	  still HARD — structure is an argument, and the discipline gates arguments.
   138	* **No new bodies in the box.** If the answer turns out to be *more*
   139	  crashers, that is a licensing change and its own stage.
   140	
   141	### 2.5 ⚠️ The one interpretive call, surfaced for the commander to reverse
   142	
   143	**The defence gets no equivalent.** This is asymmetric by construction, and
   144	I am not hiding it. Two facts make it the defensible reading rather than a
   145	gift: the defending side's landing-chase already exists and **explicitly
   146	excludes box landings** (`TeamBrain.ts:391–418` — *"box landings belong to
   147	the marking scheme"*, an unscoped first cut cost 0.77 goals/match), and
   148	T1-FLIGHT measured the defence taking **71%** of the new contests without
   149	any such help. So the asymmetry corrects an imbalance rather than creating
   150	one.
   151	
   152	Unlike T1-FLIGHT §2.4 I am **not** running the alternative as an arm: a
   153	defensive re-route is outside #32.4's authorized scope, and adding it
   154	unbidden would be exactly the improvisation the discipline forbids.
   155	Registered for the commander instead.

   173	## 4. Phase A — gates
   174	
   175	Every gate is powered ex ante against its measured base rate; **none is
   176	disclosed as weak** (#29.5), and **none is a max-statistic** (#32.1).
   177	
   178	### 4.1 A0-CENSUS — the reachability question, answered before the intervention
   179	
   180	Read-only, zero `src/**`, run first on the same block. T0's lesson:
   181	instrument before gating. It asks the one question that decides whether
   182	this mechanism can possibly work.
   183	
   184	For every H3 cross, take the nearest licensed attacking body at the kick and
   185	decompose:
   186	
   187	```text
   188	R1  REACHABLE  — his distance to the meet point is <= topSpeed x (remaining
   189	                 flight time), i.e. the routing is what failed
   190	R2  MARGINAL   — reachable within 1.15x that budget (the executor's own
   191	                 steering/accel losses live here)
   192	R3  UNREACHABLE— he could not have arrived at any routing
   193	R4  NO LICENCE — nobody was licensed at the kick at all
   194	```
   195	
   196	**A0 cannot change a single Phase-A gate value.** It can only stop the
   197	stage, by one pre-registered rule:
   198	
   199	```text
   200	STOP if  R3 + R4  >  80% of H3 crosses
   201	```
   202	
   203	**80% is derived, not chosen**: the addressable population is
   204	`(1 − R3 − R4) × 22.90%`; at the same one-in-four conversion assumption D1
   205	is powered on, an addressable share below 20% yields
   206	`0.25 × 0.20 × 22.90 = 1.15pp`, which is **below D1's 2.32pp MDE** — and
   207	#29.5 forbids running a gate that cannot distinguish its own two readings.
   208	Above the threshold the intervention proceeds; below it, the seat is
   209	pre-kick anticipation (Q2's forbidden half → Stage III) and that is the
   210	commander's, not this session's.
   211

   223	### 4.3 F — the mechanism fires (layer 1 of the six-layer chain)
   224	
   225	```text
   226	F1  LICENCE SURVIVAL. Of crosses that had >=1 licensed attacking body at the
   227	    kick, the share where >=1 licensed body is still on MakeRun at the tick
   228	    the ball first enters the header band:
   229	        A0  reported (expected near zero -- this is the defect)
   230	        A2  >= 90%                                        (seam bites, X5-class)
   231	F2  RE-ROUTE FIDELITY, per-record with NAMED exception classes (#32.1 --
   232	    NOT a max over records). On every tick where the licence is live, the
   233	    ball is above CONTROL_MAX_HEIGHT and a closest licensed body exists,
   234	    his steering target either equals `landing - flightDir*2.5` to 1e-9, or
   235	    falls into a named class:
   236	        E1  the onside clamp rewrote it (actionExecutor:547 -- inert while
   237	            the ball is unowned, so this class is expected EMPTY)
   238	        E2  the barred-box clamp rewrote it (actionExecutor:571)
   239	        E3  he stopped being the closest between decision and execution
   240	    GATE: the UNEXPLAINED residual is exactly 0. Class counts reported.
   241	```
   242	
   243	F1's 90% floor is the same seam-bites form C5 T1 used, powered the same
   244	way: at n ≈ 5,500 the binomial SE at p = 0.9 is 0.40pp, so 90% sits ~25σ
   245	below a working seam and far above a broken one — it separates *fires* from
   246	*does not fire*, which is all a layer-1 gate is for.
   247	
   248	**F1 and F2 prove the mechanism reached the world. They prove nothing about
   249	whether the world is better.** The payoff is D1.
   250	
   251	### 4.3b ⚠️ Instrument facts disclosed before the run, in their own commit
   252	
   253	Three things the implementation surfaced. None touches a gate value, the
   254	mechanism, D1's power, I2's margin, the canary's band or §6's readings.
   255	
   256	1. **F2 needs an observability field, and I added one.** The gate compares
   257	   the engine's steering target against the meet point; a probe cannot see a
   258	   local. `Player.c4Trace = { meet, applied }` is written by the executor on
   259	   the tick its branch fires and cleared at the top of every `executeAction`.
   260	   It is **never read by any decision** and is null in every flags-off world.
   261	   Without it F2 could only be *asserted* in a unit test instead of *measured*
   262	   over the run, which is the weaker thing #32.1 was trying to get away from.
   263	2. **E3 turns out to be structurally impossible, and the class is kept
   264	   anyway.** `Match.step` runs every `executeAction` in one loop, after
   265	   `simTime += dt` and before any physics or ball step, so every body executes
   266	   off the same frozen world — "he stopped being closest between decision and
   267	   execution" cannot happen within a tick. The probe replicates the executor's
   268	   own preconditions at the pre-step boundary for exactly this reason. The
   269	   class stays in the ledger; an empty class is a result, not a defect.
   270	3. **A corner takes precedence and those ticks are EXCLUDED from F2's
   271	   population, counted separately.** `crossFlight` is armed only when
   272	   `cornerCrash === null`, but a corner can begin while one is live, and the
   273	   executor's crash branch wins. This is X6's own rule seen from the other
   274	   side; the count is reported so the exclusion is visible rather than silent.
   275	
   276	### 4.4 D — the deliverable (#28.4's "CONTESTS, never goals")
   277	
   278	```text
   279	D1  PRIMARY. The ATTACKING contest share of crosses (C3atk) RISES, A2 vs A0,
   280	    paired same-seed, 95% cluster-bootstrap CI lower bound > 0
   281	```
   282	
   283	**Power, derived**: C3atk sits at **25.17%** of crosses (T1-FLIGHT §7.3,
   284	flag-on), so at n ≈ 5,500 per arm the unpaired difference SE is 0.83pp and
   285	the MDE at 80% is **2.32pp**; pairing shrinks it further. Expected effect:
   286	H3 is 22.90% of all crosses and its median miss is 2.39 m — a body who
   287	currently spends ~0.5 s of the flight walking away covers ~3.2 m at 6.5 m/s,
   288	so the geometry is comfortably inside the budget. Converting a quarter of H3
   289	gives **≈ +5.7pp**, a **2.5×** margin over the MDE.
   290	
   291	C3atk rather than total contests, deliberately: T1-FLIGHT's +3.42pp went
   292	71% to the defence, and this stage's mechanism is attacker-side only. Total
   293	contests and C3def are reported beside it.
   294	
   295	Mediators — the result must arrive via the intended path:
   296	
   297	```text
   298	M1  H3's share of ALL crosses FALLS (CI upper bound < 0) -- the target,
   299	    sized at 22.90%
   300	M2  the minimum ATTACKER distance while the ball is in the header band
   301	    falls (median, with CI) -- the half-metre itself
   302	M3  attacking bodies in the box at the tick the ball enters the band RISES
   303	    -- the direct echo of "the box stops emptying"
   304	```

   324	### 4.6 The offside canary, HARD (revert 2's +50% blast)
   325	
   326	```text
   327	OC  the 95% cluster-bootstrap CI UPPER bound on the paired difference in
   328	    BOTH-TEAM offsides per match must be BELOW +0.29 / match         (HARD)
   329	```
   330	
   331	**Both numbers derived, and the SD MEASURED before the freeze rather than
   332	assumed.** A read-only sizing smoke (360 matches, `c4Flight` ON, block
   333	910,000 — consumed for this purpose and now excluded from Phase A) gives
   334	both-team offsides **2.4861/match, SD 1.8298** (over-dispersion 1.35 — a
   335	Poisson assumption would have been 16% optimistic, which is exactly why it
   336	was measured). At 2,695 matches per arm the unpaired difference SE is
   337	**0.050/match**, so the MDE at 80% is 0.14/match.
   338	
   339	The band is **one quarter of revert 2's measured blast** (2.20 → 3.36 =
   340	+1.16/match): it fires long before the failure it exists to catch, it sits
   341	2.1× above the MDE so the gate can distinguish its two readings, and a true
   342	zero clears it by 5.8σ. Attacking-side offsides (1.2139/match, SD 1.1202)
   343	reported beside it.

   369	## 6. Pre-laid readings
   370	
   371	Three, exhaustive, laid before the run:
   372	
   373	* **(a) D1 resolves positive** — the arrival gap was a *routing* failure, the
   374	  bodies were always there, and the corner machinery's safe half generalizes
   375	  as Q2 predicted. The pair audit becomes the next question.
   376	* **(b) D1 resolves negative or straddles zero** — the bodies cannot use the
   377	  extra second, whatever A0's reachability decomposition said about the
   378	  geometry. Then the arrival seat is **anticipation, not routing**: the body
   379	  has to leave before the ball does, which is Q2's forbidden half and belongs
   380	  to the perception layer. Stop, return to the commander, no re-pose here.
   381	* **(c) D1 resolves positive but I2 or the canary fires** — the arrival was
   382	  bought with something the contract said we would not spend. HARD abort,
   383	  and the honest reading is that the box cannot be filled at this scale
   384	  without the ecology paying for it.
   385	
   386	Registered non-claims: the contest stays a lottery (Q3); `attacking = 0.3`
   387	stays and is not re-priced (Q4); conversion does not rise, and is not
   388	expected to fall as far as T1-FLIGHT's did — more attacking bodies is the
   389	one thing in v1 that pushes back on that decrease, which makes I2 a real
   390	gate here and not a formality.

   392	## 7. Result
   393	
   394	### 7.0 A0-CENSUS — ✅ **PROCEED.** The arrival gap is a routing failure.
   395	
   396	Run 2026-07-27 on block 920,000, `c4Flight` ON, 2,695 matches, **5,745
   397	crosses**, twice byte-identical, SHA `17c46125…41b0`.
   398	Probe: `scripts/probes/c4-t2-a0-census.ts` (read-only, zero `src/**`).
   399	
   400	**The target replicates on a block it was not measured on** — H3 **23.03%**
   401	of all crosses against T1-FLIGHT's 22.90%, median miss **2.32 m** against
   402	2.39 m, C3atk **25.50%** against 25.17%. The population D1 is powered on is
   403	the population that exists.
   404	
   405	```text
   406	R1  REACHABLE     96.60%
   407	R2  MARGINAL       2.04%
   408	R3  UNREACHABLE    1.21%
   409	R4  NO LICENCE     0.15%
   410	STOP statistic (R3+R4)  1.36%   CI [0.76, 2.02]   threshold 80%
   411	```
   412	
   413	Not close. The geometry is not the binding constraint anywhere: the nearest
   414	licensed body needs a median **3.35 m** against a median budget of **7.95 m**
   415	over a **1.03 s** flight — **4.86 m of slack**. A licence exists on 100% of
   416	crosses (mean 2.14 bodies) and includes the arriver on 72%.
   417	
   418	**What this does and does not license.** It is a *necessary-condition*
   419	screen and it passed with room: the bodies could be there. It says nothing
   420	about whether they will be — that is D1's question, and A0 cannot answer it.
   421	The predicate is deliberately generous (straight line at top speed), which is
   422	what R2's band existed to soften; with 4.86 m of median slack a much tighter
   423	bound would also have passed, so the reading survives the predicate's
   424	looseness rather than depending on it.
   425	
   426	**No Phase-A gate value was touched.** A0's only power was to stop the stage.
   427

   504	
   505	/**
   506	 * Loft a ball to land at `target`: flight time grows with distance
   507	 * (tBase + m·tPerM, clamped), horizontal speed = distance/time, and the
   508	 * vertical launch is whatever brings it back down exactly at landing
   509	 * (airborne balls fly friction-free, so the projectile math is exact).
   510	 * Accuracy: direction noise like a ground pass plus a RANGE error — long
   511	 * deliveries drift short/long; technique and passBias tame both.
   512	 */
   513	function loftKick(
   514	  match: Match, p: Player, target: V2,
   515	  tBase: number, tPerM: number, tMin: number, tMax: number, noiseMul: number,
   516	  spin = 0,
   517	): void {
   518	  const team = match.teams[p.side];
   519	  const opp = match.teams[1 - p.side];
   520	  const aimDir = norm(sub(target, p.pos));
   521	  const misalign = kickMisalignment(p, aimDir);
   522	  const d = dist(p.pos, target);
   523	  const pressure = pressureAt(p.pos, opp.players);
   524	  const noise =
   525	    match.rng.gaussian() *
   526	    (0.03 + pressure * 0.05 + d * 0.0011) * noiseMul *
   527	    (1.15 - team.genome.passBias * 0.3) *
   528	    (1 - team.confidence * 0.12) * // morale sharpens/frays the pass (Phase 111)
   529	    (1.3 - p.attrs.passing * 0.55) *
   530	    oneTouchMul(p) *
   531	    orientationNoiseMul(misalign, p.attrs.passing);
   532	  const dir = rotate(aimDir, noise);
   533	  // Range error + orientation power loss both shorten/stretch the delivery.
   534	  let dEff = d * orientationPowerMul(misalign, p.attrs.passing);
   535	  dEff *= 1 + match.rng.gaussian() * (0.02 + d * 0.0008) * (1.25 - p.attrs.passing * 0.5) * oneTouchMul(p);
   536	  dEff = Math.max(dEff, 3);
   537	  const T = clamp(tBase + dEff * tPerM, tMin, tMax);
   538	  // Magnus pre-compensation (Phase 37): launch rotated −spin·T/2 so the
   539	  // ARC's chord still points where the aim did — the designed landing
   540	  // point (and the whole 31.9 corner chain) is invariant; only the path
   541	  // between bends. ballLanding() projects the same closed form.
   542	  match.lastPassKind = { kind: 'through', t: match.simTime };
   543	  match.kickBall(p, spin === 0 ? dir : rotate(dir, -spin * T * 0.5), dEff / T, (GRAVITY * T) / 2);
   544	  match.ball.spin = spin;
   545	}

   718	export function performLoftedPass(match: Match, passer: Player, mate: Player, offsideExempt = false): void {
   719	  if (match.ball.owner !== passer || passer.kickCooldown > 0) return;

   722	  // hung 2.15s — any defender within ~12m of the drop reached it, and the
   723	  // receiving WINGER is the worst header in the game (AERIAL_ROLE 0.06 vs
   724	  // DF 0.3), so the diagonal completed ~20% and wing play starved. A flat
   725	  // 1.4–1.6s ball reaches the flank before the fullback does.
   726	  const flight0 = clamp(0.55 + dist(passer.pos, mate.pos) * 0.033, 1.1, 2.1);
   727	  const lead = add(mate.pos, scale(mate.vel, flight0 * 0.7));
   728	  const oneTouch = passer.firstTouchWindow > 0;
   729	  // The switch swings (Phase 70) — bulge away from whoever works the drop.
   730	  const swing = aerialSwing(passer, passer.pos, lead, match.teams[1 - passer.side].players);

   733	  team.stats.longBalls++;

   748	 * investment invisible — +0.45 strength bought +0.045 of duel score

   751	 * defending 0.15: the aerial payoff phase-47 assigned to strength is

    14	## 1. The measured case, from the map

    16	* **The delivery is HEALTHY** — lead/pull/curl/one-touch all priced
    17	  (`mechanics.ts:552-595`); the target scorer ranks who is ALREADY there
    18	  (`PlayerBrain.ts:511-533`) and nothing anywhere sends a body into the
    19	  box BECAUSE a cross is coming.
    20	* **The contest is a one-tick radius-1.35 m lottery** with a dice term
    21	  (`rng(0,0.45)`) the size of every skill term — no jump, no hang, no
    22	  body position (`mechanics.ts:785-812`).
    23	* ⛔ **The arrival aims at the WRONG radius**: the only wide-side arrival
    24	  runner is routed to the CUTBACK arc target (`actionExecutor.ts:
    25	  351-355`, 16 m out — Phase 31's spot) while a pulled cross lands near
    26	  the penalty spot; non-runners hold BALL-relative supportSpots, so a
    27	  wide ball drags support toward the touchline.
    28	* ⭐⭐ **The corner machinery already solves timed box-filling** —
    29	  3 crashers by aerialSense, `cornerCrashSpots`, nearest re-routed to
    30	  the TRUE parabola landing, staged 4.5 m off before the kick
    31	  (`actionExecutor.ts:304-349`). Open play has none of the three.
    32	* **The two archived reverts bound the design**: a generic
    33	  openness-value field EMPTIES the box (it is a low-openness contested
    34	  zone — revert 1), and unsynced crashing explodes offside +50%
    35	  (revert 2: bodies wanted to crash but ran on a different clock from
    36	  the delivery). **The disease is the two clocks again** — E5g's
    37	  overlap anatomy on a different part of the pitch.
    38	* **The numbers that aim the slice**: balanced teams already fill
    39	  decently (noAerial 26%); cross→goal ≈5% vs real football's 1–2% —
    40	  **conversion is a CEILING, never a target**.

    80	## 3. Design invariants — the map's six questions, ruled
    81	
    82	* **Q1 — C4 v1 is the ARRIVAL link.** Delivery healthy (untouched);
    83	  contest physics deferred until there are bodies to contest; the
    84	  mis-aim + the safe half of the corner machinery are the actionable
    85	  truths.
    86	* **Q2 — the corner machinery generalizes by HALVES.** The post-kick
    87	  half (landing re-route) is pure observable physics and generalizes
    88	  now. The pre-kick half (staged, timed crashers) requires knowing the
    89	  delivery moment — corners know it by rule; open play knows it only
    90	  through evidence or doctrine. v1 takes the post-kick half plus the
    91	  routing fix of the ALREADY-authorized runner (he already starts
    92	  early; he just runs to the wrong spot). The full anticipatory form
    93	  waits for the perception/positioning layer — never a hand trigger.
    94	* **Q3 — 1.35 m stays, for now.** The radius is a deliberate
    95	  simplification; the missing TIME in the contest is real and is the
    96	  same family as C5/C7 — its own stage, after arrivals exist. Fixing
    97	  the contest before the arrival would tune a lottery nobody attends.
    98	* **Q4 — `attacking = 0.3` is a NAMED SUBSIDY (I3).** It stands in for
    99	  a real arriving body. It stays in v1 (removing it is a balance
   100	  change), and T3 MEASURES whether it double-pays once real arrivals
   101	  exist; its removal is its own pre-registered step. The stagnation
   102	  precedent applies: neither copied forward nor silently deleted.
   103	* **Q5 — CONVERSION IS A CEILING (I2, hard invariant).** cross→goal is
   104	  already ≈5% vs the real game's 1–2%. Every stage carries
   105	  conversion-non-increase as a HARD gate; the deliverable is CONTESTS
   106	  (headers, both ways, arrivals), never goals. A stage that raises
   107	  conversion fails even if everything else passes.
   108	* **Q6 — split `noAerial` FIRST (T0).** "No header" ≠ "nobody there";
   109	  an aerial contract gating on the conflated number would repeat the
   110	  E5a window defect (one number, two meanings). The split definitions
   111	  pin separately per #18.

   163	
   164	Wide play becomes a real payoff channel: a cross has someone at the
   165	end of it, an aerial contest has attendance, and the value re-census

   167	precondition for width-based combinations returning measured, not

   169	stays where measurement puts it; the contest stays a lottery until its

   274

   276	
   277	| rung | count | share | CI |
   278	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
   279	| **H0** height-preempted | 829 | **56.78%** | [54.19, 59.36] |
   280	| **H1** keeper | 0 | **0.00%** | [0, 0] |

   282	| **H3** no contender at height | 611 | **41.85%** | [39.43, 44.59] |

   287	⭐ **H4 is empty.** A ladder derived from `tryAerial`'s own gate order, written
   288	before the data, accounts for **every single C2 cross** but two out of 2,905.
   289	That is the strongest possible form of "the code says where the gradient lives
   290	before the data does" — there is no unexplained mass to go looking for.
   291	
   292	⭐ **H1 is exactly zero, which is itself a finding**: keeper claims are real,
   293	but they all happen *before* arrival — they sit in C0, not in C2. The keeper is
   294	not why deliveries go unheaded.

   296	⚠️ **H2 would have read zero without the pre-run fix.** §3.2 caught
   297	`terminalZ` being read after the contact; at 1.37% the chest trap is small but
   298	real, and an unfixed instrument would have reported it as absent and made the
   299	ladder look cleaner than it is.
   300	
   301	### 7.4 ⭐⭐ Both dominant rungs are MARGINS, not absences
   302	
   303	This is the part that decides what C4 v1 can be.
   304	
   305	**H0 — the ball never gets up.** The deliveries in this rung peak at a median
   306	of **1.00–1.06 m** across all six combinations. `HEADER_MIN_HEIGHT` is 1.35 m,
   307	so these are not marginal misses of the band: they are **a third of a metre
   308	below its floor**, consistently. Pooled headable share (any cross reaching
   309	1.35 m) is **60–62% for the CROSS archetype and 76–84% for BAL**.
   310	
   311	**H3 — the bodies are 0.4–0.9 m short of a 1.35 m radius.** While the ball was
   312	headable, the nearest outfielder's median distance was **1.75–2.20 m**, with
   313	p10 **1.42–1.53 m** — i.e. even the closest tenth were *just* outside the
   314	radius. And:
   315	
   316	| combination | H3 n | median nearest | **within 2 m** | within 3 m |
   317	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   318	| CROSS vs NEUTRAL | 118 | 2.20 m | 39.8% | 79.7% |
   319	| CROSS vs BUS | 113 | 2.07 m | 42.5% | 72.6% |
   320	| CROSS vs PRESS | 115 | 2.08 m | 44.3% | 87.0% |
   321	| BAL vs NEUTRAL | 96 | 1.75 m | **61.5%** | 84.4% |
   322	| BAL vs BUS | 78 | 1.96 m | 53.8% | 91.0% |
   323	| BAL vs PRESS | 91 | 1.77 m | **65.9%** | 91.2% |
   324	
   325	**Nobody is absent. Everybody is close and nobody is close enough.** That
   326	sharpens #28.3(ii) from "the box fills" to a number: the contest fails by
   327	roughly half a metre.
   328	
   329	⚠️ **Registered honestly: H0 and H3 are a PARTITION, not a causal
   330	decomposition.** A low delivery also spends fewer ticks in the band, so it has
   331	fewer chances to have someone inside the radius — the two rungs are not
   332	independent, and "fix the height and H3 shrinks too" is a hypothesis this
   333	census cannot test. Any contract built on the split has to own that.

MUST sequence with the pinned open-play box-arrival gap (crosses currently find nobody ~50% `noAerial` — a duel model without arrivals has nothing to contest) | **PHASE-0 CODE MAP DONE 2026-07-27** → [`C4-PHASE0-CODE-MAP.md`](C4-PHASE0-CODE-MAP.md) (ruling #26.4, read-only, zero code). ⭐ **Headline: the delivery is a well-built pass to a named man; the contest is a one-tick radius lottery; the arrival is ONE licensed body aimed at the WRONG RADIUS for a cross.** `~50% noAerial` is not a crossing bug — it is the arithmetic of a **1.35 m** contest radius (`constants.ts:182`) meeting a box the run system was never asked to fill. ✅ **Delivery is the healthy link** (`mechanics.ts:552-595`): lead capped at `CROSS_LEAD_MAX` 3.5 m, 18% goal-pull (0.25 was tried and fed the keeper), technique-whipped inswinger, `oneTouch` priced. Its target scorer (`PlayerBrain.ts:511-533`) ranks **the bodies already there** — it has no term for whether anyone is there, and nothing anywhere sends bodies BECAUSE a cross is coming. ⛔ **The contest is instantaneous** (`mechanics.ts:785-812`): `s = aerialSense + attacking(0.3 in the box) + (1−d/1.35)·0.35 + rng(0,0.45)` — no jump, no takeoff, no airtime, no body position, and **the die is comparable in size to every other term**. Keeper claims first inside 1.9 m (`745-776`); the chest trap pre-empts (`781`). ⛔⛔ **The arrival mismatch is the sharpest finding**: open play licenses 1–3 runners by `RUN_ROLE_W + localX/45` (`TeamBrain.ts:185-197`) and **none of them is licensed BY a cross**; the single wide-ball arriver (`205-218`) is routed to **the edge-of-box arc 16 m out** (`actionExecutor.ts:351-355`) — that is the CUTBACK target Phase 31 built, while a cross with an 18% goal-pull drops near the penalty spot. Non-runners hold `supportSpot` (`formations.ts:546-560`), which is **relative to the ball**, so a wide ball pulls the support structure toward the touchline. ⭐⭐ **And the engine ALREADY knows how to fill a box on a delivery — it only does it for corners**: 3 licensed crashers ranked by `aerialSense − dist(flag)/45` (`TeamBrain.ts:159-168`), routed to `cornerCrashSpots`, the closest one **re-routed onto the true parabola landing**, and **held 4.5 m off the spot until the taker steps up** so the crash is a timed burst (`actionExecutor.ts:304-349`). Open play has no crash count, no landing re-route, no timing. ⚠️ **The banked history constrains the design hard** (`ROADMAP.md:1246-1306`): two honest reverts at this exact seat — an openness value-field made the box EMPTIER (*"the box is a LOW-openness contested zone, so the scorer AVOIDS it"*), and the two-eye field spiked **offsides +50%**, the tell being bodies arriving **uncoordinated with the delivery**; plus the under-weighted datum that a BALANCED team already fills the box (`noAerial` 26%, `atkHeader` 33%), so the 46–54% belongs to cross-spam and the extreme WIDE archetype; plus the honest ceiling that cross→goal ≈5% here vs **1–2% in real football**, so raising conversion is the wrong target. ⚠️ **Instrument caveat for T0**: `cross-anatomy` attributes by `headersWon` deltas in a 4 s window, so a delivery CHESTED down or controlled on the ground counts as `noAerial` — the number is *"no header"*, not *"no arrival"*, and that difference is load-bearing for a duel contract. §6 leaves six open questions (which link is C4 · does the corner machinery generalize · is 1.35 m the substrate defect or is the missing thing TIME in the contest · what `attacking = 0.3` is really standing in for · what must NOT move · whether `noAerial` should be split before it gates anything) <br>⭐⭐ **DESIGN CONTRACT DRAFTED by the commander on that map (2026-07-27): [`C4-AERIAL-ARRIVAL.md`](C4-AERIAL-ARRIVAL.md)** — the six questions RULED: **C4 v1 = the ARRIVAL link** (delivery healthy-untouched; contest physics deferred — "a duel model without arrivals has nothing to contest" still binds) · **the corner machinery generalizes by HALVES** (post-kick landing re-route = observable physics, generalizes now; docs/world-model/PROGRAMME.md:1725:| E5g | **The decision-moment trace** (ruling #23.3): in the VALUE arm, at every pass-decision moment inside an overlapper-live window, log the executable menu, each candidate's live price with its `(cell, band)` inputs, the runner's presence / rank / margin vs the winner, the chosen target, and his priced destination cell beside his truth cell — the stale-geometry seam, if it exists, shows up there. **Three outcomes pre-laid and exhaustive over the CHOICE**: (a) rarely on the menu = different clocks · (b) on the menu but not top-priced = the flags-off flip benchmark did not transfer · (c) top-priced and NOT chosen = a seam defect in the live argmax, hard escalation | [`EDS-E5G-DECISION-TRACE.md`](EDS-E5G-DECISION-TRACE.md) | **PRE-REGISTERED 2026-07-26** — P0 world-hash identity trace-on/off (X3's convention) · P1 staging pin against E5f's banked VALUE funnel integers · P2 ≥2,000 licence-active decision moments · P3 determinism. ⚠️ **#23.3 says zero `src/**` BEHAVIOUR change, not zero `src/**`**, and the menu with per-option prices existed nowhere — so `PricedPassOption` gains the `(cell, band)` it already computed internally and `PassChoiceTraceEntry` gains an `options` sidecar written only under `traceChoice`; re-deriving the menu outside would be a second implementation of the thing under measurement. ⭐ Registered as a fourth QUANTITY that is deliberately NOT a fourth outcome: the chooser picks a TARGET while the action layer decides whether to pass at all, so the chooser→release gap is measured against E5f's banked F3 and reported separately — it cannot later be presented as if it had been one of the three. <br>✅ **RUN 2026-07-26 — MEASURED; the contradiction resolves WITHOUT a defect** (§7, SHA `b6a5f43d…6c2a`, twice byte-identical, **P0 + P1 true**, fingerprint unchanged, **zero `src/**` behaviour change**). ⚠️ **First run came back INVALID and the pin did its job**: F1/F2/F3/counter/matches reproduced to the integer on all six clusters and **only F4 differed, by 1 on three of them** — this probe had nested F4 under F3 while E5f (and contract §3's own wording) counts the counter firing INDEPENDENTLY of the release. Corrected toward the pre-registration, never toward a number (E5c's U1 precedent); the re-run reproduces every banked integer and every decision-trace number is unchanged, since F4 enters none of them. ⛔ **P2 fired and it is MY DESIGN ERROR, owned not lowered**: I set the floor at 2,000 decision moments when the staging contains **854** — not a budget shortfall, six leagues × 24 seasons IS the whole of it, so **the floor was unreachable by construction**. Ruling #19's codified error in its worse form (that one was about inheriting a gate value un-re-powered; I invented one). §5 already said P2 does not invalidate, so it stands as fired and the intervals are simply wider than planned. ⭐⭐⭐ **The dominant fact is UPSTREAM of all three outcomes**: E5f's 4,812 matured runs contain only 854 decision moments — **0.177 per matured run (clusters 0.155–0.194), so in 82% of matured overlap runs the man on the ball never takes a pass decision while the licence is live**. That is #23.3's "different clocks" quantified, and it is bigger than the menu-level effect the outcome was worded around. ⭐⭐ **Outcome (c) is EXACTLY ZERO — 437 moments at rank 1, 437 chosen: whenever he is top-priced he IS taken.** The live argmax is clean, the hard-escalation branch does not fire, and no fork re-run is authorized. The remaining 417 non-picks split ~50/50 between (a) off-menu 210 and (b) on-menu-not-top 207. ⭐⭐ **The flip benchmark DID NOT TRANSFER, exactly as #23.2 registered in advance**: 0.82pp ahead in the flags-off world → **0.92pp BEHIND** in the deployed world (runner 0.0861 vs winner 0.0954), the sign flipping by about the same magnitude — a thin win on a 13.41pp axis that did not survive the world shift, and being top-priced is a coin flip (51.17%) rather than a property. **Which input moved: neither geometry nor the ladder** — priced cell equals truth cell **96.27%**, `band === −1` occurs **0.00%** of the time, and info classes are READ 644 / SEEN-UNREAD 0 / UNSEEN 112 / not-in-window 98. The loss is in the COMPARISON, against the same honest table: the winner most often sits in the runner's OWN cell (2→2 268, 3→3 160), so the threat band separates them, with 2→4 (91) the leading genuinely-more-advanced case. ⚠️ Those pairs pool wins with losses and locate the comparison rather than decompose it; the rank histogram (1→437, 2→121, 3→62, 4→24) is the loss structure. ⭐ **§3.1's fourth quantity found the OPPOSITE of a gap**: the chooser picks him 437 times against E5f's 550 banked releases over the same assignments — releases EXCEED picks (F3 counts releases anywhere in the span), so there is no action-layer loss. Registered, measured, negative. **What returns is a DESIGN question, not a defect**: the pattern needs a decision taken while a run is live, and the direct game does not take one in four fifths of them |

2747:| F8 | **PWA / install to the home screen** (user 2026-07-26: "manifest + 图标 + service worker(缓存优先 + 更新提示)+ 全屏 display + 比赛中 wake lock"). Not art — the shell around it — but run under Track F's rules because the phone is the binding constraint. ⭐ **Procedural icons, no committed binary**: iOS refuses an SVG home-screen icon, so `scripts/appIcon.ts` transcribes `public/icon.svg` into a shape list, rasterizes it analytically (3×3 supersampled, straight alpha) and encodes a PNG by hand over `node:zlib` — ~4 icons emitted straight into the bundle by a `pwaAssets` Vite plugin, nothing on disk in the repo. Each variant is right for its platform, which is itself tested: transparent rounded corners for Android's unmasked `purpose:any`, full-bleed opaque with the artwork inside the 80% safe circle for `maskable`, opaque square for `apple-touch-icon` (iOS applies its own mask). Manifest now `display: fullscreen` with a `display_override` fallback chain, `scope`/`start_url` relative so the Pages sub-path works, and a `@media (display-mode: fullscreen)` safe-area inset on `#app` so `black-translucent` does not park the topbar behind the clock — inert in a normal browser tab. Wake lock is a state machine (`src/ui/wakeLock.ts`), not a call at kickoff: the browser drops the lock on background so it must be RE-taken, and it is driven from the frame loop so a rejection must never become a per-frame retry (one attempt per episode; a paused game / finished match / attract-mode title screen all let the phone sleep, via the pure `screenShouldStayAwake`). <br>⚠️ **THREE defects a browser probe caught that the unit tests could not, all three total and all three silent — this is the row's real lesson: a service worker fails invisibly.** ① `cache.addAll` is ATOMIC and rejects on a DUPLICATE url; the plugin emits the icons *into* the bundle, so they arrived twice, install failed, and **no worker ever activated** — now deduped, and install caches entry-by-entry so one bad URL degrades to a partial cache instead of killing the worker. ② Vite marks the entry script/stylesheet `crossorigin`, so the browser sends `Origin`, and a server answering **`Vary: Origin`** (vite preview does; CDNs commonly do) made those two requests MISS entries that were provably in the cache — **offline was completely broken while the cache listing looked perfect**; fixed with `ignoreVary` on every lookup, pinned by a test that forbids a bare `.match(req)`. ③ `register()`'s implicit update check is a *soft* update Chromium throttles — a changed worker sat undetected across a reload for 24s, so **a deploy could go unnoticed indefinitely**; now an explicit `reg.update()` on load plus a throttled foreground re-check. Also removed a `window.load` gate on registration (this page holds 17 MB of audio, so `load` can be minutes away on a phone). <br>Design calls, disclosed: precache is the 1.7 MB shell ONLY — the 17 MB of audio is runtime-cached on first play into a separate UNVERSIONED media cache (re-downloading it per deploy would be hostile; `MEDIA_CACHE_VERSION` is the hand-bump escape hatch); no `skipWaiting()` on install, because swapping the bundle under a running match is exactly the interruption the cache exists to avoid — the user gets a dismissible top-centre bar (`新版本已就绪。/ 更新`) instead; **`?nosw=1` is a documented kill switch** that unregisters and clears every `evo-` cache before anything registers, the answer to a bad cache-first worker on a live site; and **`orientation` changed `landscape` → `any`** — a landscape lock would have rotated the game out from under a user who plays portrait at 390–640 px. Gates: tsc + build clean · **808/808** (+49, incl. a hand-written PNG decoder that verifies the encoder) · fingerprint `57b0bdab…c673` unchanged, measured before and after on the same tree · zero `src/sim` contact · 15/15 browser probe checks green against a served production build (installs, activates, controls, 19-entry precache with no audio, all icons 200, **boots with the network OFF**, update prompt appears and swaps the cache on accept, kill switch clears the stale one) · dev-server middleware serves every generated asset | ✅ **DONE 2026-07-26 — ✅ USER ACCEPTED 2026-07-26 ("pwa没问题"): installed on the phone, works. F8 closed** |
