     7	its own logic).
     8	
     9	Authority: [`STAGE3-POSITIONING-EYE.md`](STAGE3-POSITIONING-EYE.md) §5 P0
    10	(the deliverable), §4-Q5 (the instruments exist because a correct field can
    11	still oscillate), §6 (gate sources), §7 (stop rules) · PROBE-CONTRACTS §2 (the
    12	E5-style *one number, two meanings* sweep runs BEFORE anything gates) · #20
    13	(CI/cluster) · #22 (pattern geometry is censused, never asserted).
    14	
    15	**Nothing here gates anything and nothing here is an experiment.** P0's job is
    16	to make P1 possible: know who consumes a station, know what the incumbent's
    17	shape actually looks like, and define the instruments carefully enough that
    18	P2/P3 can gate on them without inheriting an ambiguous number.
    19	
    20	---
    21	
    22	## 1. The consumer map
    23	
    24	### 1.1 ⭐⭐⭐ The headline: there is no station DECISION. There is a station FUNCTION, evaluated every frame.
    25	
    26	`executeAction`'s own docstring (`actionExecutor.ts:33-37`) is the finding:
    27	
    28	> *"Dynamic targets — moving balls, moving opponents, sliding formation spots
    29	> — are recomputed here each frame so actions never chase stale data."*
    30	
    31	Every station producer below is a **pure function of live world state**, called
    32	inside `executeAction`, which runs for every player **every tick** (60 Hz,
    33	`Match.ts:817-819`). No station is stored, none is committed to, and none has
    34	a cadence of its own.
    35	
    36	**What DOES run on a cadence is the choice of station FAMILY, one level up:**
    37	
    38	| clock | period | what it decides | code |
    39	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    40	| `AI_INTERVAL` | **0.15 s** nominal | the player's ACTION — hence which station function owns him | `constants.ts:342`, `Match.ts:786-796` |
    41	| `TEAM_AI_INTERVAL` | **0.4 s** | runner / arriver / overlapper / chaser licences and mark assignments — hence which branch inside `MakeRun`/`MarkOpponent` applies | `constants.ts:344`, `Match.ts:766-774` |
    42	| per-event overrides | 0.05–0.30 s | reception settle, shooting range, restart taker, kickoff | `Match.ts:1255`, `1259`, `1301`, `1806`, `1995`, `2243`, `2668` |
    43	| kickoff stagger | `(index+1)·0.15/6` | de-phases the six bodies so they never all think on the same tick | `Match.ts:651` |
    44	
    45	⚠️ **This matters for Q2 and Q5 directly.** §4-Q5 asks that the eye's
    46	station decisions "run at the measured station cadence with COMMITMENT". There
    47	is no incumbent station cadence to measure — the incumbent recomputes at 60 Hz
    48	and is *implicitly* stable only because its inputs move slowly. So P1's
    49	commitment window **W is a new quantity, not an inherited one**, and the
    50	honest empirical anchors P0 can supply are (a) the 0.15 s action clock, (b) the
    51	0.4 s licence clock, and (c) the measured **persistence of the incumbent's own
    52	target** — how far the station point actually travels per second, and how long
    53	a body stays inside one station family. §3's instruments measure (c).
    54	
    55	### 1.2 The producers
    56	
    57	| producer | signature | what it is | code |
    58	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
    59	| `formationSpot` | `(p, team, ball, hasBall, opp?)` | the entry point; delegates to `emergentStation` whenever `emergentPosOn()` (**default ON**), else the legacy fixed tables | `formations.ts:129-136` |
    60	| `emergentStation` | same | **the incumbent any eye must beat.** Role depth/lane fractions + ball slide + `formationDepth` + `pressIntensity` step-up + `MODE_SHIFT` + rest-defence clamp + width multiplier + ball-side translate + opponent-line convergence ×0.14 + pairwise repulsion inside 9 m scaled `2.6·(1−0.7·threat)` + box relief + goal-ward collapse | `formations.ts:238-348` |
    61	| `supportSpot` | `(p, team, ball)` | ball-relative, **always AHEAD** (`aheadBias` 0.35 / 0.75), radius `10 + supportDistance·8`, lateral pull toward the player's own `formationSpot` lane capped at 0.9·radius | `formations.ts:546-561` |
    62	| `runTarget` | `(p, team, opponents)` | past the last defender's shoulder, `clamp(max(line+7, myX+5), myX+3, HALF_L−9)`, narrowing `y·0.6` (poacher: post channel ±3.5) | `formations.ts:490-504` |
    63	| mark stance | inline | goal-side ∧ ball-side blend, contain standoff, trap-bias pull back toward `formationSpot`, marker reaction lag via `markAnchor` | `actionExecutor.ts:174-273` |
    64	| the licensed branches | inline | corner crash spots + meet re-route, the arriver's 16 m arc, the overlap lane, and (dormant) C4 T2's cross meet point | `actionExecutor.ts:294-390` |
    65	
    66	### 1.3 The consumers, and when each reads
    67	
    68	| # | consumer | reads | when | cadence |
    69	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
    70	| 1 | `executeAction` `MoveToFormationSpot` / `HoldPosition` | `formationSpot` | the body is holding shape | **every tick** |
    71	| 2 | `executeAction` `SupportBallCarrier` | `supportSpot` (which itself calls `formationSpot`) | we have the ball, he is not the carrier | **every tick** |
    72	| 3 | `executeAction` `MakeRun` | `runTarget`, or a licensed branch | he is a runner / arriver / overlapper / crasher | **every tick** |
    73	| 4 | `executeAction` `MarkOpponent` | the mark stance, and `formationSpot` again for the trap-bias pull | he has a mark | **every tick** |
    74	| 5 | `executeAction`, post-switch | the **onside clamp** rewrites ANY of the above while a teammate carries | always | every tick |
    75	| 6 | `executeAction`, post-switch | the **barred-box clamp** rewrites any target during a goal kick / keeper hold | always | every tick |
    76	| 7 | `assignMarks` (TeamBrain) | `formationSpot(hasBall=false)` as each free defender's ZONE centre, zonal scheme only | zonal marking | **0.4 s** |
    77	| 8 | `shapeReady` | `formationSpot(hasBall=true)` for ≥3 settled outfielders | keeper distribution gate, goal-kick restart gate | on demand |
    78	| 9 | `Match.resetForKickoff` | `formationSpot` | kickoff placement | per kickoff |
    79	| 10 | `RenderStateAdapter` | `formationSpot` | the pre-match / debug shape overlay | per render frame |
    80	
    81	⭐ **Consumers 5–8 are the ones a naive replacement breaks.** The onside clamp
    82	(#5) silently caps every station beyond the offside line — an eye that prices
    83	stations beyond the line will find its choice rewritten rather than penalised,
    84	which is a *different* thing from revert 2's blast and must not be confused
    85	with it. The zonal zone centre (#7) means replacing `formationSpot` also
    86	**re-draws the marking lattice**, a second-order effect entirely outside the
    87	positioning seat. And `shapeReady` (#8) means the station function is a
    88	**restart gate**: a shape the eye never settles into stalls goal kicks.
    89	
    90	### 1.4 The one defect §3.3 named, confirmed
    91	
    92	`supportSpot` places every supporter at `ball.x + attackDir·radius·aheadBias`
    93	with `aheadBias ∈ {0.35, 0.75}` — both **positive**. Drop-to-receive is
    94	geometrically unreachable, exactly as the contract says. Note the coupling the
    95	contract did not state: `supportSpot` **calls `formationSpot` internally**
    96	(`formations.ts:554`) for its lateral lane, so it is a consumer of the
    97	incumbent as well as a sibling of it. Replacing the station changes support
    98	geometry whether or not P1 intends to.
    99	
   100	---
   101	
   102	## 2. The instruments — DEFINED before measurement
   103	
   104	Six, from §5 P0. Every one is a **distribution over sampled ticks**, clustered
   105	by match seed (#20), reported with CIs and never as a bare mean.
   106	
   107	Sampling: every tick would be 60 Hz × 6 bodies × 2 teams; the instruments are
   108	sampled every **10th tick (6 Hz)**, declared here rather than chosen later, and
   109	only while `phase === 'playing'`. Keepers are excluded from every body-based
   110	instrument (they have their own clamp and are not a positioning seat).
   111	
   112	```text
   113	I1  STATION-FAMILY DWELL      how long a body stays inside one station family
   114	I2  TARGET DRIFT              how far his station target moves, per second
   115	I3  PAIRWISE SPACING          distribution of outfield teammate-teammate distance
   116	I4  BALL CONVERGENCE          bodies within 5 m / 10 m of the ball, per side
   117	I5  REST-DEFENCE OCCUPANCY    own outfielders in our defensive third, in possession
   118	I6  DUPLICATE RUNS            two licensed runners whose targets are within 4 m
   119	I7  ATTACK/DEFENCE SHAPE      centroid depth, spreadX, spreadY, per face, and the delta
   120	```
   121	
   122	(I1 and I2 are the split of §5's single "station-switch rate" — see §2.1.)
   123	
   124	## 2.1 The *one number, two meanings* sweep (PROBE-CONTRACTS §2)
   125	
   126	Run over every instrument BEFORE any of them is measured, and it caught three:
   127	
   128	| instrument | the two meanings | ruling |
   129	| --- | --- | --- |
   130	| **station-switch rate** (§5's name) | (a) the body changed which station FAMILY owns him — a decision-level event on the 0.15 s clock; (b) his station POINT jumped — a geometry-level event that happens continuously at 60 Hz with no decision at all | ⛔ **SPLIT into I1 and I2.** These have different units, different clocks and different failure modes: an eye that flickers between families and an eye whose point jitters are separate diseases, and a single "switch rate" would report them as one. This is the E5a window defect exactly. |
   131	| **ball convergence** (乱抢) | (a) OUR bodies collapsing onto the ball — the shape failure the user hates; (b) BOTH teams' bodies near the ball — which also counts a legitimate contested duel, and rises when the football is *good* | ⛔ **SPLIT by side.** I4 reports own-side and opponent-side separately and never sums them. A pooled count would make a healthy 50/50 look like a scramble. |
   132	| **rest-defence occupancy** | (a) any own outfielder in our defensive third; (b) the DESIGNATED rest defender (index 1, the slot `emergentStation` clamps at `x ≤ −8 − coverBias·8`) being there | ⛔ **BOTH reported, never merged.** (a) can be satisfied by a beaten winger jogging home, which is the opposite of rest defence. (b) is the structural claim. |
   133	| pairwise spacing | one meaning (a distance distribution) — but a MEAN hides the failure | ✅ kept, reported as **p10 / median / p90 and the share under 4 m**: piling up is a left-tail event and a mean cannot see it. |
   134	| duplicate runs | (a) two bodies running to nearby TARGETS; (b) two bodies physically near each other while running | ✅ **(a) only**, stated: the disease is two bodies *aimed* at the same place. (b) is I3's job. |
   135	| shape delta | one meaning, but the FACE must be defined by possession, not by `team.mode` | ✅ kept, defined off `match.possessionSide` — `mode` is a hand table and would make the instrument circular with the thing Stage III wants to retire. |
   136	
   137	**Registered non-instrument**: no scalar "positioning score" is defined here or
   138	anywhere later (PROBE-CONTRACTS §3's no-single-VisionScore law).
   139	
   140	## 2.2 Exact definitions
   141	
   142	```text
   143	I1  For each off-ball outfielder, the station FAMILY is:
   144	      FORMATION (MoveToFormationSpot | HoldPosition)
   145	      SUPPORT   (SupportBallCarrier)
   146	      RUN       (MakeRun)
   147	      MARK      (MarkOpponent)
   148	      BALL      (ChaseBall | ReceivePass | InterceptPass)   -- not a station,
   149	                excluded from I1/I2 but counted so the denominator is honest
   150	    DWELL = the length in seconds of a maximal run of consecutive sampled
   151	    ticks with the same family, closed by a change or by the ball being won.
   152	    Reported: median, p90, and the per-minute family-change count.
   153	
   154	I2  DRIFT = |station target at this sample - station target at the previous
   155	    sample| / 0.1667 s, in m/s, for bodies who stayed in the same family
   156	    across the pair (a family change is I1's event, not a drift).
   157	    Reported: median, p90, and the share of samples above 4 m/s -- the speed a
   158	    body cannot actually track, so a target moving faster than that is a
   159	    target he is chasing rather than standing on.
   160	
   161	I3  All unordered pairs of own outfielders, both teams pooled by side.
   162	    Reported: p10, median, p90, share < 4 m.
   163	
   164	I4  Count of own outfielders within 5 m and within 10 m of the ball, and the
   165	    same for the opponent, reported SEPARATELY (never summed).
   166	
   167	I5  (a) own outfielders with localX < -HALF_L/3, while possessionSide is ours;
   168	    (b) the share of those ticks where the index-1 slot is one of them.
   169	
   170	I6  Among bodies whose family is RUN, the share of sampled ticks with at least
   171	    one pair of run targets within 4 m of each other.
   172	
   173	I7  Per side per tick: centroid localX, spreadX (sd), spreadY (sd) over own
   174	    outfielders, split by whether possession is ours. DELTA = the in-possession
   175	    value minus the out-of-possession value, per match, then pooled.
   176	```
   177	
   178	Every threshold above (4 m, 5 m, 10 m, 4 m/s, `HALF_L/3`) is a **reporting
   179	bucket**, not a gate. P2/P3 freeze gates against these measured distributions;
   180	none is frozen here, because a baseline that pre-commits to its own tolerance
   181	is the #19 error in advance.
   182	
   183	---
   184	
   185	## 3. Baselines
   186	
   187	Measured 2026-07-27, `scripts/probes/stage3-p0-instruments.ts`, read-only.
   188	**300 random-genome matches**, fresh block 930,000, **389,865 samples at
   189	6 Hz**, twice byte-identical, SHA `dc74fb02…813f`. Incumbent = `emergentStation`
   190	(default ON). Cluster unit = the match seed; CIs are 2,000-resample cluster
   191	bootstraps.
   192	
   193	Random genomes on purpose: this is the population the eye will actually live
   194	in, so the baselines carry the spread the P2/P3 gates will have to clear, not
   195	a neutral-genome point.
   196	
   197	### I1 — station-family dwell
   198	
   199	```text
   200	dwell       p10 0.167 s   median 0.667 s   p90 3.833 s   mean 1.466 s
   201	family changes   43.98 / body / minute   CI [43.26, 44.70]   = one per 1.36 s
   202	family share  MARK 32.11%  FORMATION 29.04%  BALL 19.35%
   203	              SUPPORT 9.06%  RUN 7.21%  ONBALL 2.37%  OTHER 0.86%
   204	```
   205	
   206	**Station families own 77.4% of outfield body-ticks**; the ball-directed
   207	actions own 19.4%. The median spell is **4.4× the 0.15 s action clock**, so the
   208	action clock is not what flips families — the choice is genuinely re-affirmed
   209	most ticks. But **p10 is one single sample**: a tenth of all station spells
   210	last ≤0.167 s. That flicker tail is the incumbent's, before any eye exists.
   211	
   212	### I2 — ⭐⭐⭐ target drift: the incumbent has no commitment, and a quarter of its motion is untrackable
   213	
   214	```text
   215	drift   p10 0.09   median 2.571   p90 6.244   mean 4.415   p99 54.11   m/s
   216	        share above 4 m/s (faster than a body can track):  27.35%
   217	```
   218	
   219	**More than a quarter of the time the station point is moving faster than the
   220	player chasing it**, and the p99 is a 9 m jump inside one 0.167 s sample. A
   221	structural cause is visible in the signature rather than inferred: `hasBall` is
   222	an *input* to `formationSpot`, so a possession flip re-evaluates the entire
   223	block in one tick — the incumbent's shape is a step function of possession,
   224	not a trajectory.
   225	
   226	This is the number §4-Q5's commitment window exists for, and it says the
   227	incumbent's implicit stability is an illusion produced by slow inputs, not by
   228	any commitment. **P1's W has an empirical anchor now**: the incumbent's own
   229	mean dwell is 1.47 s and its median is 0.67 s, bracketed by the 0.15 s action
   230	clock below and the 0.4 s licence clock in between.
   231	
   232	### I3 — pairwise spacing
   233	
   234	```text
   235	p10 4.188   median 12.955   p90 26.402   mean 14.402   m
   236	share under 4 m:  9.40%
   237	```
   238	
   239	The hand repulsion (9 m radius, `2.6·(1−0.7·threat)`) leaves about **one
   240	teammate pair in eleven inside 4 m**. That is the left tail a mean would hide,
   241	and it is the number an eye that prices crowding as a table row (§4-Q4) has to
   242	beat.
   243	
   244	### I4 — ball convergence, and the split paid for itself
   245	
   246	```text
   247	own within  5 m  0.956  CI [0.940, 0.973]      opp within  5 m  0.952  CI [0.937, 0.969]
   248	own within 10 m  2.204  CI [2.183, 2.227]      opp within 10 m  2.197  CI [2.175, 2.218]
   249	```
   250	
   251	⭐ **The two sides are indistinguishable.** Pooled, this instrument would have
   252	read *"1.9 bodies within 5 m of the ball"* and been filed as the 乱抢 residual;
   253	split, it says both teams commit **44% of their outfield inside 10 m** and
   254	neither is scrambling more than the other. Whatever E4 round 2 saw, it is not
   255	an asymmetry — which changes what P2/P3 can claim to have fixed. §2.1's sweep
   256	earned its keep here.
   257	
   258	### I5 — rest defence
   259	
   260	```text
   261	own outfielders in our defensive third, in possession   1.328  CI [1.288, 1.368]
   262	the DESIGNATED slot (index 1) is one of them            65.82% CI [64.42, 67.16]
   263	```
   264	
   265	The clamp at `x ≤ −8 − coverBias·8` exists to keep one specific body home, and
   266	**a third of the time he is not the body that is home**. Merging these two
   267	readings — as §2.1 refused to — would have reported "rest defence occupied
   268	1.33 bodies" and hidden that.
   269	
   270	### I6 — ⭐⭐ duplicate runs are the NORM
   271	
   272	```text
   273	share of multi-runner ticks with two run targets within 4 m:  54.71%  CI [52.96, 56.37]
   274	multi-runner ticks per match  276.3      licensed body-ticks excluded  120.9
   275	```
   276	
   277	**Over half.** And it is structural, not accidental: `runTarget` is
   278	`clamp(max(line + 7, myX + 5), myX + 3, HALF_L − 9)` with `y → y·0.6`, so two
   279	runners anywhere near each other are mapped to the same shoulder of the same
   280	line and then narrowed toward the same lane. The survey's "duplicate runs"

   838	/**
   839	 * The paired cluster bootstrap for a DIFFERENCE of two rates across arms.
   840	 * Clusters are match seeds; a drawn cluster contributes BOTH arms' rows, so
   841	 * the same worlds are compared however the resample falls.

   843	const pairedDifferenceCI = (
   844	  left: readonly CrossRow[], right: readonly CrossRow[],
   845	  hit: (row: CrossRow) => boolean, offset: number,
   846	) => {
   847	  const byCluster = new Map<number, { l: CrossRow[]; r: CrossRow[] }>();
   848	  const put = (row: CrossRow, side: 'l' | 'r') => {
   849	    const bucket = byCluster.get(row.cluster) ?? { l: [], r: [] };
   850	    bucket[side].push(row);
   851	    byCluster.set(row.cluster, bucket);
   852	  };
   853	  for (const row of left) put(row, 'l');
   854	  for (const row of right) put(row, 'r');
   855	  const clusters = [...byCluster.values()];
   856	  const rate = (rows: readonly CrossRow[]) =>
   857	    (rows.length === 0 ? Number.NaN : rows.filter(hit).length / rows.length);
   858	  const point = rate(right) - rate(left);
   859	  const rng = new Rng(BOOTSTRAP_SEED + offset);
   860	  const draws: number[] = [];
   861	  for (let draw = 0; draw < BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES; draw++) {
   862	    let lh = 0; let ln = 0; let rh = 0; let rn = 0;
   863	    for (let index = 0; index < clusters.length; index++) {
   864	      const pick = clusters[rng.int(0, clusters.length - 1)];
   865	      for (const row of pick.l) { ln += 1; if (hit(row)) lh += 1; }
   866	      for (const row of pick.r) { rn += 1; if (hit(row)) rh += 1; }
   867	    }
   868	    if (ln > 0 && rn > 0) draws.push(rh / rn - lh / ln);
   869	  }
   870	  draws.sort((a, b) => a - b);
   871	  const at = (q: number) => draws[Math.min(draws.length - 1,
   872	    Math.max(0, Math.floor(q * (draws.length - 1))))];
   873	  return {
   874	    point: round(point), lower: round(at(0.025)), upper: round(at(0.975)),
   875	  };
   876	};

    16	## 1. The six-layer acceptance chain
    17	
    18	Any new capability, attribute, or gene proves these **in sequence** — a failure at
    19	layer N means STOP, do not chase layer N+1:
    20	
    21	| # | Layer | The question | Evidence style |
    22	|---|---|---|---|
    23	| 1 | **Mechanism exists** | did the internal mechanism actually change? (obs-error moved, ETA sharper, first-touch faster, turn cost lower, trajectory error changed) | frozen-scene, **direct mediator** measurement |
    24	| 2 | **Gene bites correctly** | is the causal PATH right, not a shortcut? `awareness↑ → info fresher → prediction better`, **NOT** `awareness↑ → +10% tackle` | causal-path (mediator) test, not just directional |
    25	| 3 | **Capability appears** | does the world ALLOW the behaviour? (candidate generated, window exists, receiver reachable) | behaviour-possibility probe |
    26	| 4 | **It pays** | vs hold / neutral / alternative, does it improve the NEXT state? | **counterfactual** rollout (the layer we kept missing) |
    27	| 5 | **Evolution selects conditionally** | does **fresh** evo keep it in SOME ecologies, reject in others, at a real budget price? | multi-world fresh-evo + shadow-price |
    28	| 6 | **World remains healthy** | §2 watchability, readability, diversity, realism, ecology, perf, determinism | paired non-inferiority + ecological + replay clips |
    29	
    30	**The new default question** is no longer *"did behaviour X happen more?"* but
    31	*"why did it happen, what did it create, why did evolution keep it, and did it
    32	crowd out other football?"*
    33	
    34	---
    35	
    36	## 2. Six threshold TYPES (never mix them)
    37	
    38	Each gate belongs to exactly one type; state which when you write the contract.
    39	
    40	- **Exact invariant** — must hold to the bit: feature-off is bit-identical
    41	  (`fingerprint`), state ledger conserves, `watched === headless`, no illegal
    42	  states. *(vitest: `match.test`, `simRunner.test`, `rng.test`.)*
    43	  **Determinism hashes cover WORLD OUTCOMES only — wall-clock / perf numbers
    44	  are reported alongside, never hashed.** A probe cannot both hash wall-clock
    45	  and promise byte-identity; the two claims are different epistemic
    46	  categories. *(Registered from EDS E2b-1, 2026-07-25: a perf block inside
    47	  the hashed object made X3 structurally unpassable while the world itself
    48	  was proven deterministic.)*
    49	- **Directional** — only the sign is required: `awareness↑ → obs-error↓`,
    50	  `agility↑ → turn-ETA↓`. Side-balanced, enough seeds (ARCHITECTURE rule).
    51	- **Calibration** — predicted probability ≈ observed frequency: events predicted
    52	  "70% control" should land ≈70%. *(The whole point of `arrival-calibration`.)*
    53	- **Paired non-inferiority** — same-seed A/B: scramble/goals/route-mix must not
    54	  regress out of the agreed band. The verdict is *"not worse,"* not *"better."*
    55	- **Ecological** — multi-seed, multi-generation, **fresh** evo: divergence exists,
    56	  **no runaway** axis, payoff is frequency-dependent.
    57	  **Type your gate and OBEY the type**: an ecological claim gated on a single
    58	  seed is mis-typed and noise-dominated, whatever its threshold. *(Registered
    59	  from EDS E3R CE2, 2026-07-25: a one-seed style-entropy floor read 0.5797 —
    60	  FAIL — while the pre-registered robustness seed flipped the same statistic
    61	  to 1.5321 and all three mechanism discriminators said diversity ROSE.)*
    62	
    63	**Ruling #20 (2026-07-26, cross-AI audit adopted — verdict semantics and
    64	power discipline, binding on all NEW contracts):**
    65	
    66	- **CI verdict semantics replace point-threshold rules.** Equivalent /
    67	  non-inferior only if the ENTIRE confidence interval lies inside the
    68	  acceptance region; superior only if the lower bound clears the
    69	  threshold; REFUTED only if the upper bound lies below it; anything
    70	  else is verdict `INCONCLUSIVE` — never "refuted by a point estimate".
    71	- **Power calculations must declare the CLUSTER UNIT** (match / league
    72	  seed), not treat forks or moments as independent; report effective n.
    73	- **Every audit carries a family-wise fire budget**: the gate table sums
    74	  each gate's H0 fire probability; observed fires within budget are
    75	  triaged as noise-suspects (report + powered re-check), only an
    76	  over-budget audit stops the queue outright.
    77	- **Rare-event counters get Poisson-powered match budgets**: a ratio
    78	  gate on a counter with single-digit expected events cannot decide at
    79	  any tolerance — size the match count to the counter, or the gate is
    80	  mis-typed.
    81	- **The six watchability counters are HARD non-inferiority gates**
    82	  (flags-off paired) in every live-facing audit, with the user's eyes
    83	  as the final judge above them — "reported only" is retired (a
    84	  measured regression once passed 29 gates).
    85	- Ledger relabels under these semantics: E5c's HM "refuted" →
    86	  **INCONCLUSIVE** (+3.38pp, SE≈1.32, upper bound above the +4.0 band);
    87	  E3R2's CE1 waiver → **INCONCLUSIVE** (2/5 fresh seeds; multi-seed CE1
    88	  joins the pre-ship confirmatory audit).
    89	
    90	**Pattern-geometry premises are CENSUSED, never asserted (ruling #22,
    91	2026-07-26).** Where a pattern's forks land (which cells they occupy) and
    92	which comparison the pattern wins or loses are measurable census columns,
    93	not things to reason out from the pitch diagram. Two commander premises
    94	died by assertion: EDS #16.3 ("third-man runners arrive in the inner box"
    95	— measured 4.1%) and #21.3's labelled reading ("overlap lands
    96	attacking-wide and loses the argmax" — measured 55%/38% middle third, and
    97	the runner was already the top-priced option). A drafting premise about
    98	pattern geometry must cite a census row or be labelled UNTESTED and kept
    99	out of every gate derivation.
   100	
   101	**Inherited gate values must be RE-POWERED against the inheriting
   102	contract's own parameters (ruling #19, 2026-07-26).** A tolerance is only
   103	meaningful relative to the n it was powered at; inheriting the number
   104	without redoing the power calculation is an unpowered predicate in
   105	disguise. *(Registered from EDS E5d Phase 1 C3: a 5.0pp tolerance
   133	- **Equivalence / flatness** — the claim is *"no effect"* / *"no longer rises"*:
   134	  must be pre-registered as an INTERVAL test (an explicit equivalence band) with
   135	  a sample size computed against the predicted effect. A strict point inequality
   136	  where the per-arm SE swamps the predicted difference is structurally
   137	  undecidable — the gate can only ever return `unexplained`, whichever way the
   138	  world is. *(Registered from EDS E1a-I2, 2026-07-25: a 0.5pp endpoint gap was
   139	  coded as "rises" where the SE of that difference was ≈5.6pp at n≈60 — the
   140	  probe was honest, the predicate was unpowered by construction.)*
   141	
   142	**Power is a FREEZE-TIME obligation, and a pre-run disclosure does not
   143	discharge it (commander ruling #29.5, 2026-07-27).** A gate you can already
   144	see is under-powered must be **re-powered or re-derived ex ante, before the
   145	freeze** — writing down that it is weak is honesty about a defect, not a
   146	licence to run with it. A knowingly ~2σ gate buys a verdict that cannot
   147	distinguish its own two readings: *the world moved* and *my tolerance was too
   148	tight* both produce the same fire, and no amount of after-the-fact prose
   149	separates them. *(Registered from C5 T1's H1: the contract disclosed, in its
   150	own committed §7.2b before the run, that the realised base rate made a 2.0pp
   151	tolerance 2.1σ instead of ≈3σ — and then ran it. It fired at ≈3.1σ on one arm
   152	while the three arms the table existed to price reproduced at 1.56 / 0.06 /

   156	**A MAX-statistic over thousands of records at a tight tolerance is a
   157	COUPON-COLLECTOR gate and is FORBIDDEN (commander ruling #32.1,
   158	2026-07-27).** `max|x_i − y_i| ≤ ε` over n records does not ask the claim
   159	*"the arithmetic reached the world"*; it asks that **no single record
   160	anywhere** be pathological, and its fire probability grows with n for any
   161	fixed per-record tail. On a few thousand records it is a near-certain fire

   163	stage exists to prove. Write it instead as **per-record with NAMED

    93

   103	  waiting, and moving the origin to the release would hand the hold arms free

   294	release; and the **paired-vs-unpaired** estimator side by side, so the pairing
   295	premium is visible rather than claimed.
   296	
   297	### 8.3 The release-origin twin
   298	
   299	The same statistic with each hold arm's 240-tick window starting at RELEASE
   300	instead of at the decision moment. **Reported, never gated, and never
   301	substituted for the primary** — it answers "was the ball better when he finally
   302	played it", which is a different question from "was waiting worth it", and
   303	keeping both visible is what stops the second question being quietly answered
   304	with the first.

   361	### 11.1 The FAIL, and what it is actually made of
   362	
   363	**Only the act-now arm missed, and only on the marginal.** All three HOLD arms
   364	reproduce across disjoint blocks at 1.56 / 0.06 / 0.87pp, and every one of the
   365	twelve gated pressure rows is inside H2's 5.0pp. The act-now level moved
   366	31.35% → 28.36%, and the movement is concentrated in the top pressure band
   367	(31.71% → 27.72%, 4.0pp), which is also where two thirds of the moments live.
   368	
   369	This is the gate §7.2b flagged before the run as **2.1σ rather than ~3σ at the
   370	realised base rate**, and it fired at ≈3.1σ of the naive interval — i.e. right
   371	at the edge where a mis-sized tolerance and a real block difference are not
   372	distinguishable by this design. With the match seed as the cluster unit and
   373	**32 held-out clusters**, "how shot-heavy a match is" is a cluster-level
   374	property, and the marginal is the statistic most exposed to it; the per-row
   375	comparison at a tolerance that respects that passes everywhere.
   376	
   377	**I am not relaxing it.** §12 says H may not be relaxed after sight and the
   378	tolerances were inherited whole precisely so they could not be argued about
   379	later. The honest statement is the one recorded in advance: *if H1 fires, that
   380	is a gate I mis-sized, not a table that failed to reproduce* — and the evidence
   381	now says exactly that, because the arms the table exists to price all reproduce
   382	and the rows all reproduce. A re-powered T1R would size H1 off this run's own
   383	cluster variance and use more held-out clusters, not a looser number.
   384	
   385	### 11.2 ⭐⭐⭐ The exchange rate: reading (a), resolved, and monotone in k
   386	
   387	Paired per-moment difference (hold-k − act-now), 95% cluster bootstrap:
   388	
   389	| k | waiting's cost | 95% CI | concession twin | release-origin twin |
   390	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   391	| **30** (0.5 s) | **−7.55pp** | [−9.35, −5.73] | **+1.45pp** [0.73, 2.18] | −6.53pp [−8.47, −4.45] |
   392	| **60** (1.0 s) | **−12.77pp** | [−14.68, −10.95] | **+2.63pp** [1.82, 3.45] | −10.20pp [−12.13, −8.32] |
   393	| **90** (1.5 s) | **−16.12pp** | [−18.02, −14.28] | **+3.55pp** [2.68, 4.42] | −12.40pp [−14.50, −10.47] |
   394	
   395	Marginal shot rates: act-now **31.35%**, hold-30 23.80%, hold-60 18.58%,
   396	hold-90 15.23%.
   397	
   398	**In today's world, waiting is expensive at both ends and the cost grows with
   399	every tick held.** Half a second costs 7.6pp of shot probability and buys 1.5pp
   400	of extra concession; a second and a half costs 16.1pp and concedes 3.6pp. Every
   401	interval is far from zero — this is not the 1.6pp-resolution question §7.1
   402	worried about, it is an effect ten times the resolution.
   403	
   404	**§8.3's twin closes the obvious defence.** "He waited and then played a better
   405	ball" is measurable, and it is false: re-anchoring the window at the RELEASE
   406	still leaves waiting **−6.53 / −10.20 / −12.40pp**. The ball is not better when
   407	it finally goes; it is simply later. The twin is reported, never substituted —
   408	but the direction it points is the same one.
   409	
   410	**By pressure band** (k=90): free **−10.53pp**, mid **−18.87pp**, pressed
   411	**−16.77pp**. Waiting costs least when nobody is near you, which is coherent
   412	without anyone designing it in, and matches T0R's shape — the world only
   413	charges for time when there is someone to charge you.
   414	
   415	**Hold anatomy**: the forced hold survives its own window 84.8 / 76.7 / 68.8%
   416	of the time, losing to a tackle in 5.7 / 12.7 / 19.4%. The 68.8% at k=90 sits
   417	beside T0R's 70.2% on a different population and a different arm — close, and
   418	neither is a pin.
   419	
   420	### 11.3 What this does and does not say
   421	
   422	**Registered in advance and honoured now**: reading (a) is not a FAIL and not a
   423	refutation of C5. What it establishes is narrower and sharper —
   424	
   425	* **A T2 chooser priced from this table would essentially never hold.** That is
   426	  the single most consequential thing T1 hands forward, and it is a design fact
   427	  the commander needs before T2 is drafted, not after.
   428	* **Part of the cost is mechanical by construction, and that was the design.**
   429	  A held tick is a tick removed from the same 240-tick window, and §4 fixed the
   430	  horizon at the decision moment precisely so that time cost would be counted
   431	  rather than hidden. So the honest claim is *"on this axis, in this world, a
   432	  held tick is a spent tick and nothing currently pays it back"* — **not**
   433	  "patience has no value in football".
   434	* **Q2 anticipated this exact outcome**: *"if today's world pays little for
   435	  patience, the table says so honestly; road B enriches the world and
   436	  re-censuses (#26.5)."* The world that would pay for waiting — a maturing run
   437	  that is worth waiting for, a press that can be drawn and beaten, a receiver
   438	  repertoire — is the world road B is building. This table is the before.
   439	* **It is the fourth independent arrow at the same seat, pointing the other
   440	  way.** E4r1, the user's round-2 anchor, E5f/E5g and now T1 all agree that the
   441	  substrate does not currently reward waiting; the first three read it as a
   442	  missing capability, and T1 says the capability alone would not be selected.

   132	interface Moment {
   133	  readonly cluster: number;
   134	  readonly pressureBand: Band;
   135	  readonly staleBand: Band;
   136	  readonly support: number;
   137	  readonly arms: readonly ArmOutcome[]; // [A0, A1, A2, A3]

   139	
   140	/** Run one fork forward and read the axis off it. */
   141	const runArm = (
   142	  before: Match, ownerGid: number, holdTicks: number,
   143	): ArmOutcome => {
   144	  const fork = cloneSimulationState(before);
   145	  const owner = fork.allPlayers.find((p) => p.gid === ownerGid)!;
   146	  const side = owner.side;
   147	  const attacking = fork.teams[side];
   148	  const defending = fork.teams[1 - side];
   149	  const shotsBefore = attacking.stats.shots;
   150	  const concededBefore = defending.stats.shots;
   151	  const tacklesBefore = defending.stats.tackles;
   152	  const startTick = fork.simTick;
   153	  if (holdTicks > 0) fork.forcedHold = { gid: ownerGid, untilTick: startTick + holdTicks };
   154	
   155	  let shot = false;
   156	  let horizonReached = false;
   157	  let survivedHold: boolean | null = holdTicks > 0 ? true : null;
   158	  let lostDuringHold = false;
   159	  // The release-origin twin needs the window to keep running past the
   160	  // horizon, so hold arms are simulated for holdTicks + HORIZON.
   161	  const total = holdTicks + HORIZON;
   162	  let shotsAtRelease = -1;
   163	  for (let tick = 0; tick < total; tick++) {
   164	    if (fork.finished) break;
   165	    fork.step(DT);
   166	    const elapsed = fork.simTick - startTick;
   167	    if (holdTicks > 0 && elapsed === holdTicks) {
   168	      shotsAtRelease = attacking.stats.shots;
   169	      if (fork.ball.owner?.gid !== ownerGid) {
   170	        survivedHold = false;
   171	        lostDuringHold = true;
   172	      }
   173	    }
   174	    if (holdTicks > 0 && elapsed <= holdTicks && fork.ball.owner?.gid !== ownerGid) {
   175	      lostDuringHold = true;
   176	    }
   177	    if (elapsed === HORIZON) {
   178	      // Read the axis AT the horizon and never again: a hold arm keeps
   179	      // simulating for the release twin, and letting a post-horizon shot flip
   180	      // this flag would silently give the hold arms a longer window than
   181	      // act-now. The smoke found that in the first draft.
   182	      shot = attacking.stats.shots > shotsBefore;
   183	      horizonReached = true;
   184	      if (holdTicks === 0) break;
   185	    }
   186	  }
   187	  // A window the match ended inside reads at whatever it reached.
   188	  if (!horizonReached) shot = attacking.stats.shots > shotsBefore;
   189	  const conceded = defending.stats.shots > concededBefore;
   190	  return {
   191	    shot,
   192	    conceded,
   193	    survivedHold: holdTicks > 0 ? survivedHold && !lostDuringHold : null,
   194	    lostToTackle: holdTicks > 0
   195	      ? lostDuringHold && defending.stats.tackles > tacklesBefore : null,
   196	    shotFromRelease: holdTicks > 0 && shotsAtRelease >= 0
   197	      ? attacking.stats.shots > shotsAtRelease : null,
   198	    signature: stateSignature(fork),
   199	  };
   200	};

   203	 * Walk a seed block, and at every qualifying decision moment fork the world
   204	 * four ways off the SAME pre-step state — paired by construction.
   205	 */
   206	const harvest = (seedStart: number, budget: number) => {
   207	  const moments: Moment[] = [];
   208	  let matches = 0;
   209	  let inertPins: { seed: number; identical: boolean }[] = [];
   210	  for (
   300	  return { low: sorted[third] ?? 0, high: sorted[sorted.length - third] ?? 0 };
   301	};
   302	const supportBandOf = (
   303	  value: number, cuts: { low: number; high: number },
   304	): Band => (value < cuts.low ? 0 : value >= cuts.high ? 2 : 1);
   305	
   306	const ARM_NAMES = ['actNow', 'hold30', 'hold60', 'hold90'] as const;
   307	
   308	/** The census table: shot rate per arm per cell, with the frozen ladder. */
   309	const buildTable = (moments: readonly Moment[], cuts: { low: number; high: number }) => {
   310	  const key = (m: Moment) => `${m.pressureBand}|${m.staleBand}|${supportBandOf(m.support, cuts)}`;
   311	  const cells = new Map<string, Moment[]>();
   312	  for (const m of moments) {
   313	    const bucket = cells.get(key(m));
   314	    if (bucket === undefined) cells.set(key(m), [m]); else bucket.push(m);
   315	  }
   316	  const rateOf = (rows: readonly Moment[], arm: number) => (rows.length === 0 ? Number.NaN
   317	    : rows.filter((m) => m.arms[arm].shot).length / rows.length);
   318	  const rowsFor = (predicate: (m: Moment) => boolean) => moments.filter(predicate);
   319	
   320	  const cellRows = [...cells.entries()].sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : 1)).map(([k, rows]) => {
   321	    const [p, s, sup] = k.split('|').map(Number);
   322	    // Frozen ladder: (p × s × sup) → (p × s) → p → marginal.
   323	    const ladder = rows.length >= BUCKET_FLOOR ? 'cell'
   324	      : rowsFor((m) => m.pressureBand === p && m.staleBand === s).length >= BUCKET_FLOOR
   325	        ? 'pressureStale'
   326	        : rowsFor((m) => m.pressureBand === p).length >= BUCKET_FLOOR ? 'pressure' : 'marginal';
   327	    return {
   328	      pressureBand: p, staleBand: s, supportBand: sup, n: rows.length, ladder,
   329	      rates: Object.fromEntries(ARM_NAMES.map((name, arm) => [name, round(rateOf(rows, arm))])),
   330	    };
   331	  });
   332	
   333	  const pressureRows = ([0, 1, 2] as Band[]).map((p) => {
   334	    const rows = rowsFor((m) => m.pressureBand === p);
   335	    return {
   336	      pressureBand: p, n: rows.length,
   337	      rates: Object.fromEntries(ARM_NAMES.map((name, arm) => [name, round(rateOf(rows, arm))])),
   338	    };
   339	  });
   340	
   341	  return {
   342	    cells: cellRows,
   343	    pressureRows,
   344	    marginal: {
   345	      n: moments.length,
   346	      rates: Object.fromEntries(
   347	        ARM_NAMES.map((name, arm) => [name, round(rateOf(moments, arm))]),
   348	      ) as Record<typeof ARM_NAMES[number], number>,
   349	    },
   350	  };
   351	};

   121	## 4. Design invariants — the Phase-0 map's six questions, ruled
   122	
   123	* **Q1 — Hold is a CANDIDATE, never a modifier.** The measured gap IS the
   124	  missing option; a modifier hides the choice from measurement and from
   125	  selection, and a candidate is an observable external state — opponents
   126	  see shielding, never intention (the 内心/外显/推断 model holds).
   127	* **Q2 — the WORLD pays for waiting; the census prices it.** No
   128	  forward-looking bonus term is invented anywhere. Waiting's real
   129	  benefits (runs maturing, pressure drawn, percepts refreshing under
   130	  pull semantics) flow through the NEXT decision's genuinely better
   131	  menu; the census measures the net exchange rate on the same outcome
   132	  axis the pass prices use — the E2b-0 move applied to time. If today's
   133	  world pays little for patience, the table says so honestly; road B
   134	  enriches the world and re-censuses (#26.5).
   135	* **Q3 — stagnation stays legacy-only.** In the measured seat, time's
   136	  price comes from the census (staleTime is a census feature, so any
   137	  real decay is IN the table); the hand-penalty is neither copied into
   138	  the value seat nor removed from the legacy one.
   139	* **Q4 — a NEW generalized Hold; legacy HoldUp untouched.** Shield-hold
   140	  is the v1 action. "Look around" is not a separate action in v1 —
   141	  that is seat 2's future consumer. The `layingOff` synergy (`281/326`)
   142	  is a named natural consumer, later.
   143	* **Q5 — C7 shares the contract, not the stages** (§2 above).
   144	* **Q6 — NO FREE TIME (I1, the hard invariant).** Every held tick must
   145	  be attackable: pressure closes, poke/tackle windows open against the
   146	  shield (priced by both sides' attrs), stamina drains. A Hold that
   147	  cannot be lost is the ×1.3 subsidy in a new costume (E5h) and C1-A2's
   148	  free option. T3 carries an explicit pre-registered hold-dominance
   149	  ceiling; a world where holding never loses the ball stops the queue.

   129	## 4. Design invariants — the survey's five questions + the house's three, ruled
   130	
   131	* **Q1 — the state is the player's OWN percept, priced by class.** The
   132	  eye consumes the pulled snapshot, never truth. A candidate whose
   133	  context depends on unseen bodies prices at the census MARGINAL for the
   134	  perceived features (the E2b-1 ladder: READ full-featured, within
   135	  retention BANDED, UNSEEN marginal); no truth-fallback by the back door
   136	  (#8(l)). The census itself is fitted on TRUE context (the world's
   137	  honest exchange rates) and consumed through perceived context — the
   138	  same architecture E2b-1R proved live, so the fidelity question is
   139	  already answered in this repo, not reopened.
   140	* **Q2 — the census cell is a TARGET-CHOICE intervention.** Fork at real
   141	  off-ball moments, force the station target for a frozen window W, live
   142	  machinery does movement/decisions/physics both teams; outcome =
   143	  what happened within horizon H from the force, both faces, every
   144	  window simulated (E5d). The harness gate: forcing the incumbent's own
   145	  target reproduces the unforked match bit-identically. W and H are
   146	  pre-registered per stage, and the P1 contract must state ex ante what
   147	  a station can and cannot causally reach at its horizon (a station is
   148	  slower machinery than a pass — H_station > H_pass is expected, its
   149	  value derived from P0's measured decision cadences, not invented).
   150	* **Q3 — the preference seat opens HERE, and only here.** The chooser's
   151	  preference-seat fork stayed closed (#13.2, CE2R) because a measured
   152	  probability needs no taste. A tactical STANCE is not a probability:
   153	  how to trade the score face against the concede face IS style, and
   154	  VISION mandates it evolves. So: **component VALUES are census-measured,
   155	  component WEIGHTS are genes** — the two-engines junction, cashed as
   156	  designed. Guard rails: exactly TWO measured faces in v1 (score,
   157	  concede — one signed axis split, so nothing double-counts); weights
   158	  map from EXISTING tactical genes (§4-Q6); no hand constant anywhere in
   159	  the composition; and the E5d anti-composition law binds WITHIN a face
   160	  (never P̂×V̂ where EV̂ is measurable).
   161	* **Q4 — crowding is a FEATURE, not a rule.** Don't-crowd must emerge
   162	  from a measured fact: local teammate density enters the census feature
   163	  set, so "a third body in an occupied zone adds little" is a TABLE ROW,
   164	  not a repulsion constant. The incumbent's hand repulsion stays only in
   165	  the legacy path. Same treatment for the offside structure: the
   166	  perceived offside line is field geometry the eye reads (VISION input
   167	  ④), stations beyond it price at their measured (poor) face values —
   168	  and revert 2's +50% blast becomes a hard canary, not a hand clamp.
   169	* **Q5 — stability is gated, not assumed.** The survey's sharpest
   170	  warning (a correct field can still oscillate, pile up, duplicate runs,
   171	  abandon rest defence under simultaneous consumption) is the incumbent's
   172	  hand-tuning in disguise. v1's answer: station decisions run at the
   173	  measured station cadence with COMMITMENT (a chosen station persists
   174	  its window unless the percept materially changes — the banked
   175	  short-lived-commitment substrate, AUTHORITY §2, finally consumed), and
   176	  P2/P3 carry pre-registered stability instruments: station-switch rate,
   177	  pairwise-spacing distribution, ball-convergence index, rest-defence
   178	  occupancy, duplicate-run rate — gated against the incumbent's own
   179	  measured bands.
   180	* **Q6 — no new genes in v1.** Weights map from the EXISTING tactical
   181	  genome (attackingWidth, formationDepth, defensiveCompactness,
   182	  pressIntensity, supportDistance, coverBias — the P1 contract freezes
   183	  the mapping ex ante); serialized keys keep meaning, the budget law is
   184	  untouched, evolved populations stay comparable. Dedicated
   185	  preference genes (risk appetite as its own axis) are a named FOLLOW-UP
   186	  with their own budget-law step — after the eye proves the seat.
   187	* **Q7 — intent privacy holds.** The cooperation reading (队友协同 —
   188	  "winger wide and high = a cross is coming") consumes EXTERNAL evidence
   189	  through the percept only: positions, velocities, ball flight,
   190	  observable wind-ups (C7's future output). No teammate's private
   191	  intent, no coach-truth broadcast, no commander (D-ROTATE's grave).
   192	  Familiarity/doctrine as PRIORS on interpretation stay A4's seat,
   193	  explicitly not smuggled in here.
   194	* **Q8 — symmetry by construction.** Every outfielder on BOTH teams runs
   195	  the same eye over his own percept (the S3b/vision-attr law is built
   196	  in, not bolted on). The two faces make the same machinery the
   197	  attacking eye in possession and the defensive eye out of it — and the
   198	  **shape DIFFERENCE between the faces is an acceptance instrument**
   199	  (VISION 2026-07-27 anchor), measured, not asserted.

   245	## 5.5 The arrival hypothesis, reality-calibrated (commander amendment,
   246	2026-07-27, user-ratified — supersedes the "price the landing" framing)
   247	
   248	Real box attack happens BEFORE the kick, and C4's own chain measured the
   249	same thing (T2: presence without pre-aim moved nothing; the corner
   250	machinery works because it stages pre-kick). The P5+/C4-handshake
   251	hypothesis is therefore posed as:

   253	* **Evidence read, pre-kick**: the eye reads observable carrier context
   254	  (teammate wide + high + body set to deliver — external evidence only,
   255	  intent privacy holds) and prices the box ZONES ahead of the kick. The
   256	  last-half-second landing re-route is already banked dormant (C4) and
   257	  is the correction, never the mechanism.
   258	* **Division of labour EMERGES**: near/far/spot splits are never
   259	  hand-assigned — they fall out of don't-crowd (an occupied zone prices
   260	  lower in the next man's eye) plus per-player gene/attr differences.
   261	  A4's doctrine, when it opens, sharpens the split as a shared PRIOR
   262	  (latency/coordination), never revealing hidden truth.
   263	* **Timing comes from reading the crosser, not from wanting the space**
   264	  — revert 2's +50% offsides was value without the evidence read; the

   266	* **Wasted runs are the honest price**: evidence-driven anticipation
   267	  is sometimes wrong (the cross never comes; the run recycles).
   268	  Acceptance instruments must not penalize recycled runs as waste —

   284	## 7. Stop rules
   285	
   286	Any stage FAIL → the queue stops, the fork returns to the commander; no
   287	stage rescues a neighbour by tuning. The offside canary or the
   288	box-occupancy canary firing stops the queue outright (the two reverts'
   289	graves are load-bearing). A DEGENERATE ATTRACTOR (a station family the
   290	eye never leaves, or a collapse of the spacing distribution — the
   291	positional twin of always-heavy) is a hard stop with its own
   292	pre-registered form at P2/P3. Perf misses → report, no honesty shaving,
   293	no budget raise. Population law (#26.5): any live substrate change (C5,
   294	C4, C6) invalidates P1's tables — the SHIPPING table must be censused at
   295	the substrate HEAD it deploys on; an early P1 run on the incumbent world
   296	is design calibration only and must say so on its face.

   456	function assignMarks(team: Team, match: Match): void {
   457	  team.marks.clear();
   458	  if (match.possessionSide === team.side) return;
   459	
   460	  const zonal = team.style.scheme === 'zonal';
   461	  const opp = match.teams[1 - team.side];
   462	  const carrier = match.ball.owner;
   463	  // Sort by how deep they are in OUR half: smaller localX for them = deeper
   464	  // for us. (A numerically identical pre-sort used to run first; this
   465	  // comparator is a total order — index tiebreak — so one sort decides fully.)
   466	  // The restart taker is not a threat (Phase 29.1): they're pinned to a dead
   467	  // ball the clearance circle already guards, and the assigned chaser blocks
   468	  // the short option — a marker sent there too made TWO men stand uselessly
   469	  // at the corner flag while the box went a body short.
   470	  const takerGid = match.restart?.takerGid;
   471	  const inOurBox = (x: number, y: number): boolean =>
   472	    team.localX(x) < -HALF_L + BOX_DEPTH && Math.abs(y) < BOX_WIDTH / 2;
   473	  const threats = opp.players
   474	    .filter((o) => o.role !== 'GK' && o !== carrier && !o.sentOff && o.gid !== takerGid)
   475	    .sort((a, b) => opp.localX(b.pos.x) - opp.localX(a.pos.x) || a.index - b.index);
   476	
   477	  const free = team.players.filter((p) => p.role !== 'GK' && !team.chasers.has(p.index) && !p.sentOff);
   478	  // Zonal: each free defender's zone is centered on their DEFENDING spot.
   479	  const zones = zonal ? new Map(free.map((p) => [p.index, formationSpot(p, team, match.ball, false, match.teams[1 - team.side])])) : null;
   480	  const used = new Set<number>();
   481	  for (const threat of threats) {
   482	    const boxThreat = inOurBox(threat.pos.x, threat.pos.y);
   483	    let best: { idx: number; d: number } | null = null;
   484	    for (const p of free) {
   485	      if (used.has(p.index)) continue;
   486	      // Width discipline (Phase 28.4): a WIDE winger does not abandon the
   487	      // flank to join a central pile-up — central threats belong to the
   488	      // spine. This is the user-diagnosed collapse: turnover in midfield →
   489	      // wingers tuck in → six bodies in one corridor → playground scramble.
   490	      if (p.role === 'WG' && Math.abs(p.pos.y) > 12 && Math.abs(threat.pos.y) < 8) continue;
   491	      // Zonal: outside our box, only the defender whose ZONE the threat
   492	      // entered may engage — everyone else keeps the lattice.
   493	      if (zones && !boxThreat && dist(zones.get(p.index)!, threat.pos) > 9) continue;
   494	      const d = dist(p.pos, threat.pos);
   495	      if (d < 22 && (best === null || d < best.d)) best = { idx: p.index, d };
   496	    }
   497	    if (best) {
   498	      used.add(best.idx);
   499	      team.marks.set(best.idx, threat.index);
   500	    }
   501	  }
   502	}
   284	## 7. Stop rules
   285	
   286	Any stage FAIL → the queue stops, the fork returns to the commander; no
   287	stage rescues a neighbour by tuning. The offside canary or the
   288	box-occupancy canary firing stops the queue outright (the two reverts'
   289	graves are load-bearing). A DEGENERATE ATTRACTOR (a station family the
   290	eye never leaves, or a collapse of the spacing distribution — the
   291	positional twin of always-heavy) is a hard stop with its own
   292	pre-registered form at P2/P3. Perf misses → report, no honesty shaving,
   293	no budget raise. Population law (#26.5): any live substrate change (C5,
   294	C4, C6) invalidates P1's tables — the SHIPPING table must be censused at
   295	the substrate HEAD it deploys on; an early P1 run on the incumbent world
   296	is design calibration only and must say so on its face.
   297

   299	
   300	The road-B dependency order stands: **C5 → C4 → re-measure → joint value
   301	only on the residual** (#26.3), with Stage III's contract now in
   302	existence alongside C5's. The commander's recommendation for the slot —
   303	**RATIFIED by the user 2026-07-27, binding as written**:
   304	
   305	* **P0 is gap work** — read-only, zero src, executor-runnable in a C5/C4
   306	  queue gap exactly like C4 T0 (it competes only for session time, not

   308	* **P1–P4 queue BEHIND C4's T3** on the population law: C5 and C4 both
   309	  intend live landings; censusing the station tables before the world
   310	  they deploy into exists would guarantee a re-census. If C5/C4 stall at

   312	* The eye's design does NOT block on C5/C4 results — this contract is

    25	## 2. The mechanism, derived from the code before any data (#30.3)
    26	
    27	### 2.1 The arithmetic
    28	
    29	`performCross` (`mechanics.ts:552-595`) delegates the flight to
    30	`loftKick(match, crosser, spot, 0.5, 0.038, 0.7, 1.7, 1.1, spin)`
    31	(`mechanics.ts:512-544`), which computes
    32	
    33	```text
    34	T  = clamp(tBase + dEff·tPerM, tMin, tMax)   = clamp(0.5 + dEff·0.038, 0.7, 1.7)
    35	kickBall(..., speed = dEff / T, loft = GRAVITY·T/2)
    36	```
    37	
    38	That is a plain ballistic launch: apex at `T/2`, and
    39	
    40	```text
    41	peak = vz² / 2g = (gT/2)² / 2g = g·T² / 8 = 1.22625 · T²      (GRAVITY 9.81, constants.ts:176)
    42	```
    43	
    44	Setting `peak ≥ HEADER_MIN_HEIGHT` (1.35 m, `constants.ts:186`):
    45	
    46	```text
    47	T    ≥ √(8 · 1.35 / 9.81)      = 1.04925 s
    48	dEff ≥ (1.04925 − 0.5) / 0.038 = 14.454 m
    49	```
    50	
    51	⭐ **A cross whose effective range is under ~14.5 m cannot reach header height.
    52	That is arithmetic, not tuning.** At the current `tMin` of 0.7 s the apex is
    53	**0.601 m**; at `tMax` 1.7 s it is 3.544 m.
    54	
    55	### 2.2 The prediction this makes about T0b's own numbers
    56	
    57	Inverting `peak = 1.22625·T²` on the measured medians, **registered here as an
    58	ex-ante prediction the run will check**:
    59	
    60	```text
    61	H0 (peak 1.00–1.06 m)  ⇒ T ≈ 0.903–0.930 s ⇒ dEff ≈ 10.6–11.3 m
    62	BAL crosses (2.19–2.26) ⇒ T ≈ 1.337–1.358 s ⇒ dEff ≈ 22.0–22.6 m
    63	```
    64	
    65	⭐⭐ **If that holds, the archetype gap is a DISTANCE gap, not a flight-law
    66	gap**: CROSS-archetype deliveries (60–62% headable) are struck from ~11 m and
    67	BAL's (76–84%) from ~22 m, through one shared law. The flight curve is not
    68	broken; it is *a function of distance only*, and a short cross therefore cannot
    69	be lofted. **F3 measures this and it is REPORTED, not gated** — if it holds it
    70	is a finding the commander needs, because it says the cross TRIGGER's distance
    71	is a second seat that neither the aim nor the flight owns.
    72	
    73	### 2.3 The intervention
    74	
    75	**Flag `c4Flight` (`MatchConfig`, default `EDS_BUNDLE_ARMED` = false).** In
    76	`performCross` **only** — no other `loftKick` caller is touched — the flight
    77	time gains a floor at the apex that clears the band:
    78	
    79	```text
    80	T_HEAD = √(8 · HEADER_MIN_HEIGHT / GRAVITY)     // 1.04925 s, DERIVED
    81	tMin:  0.7  →  T_HEAD          (crosses only, flag on)
    82	```
    83	
    84	**One derived constant and no free parameter.** The value is not chosen; it is
    85	the solution of `peak(T) = HEADER_MIN_HEIGHT`, and it is written in the code as
    86	that expression, not as a literal.
    87	
    88	Everything the change carries with it is automatic, and is **reported, never
    89	tuned**:
    90	
    91	* **horizontal speed falls** to `dEff/T` on short crosses (a 10 m delivery:
    92	  11.4 → 9.5 m/s);
    93	* **hang time rises** (10 m: 0.88 → 1.049 s) — and that gives the DEFENCE the
    94	  same extra time it gives the attack. An honest symmetric cost, not a
    95	  subsidy;
    96	* **the Magnus pre-compensation** `−spin·T/2` scales with T, so the closed-form
    97	  landing invariance the comment at `mechanics.ts:539-542` describes still
    98	  holds.
    99	
   100	**Why technique does not scale the floor.** Getting a cross airborne is not the
   101	hard part of crossing; putting it in the right place is — and that half is
   102	*already* technique-priced through `loftKick`'s existing noise and range-error
   103	channels (`1.3 − passing·0.55`, `1.25 − passing·0.5`, `orientationNoiseMul`,
   104	`orientationPowerMul`). Adding a second technique term to the capability would
   105	price the same attribute twice, which is exactly the double-pay hazard #28.5
   106	registered for `attacking = 0.3`.
   107	
   108	### 2.4 ⚠️ The one interpretive call, surfaced for the commander to reverse
   109	
   110	`performCross` leads the target's run by `target.vel × flight0 ×
   111	CROSS_LEAD_FRAC` where `flight0 = clamp(0.5 + d·0.038, 0.7, 1.7)` — **the same
   112	law**, used as the crosser's estimate of his own flight time. So "aim
   113	untouched" has two readings:
   114	
   115	* **literal** — leave `flight0` alone. The aim NUMBER is unchanged, and the aim
   116	  RULE ("lead the run by a meetable fraction of the flight") silently becomes
   117	  wrong: on short crosses the true flight is now longer than the estimate, so
   118	  every running target is systematically under-led.
   119	* **rule-preserving** — `flight0` takes the same floor. The aim number moves,
   120	  by at most `CROSS_LEAD_MAX` 3.5 m and only for moving targets, and the rule
   130	measured rather than argued, and **this is flagged as the single place I
   131	interpreted the ruling** — the commander can reverse it before the run at no
   132	cost.

   374	### 7.1 The FAIL is my gate, again, and I am not re-scoping it
   375	
   376	F2 is a **max over 5,547 records with a 1e-3 tolerance**. It fired on exactly
   377	one delivery, whose measured peak (2.661 m) is 1.02 m ABOVE the apex its launch
   378	capture implies (1.639 m) — the ball rose higher than the kick that was
   379	recorded. Diagnosed read-only: it is a delivery **re-struck by the same player
   380	inside its own window**, so `lastTouch` never changes, the `maxZ` guard never
   381	trips, and the capture's apex and the observed peak describe two different
   382	kicks. Its class is `C3def`, `band = 40`, no touch registered.
   383	
   384	**A max-statistic over thousands of records at a tight tolerance is a
   385	coupon-collector gate** — it asks that no single record anywhere be
   386	pathological, which is a different claim from "the arithmetic reached the
   387	world". That is a gate-design defect I own, and it is the **second time in this
   388	stage** my own instrument has fired rather than the world (the first, F1/F2's
   389	sampling forms, was caught before the run; this one was not).

    29	## 2. The mechanism, derived from the code before any data (#30.3)
    30	
    31	### 2.1 ⚠️ One of the three authorized components is ALREADY IN THE ENGINE
    32	
    33	The contract's §2 describes the post-kick landing re-route as something to
    34	build. **It exists in open play, and has since Phase 63** —
    35	`actionExecutor.ts:159–166`:
    36	
    37	```ts
    38	if (p.action.type === 'ReceivePass' && ball.owner === null && ball.z > CONTROL_MAX_HEIGHT) {
    39	  const { x: lx, y: ly } = ballLanding(ball);
    40	  const vl = Math.hypot(ball.vel.x, ball.vel.y) || 1;
    41	  target = { x: lx - (ball.vel.x / vl) * 2.5, y: ly - (ball.vel.y / vl) * 2.5 };
    42	}
    43	```
    44	
    45	Its own comment says it is *"the 31.9 corner principle in open play"*:
    46	attack the DESCENT 2.5 m upstream, not the drop. `ballLanding`
    47	(`perception.ts:97–112`) is the one shared projector, Magnus-corrected and
    48	exact.
    49	
    50	**So the re-route is not missing. It is granted to exactly one body — the
    51	registered pass target** (`registerPass` → `match.pendingPass` → the
    52	`ReceivePass` candidate at `PlayerBrain.ts:1105–1107`, live for 3.5 s,
    53	longer than any cross flight). This re-shapes T2's mechanism from *"add a
    54	re-route"* to *"widen who is eligible for the one that already works"* —
    55	still Q2's safe half, still post-kick, still observable physics. **Flagged
    56	as a correction to the contract's own premise; the commander can reverse
    57	the framing before the run at no cost.**
    58	
    59	### 2.2 ⭐⭐⭐ And the real defect is that the box EMPTIES during the flight
    60	
    61	`PlayerBrain.ts:1144`, the gate on every licensed attacking run:
    62	
    63	```ts
    64	if ((team.runners.has(p.index) || arriving) &&
    65	    (carrier ? carrier !== p : match.phase === 'restart' || crashLive)) {
    66	```
    67	
    68	Read the false branch. The instant a cross leaves the boot in open play,
    69	`ball.owner === null`, `match.phase === 'playing'`, and `crashLive` is
    70	false (`team.cornerCrash` is set for corners only, `Match.ts:2208–2214`).
    71	**Every runner and the arriver lose their `MakeRun` candidate.**
    72	`SupportBallCarrier` also requires a carrier (`1128`), so what is left is
    73	`MoveToFormationSpot` (`1172–1176`). With a decision cadence of ~0.3–0.5 s
    74	inside a ~1.1 s flight, most of them re-decide once or twice mid-air.
    75	
    76	Upstream, the license itself dies too: `assignRunners` clears
    77	`team.arriver = null` every tick (`TeamBrain.ts:113–114`) and re-sets it
    78	only while the ball is *in the wide attacking channel*
    79	(`ballLocalX > HALF_L − 21 && |ballPos.y| > 10`, `211`) — which a ball
    80	flying into the box has left.
    81	
    82	**This is Phase 31.9's bug, still present in open play.** The engine has
    83	already been patched for it twice, in the same shape, with the reasons
    84	in-comment: `team.cornerCrash` for corners (*"the licenses died HERE and
    85	the crashers turned back toward their formation spots before the ball was
    86	struck"*) and the overlap license at `TeamBrain.ts:114–117` (*"the kick
    87	clears `ball.owner`, and a license torn up at that instant strands the
    88	runner — and the arriving ball — mid-flight"*).
    89	
    90	And it explains H3 exactly: the ball needs ~1.1 s to reach the header
    91	band, and for most of that second every attacking body except the
    92	registered target is running **away from the box**.
    93	
    94	### 2.3 The intervention, therefore: the open-play analogue of `cornerCrash`
    95	
    96	Two nested flags, both default OFF, crosses only:
    97	
    98	**`c4Arrival` — the license survives the delivery.** `performCross` snapshots
    99	the already-licensed bodies (`team.runners` + `team.arriver`, exactly as
   100	`Match.ts:2210–2213` snapshots them at the corner hand-off) into a
   101	`team.crossFlight` record, and `PlayerBrain.ts:1144`'s `crashLive` clause is
   102	generalized to accept it. **No new license, no new count, no new scorer** —
   103	whoever the engine had already sent forward simply does not turn around
   104	mid-air.
   105	
   106	*Duration, derived not chosen*: `until = simTime + ballLanding(ball).t` read
   107	at the kick — the license lasts exactly the flight and not a tick longer.
   108	(The corner's 2.8 s carries hand-off slack open play does not have.)
   109	It also ends early the moment the ball is owned again.
   110	
   111	*Scope, derived*: armed only when `team.cornerCrash === null`, so a corner
   112	delivery keeps its own machinery and can never be double-licensed.
   113	
   114	**`c4ArrivalReroute` — the closest licensed body gets the re-route that
   115	already works.** While the license is live and the ball is above
   116	`CONTROL_MAX_HEIGHT`, the licensed body closest to `ballLanding` targets the
   117	meet point `landing − flightDir·2.5` — the **same formula** as
   118	`actionExecutor.ts:164–166` and as the corner branch at `320`/`344`. The
   119	others keep their existing routing untouched, exactly as the corner branch
   120	leaves its non-closest crashers on their structure spots for the knockdown.
   121	
   122	Nesting is forced: without the license there is no `MakeRun` to re-route, so
   123	the ladder OFF → license → license+re-route is the only decomposition
   124	available, and it is the one the arms below run.
   125	
   126	### 2.4 What this deliberately does NOT do
   127	
   128	* **Nothing pre-kick.** The arriver keeps the 16 m arc until the ball is
   129	  struck. That is Q2's forbidden half (it needs the delivery moment, which
   130	  open play knows only through evidence or doctrine), it is what revert 2
   131	  broke, and the arc is a *measured* channel in its own right
   132	  (`cutback-anatomy`: 20% → shot).
   133	* **Therefore the offside exposure is structurally bounded**, not merely
   134	  gated: the flag is judged at the kick (`offsideAtKick`, `mechanics.ts:234`)
   135	  and every body this stage moves starts moving *after* it. Revert 2's blast
   136	  came from bodies crashing *before* the delivery. The canary in §4.6 is
   137	  still HARD — structure is an argument, and the discipline gates arguments.
   138	* **No new bodies in the box.** If the answer turns out to be *more*
   139	  crashers, that is a licensing change and its own stage.
   140	
   141	### 2.5 ⚠️ The one interpretive call, surfaced for the commander to reverse
   142	
   143	**The defence gets no equivalent.** This is asymmetric by construction, and
   144	I am not hiding it. Two facts make it the defensible reading rather than a
   145	gift: the defending side's landing-chase already exists and **explicitly
   146	excludes box landings** (`TeamBrain.ts:391–418` — *"box landings belong to
   147	the marking scheme"*, an unscoped first cut cost 0.77 goals/match), and
   148	T1-FLIGHT measured the defence taking **71%** of the new contests without
   149	any such help. So the asymmetry corrects an imbalance rather than creating
   150	one.
   151	
   152	Unlike T1-FLIGHT §2.4 I am **not** running the alternative as an arm: a
   153	defensive re-route is outside #32.4's authorized scope, and adding it
   154	unbidden would be exactly the improvisation the discipline forbids.
   155	Registered for the commander instead.

   178	### 4.1 A0-CENSUS — the reachability question, answered before the intervention
   179	
   180	Read-only, zero `src/**`, run first on the same block. T0's lesson:
   181	instrument before gating. It asks the one question that decides whether
   182	this mechanism can possibly work.
   183	
   184	For every H3 cross, take the nearest licensed attacking body at the kick and
   185	decompose:
   186	
   187	```text
   188	R1  REACHABLE  — his distance to the meet point is <= topSpeed x (remaining
   189	                 flight time), i.e. the routing is what failed
   190	R2  MARGINAL   — reachable within 1.15x that budget (the executor's own
   191	                 steering/accel losses live here)
   192	R3  UNREACHABLE— he could not have arrived at any routing
   193	R4  NO LICENCE — nobody was licensed at the kick at all
   194	```
   195	
   196	**A0 cannot change a single Phase-A gate value.** It can only stop the
   197	stage, by one pre-registered rule:
   198	
   199	```text
   200	STOP if  R3 + R4  >  80% of H3 crosses
   201	```
   202	
   203	**80% is derived, not chosen**: the addressable population is
   204	`(1 − R3 − R4) × 22.90%`; at the same one-in-four conversion assumption D1
   205	is powered on, an addressable share below 20% yields
   206	`0.25 × 0.20 × 22.90 = 1.15pp`, which is **below D1's 2.32pp MDE** — and
   207	#29.5 forbids running a gate that cannot distinguish its own two readings.
   208	Above the threshold the intervention proceeds; below it, the seat is
   209	pre-kick anticipation (Q2's forbidden half → Stage III) and that is the

   223	### 4.3 F — the mechanism fires (layer 1 of the six-layer chain)
   224	
   225	```text
   226	F1  LICENCE SURVIVAL. Of crosses that had >=1 licensed attacking body at the
   227	    kick, the share where >=1 licensed body is still on MakeRun at the tick
   228	    the ball first enters the header band:
   229	        A0  reported (expected near zero -- this is the defect)
   230	        A2  >= 90%                                        (seam bites, X5-class)
   231	F2  RE-ROUTE FIDELITY, per-record with NAMED exception classes (#32.1 --
   232	    NOT a max over records). On every tick where the licence is live, the
   233	    ball is above CONTROL_MAX_HEIGHT and a closest licensed body exists,
   234	    his steering target either equals `landing - flightDir*2.5` to 1e-9, or
   235	    falls into a named class:
   236	        E1  the onside clamp rewrote it (actionExecutor:547 -- inert while
   237	            the ball is unowned, so this class is expected EMPTY)
   238	        E2  the barred-box clamp rewrote it (actionExecutor:571)
   239	        E3  he stopped being the closest between decision and execution
   240	    GATE: the UNEXPLAINED residual is exactly 0. Class counts reported.
   241	```
   242	
   243	F1's 90% floor is the same seam-bites form C5 T1 used, powered the same
   244	way: at n ≈ 5,500 the binomial SE at p = 0.9 is 0.40pp, so 90% sits ~25σ
   245	below a working seam and far above a broken one — it separates *fires* from
   246	*does not fire*, which is all a layer-1 gate is for.
   247	
   248	**F1 and F2 prove the mechanism reached the world. They prove nothing about
   249	whether the world is better.** The payoff is D1.

   251	### 4.3b ⚠️ Instrument facts disclosed before the run, in their own commit
   252	
   253	Three things the implementation surfaced. None touches a gate value, the
   254	mechanism, D1's power, I2's margin, the canary's band or §6's readings.
   255	
   256	1. **F2 needs an observability field, and I added one.** The gate compares
   257	   the engine's steering target against the meet point; a probe cannot see a
   258	   local. `Player.c4Trace = { meet, applied }` is written by the executor on
   259	   the tick its branch fires and cleared at the top of every `executeAction`.
   260	   It is **never read by any decision** and is null in every flags-off world.
   261	   Without it F2 could only be *asserted* in a unit test instead of *measured*
   262	   over the run, which is the weaker thing #32.1 was trying to get away from.
   263	2. **E3 turns out to be structurally impossible, and the class is kept
   264	   anyway.** `Match.step` runs every `executeAction` in one loop, after
   265	   `simTime += dt` and before any physics or ball step, so every body executes
   266	   off the same frozen world — "he stopped being closest between decision and
   267	   execution" cannot happen within a tick. The probe replicates the executor's
   268	   own preconditions at the pre-step boundary for exactly this reason. The
   269	   class stays in the ledger; an empty class is a result, not a defect.
   270	3. **A corner takes precedence and those ticks are EXCLUDED from F2's
   271	   population, counted separately.** `crossFlight` is armed only when
   272	   `cornerCrash === null`, but a corner can begin while one is live, and the
   273	   executor's crash branch wins. This is X6's own rule seen from the other
   274	   side; the count is reported so the exclusion is visible rather than silent.

   396	Run 2026-07-27 on block 920,000, `c4Flight` ON, 2,695 matches, **5,745
   397	crosses**, twice byte-identical, SHA `17c46125…41b0`.
   398	Probe: `scripts/probes/c4-t2-a0-census.ts` (read-only, zero `src/**`).
   399	
   400	**The target replicates on a block it was not measured on** — H3 **23.03%**
   401	of all crosses against T1-FLIGHT's 22.90%, median miss **2.32 m** against
   402	2.39 m, C3atk **25.50%** against 25.17%. The population D1 is powered on is

   406	R1  REACHABLE     96.60%
   407	R2  MARGINAL       2.04%
   408	R3  UNREACHABLE    1.21%
   409	R4  NO LICENCE     0.15%

   412	
   413	Not close. The geometry is not the binding constraint anywhere: the nearest
   414	licensed body needs a median **3.35 m** against a median budget of **7.95 m**
   415	over a **1.03 s** flight — **4.86 m of slack**. A licence exists on 100% of
   416	crosses (mean 2.14 bodies) and includes the arriver on 72%.
   417	
   418	**What this does and does not license.** It is a *necessary-condition*
   419	screen and it passed with room: the bodies could be there. It says nothing
   420	about whether they will be — that is D1's question, and A0 cannot answer it.
   421	The predicate is deliberately generous (straight line at top speed), which is
   422	what R2's band existed to soften; with 4.86 m of median slack a much tighter
   423	bound would also have passed, so the reading survives the predicate's
   424	looseness rather than depending on it.

   473	```
   474	
   475	**M3 resolves and M1/M2 do not.** The bodies really did stay — 0.027 of a body
   476	more in the box at the contestable instant — and they arrived **no nearer the
   477	ball**; if anything M2 points the wrong way. The half-metre is untouched.
   478	
   479	#### 7.1.3 ⭐⭐⭐ Why: the closest licensed body was already going
   480	
   481	F2's `noTrace` bucket is the finding, not the failure. On 36,121 live-licence
   482	ticks the probe expected the re-route to fire and no trace was written, and a
   483	read-only diagnosis (660 matches, then all six cells) resolves that bucket
   484	completely:
   485	
   486	```text
   487	closest licensed body's ACTION when no trace was written  (n = 36,121)
   488	  ReceivePass  30,020  83.11%      MoveToFormationSpot  5
   489	  ChaseBall     6,095  16.87%      Dribble              1
   490	```
   491	
   492	The diagnosis reproduces the run exactly (30,276 ok, 36,121 no-trace), so it
   493	is the same population and not a re-measurement.
   494	
   495	The two real buckets are bodies **already being sent to the ball by an
   496	existing mechanism**:
   497	`ReceivePass` has carried the identical `landing − flightDir·2.5` re-route
   498	since Phase 63 (§2.1), and `ChaseBall` routes through `interceptBall`, which
   499	projects the same landing. The branch this stage added lives inside
   500	`case 'MakeRun'`, so it can only ever reach a body who is *not* one of those.
   501	
   502	**So `c4ArrivalReroute` almost never adds a new body to the descent — it
   503	mostly re-labels one that was already on its way.** That is exactly why D1 is
   504	flat.
   505	
   506	**The arithmetic, stated exactly.** Across 66,469 live-licence ticks the
   507	branch fired on **30,276 (45.6%)** and had nothing to add on **36,121
   508	(54.4%)**, because the closest licensed body was already the receiver (83% of
   509	that bucket) or already a chaser reading the same landing (17%). So the
   510	mechanism is not inert — it steers a genuinely different body on nearly half
   511	the ticks — but on the other half it is duplicating a route the engine has
   512	had since Phase 63, and **the body it does add produces no measurable extra
   513	attacking contest**.
   514	
   515	§2.1 established *that* the receiver had the re-route. What it did not ask —
   516	and what F2's population should have conditioned on — is *how often the
   517	receiver IS the closest licensed body*.
   518	
   519	#### 7.1.4 The A1 rung — the pre-registered backfire is real
   520	
   521	```text
   522	licence survival ALONE   C3atk 25.50% → 24.75%   −0.75pp  CI [−1.77, +0.29]
   523	```
   524	
   525	§4.8 named this in advance: the arriver's 16 m arc target points **away** from
   526	the landing, so holding him on it through the flight is worse than letting him
   527	go home. The re-route rung then recovers it to about zero. **The two halves
   528	roughly cancel**, which is a cleaner statement of the stage's outcome than
   529	either number alone.

   532	
   533	```text
   534	ok 30,276 · UNEXPLAINED 72 · noTrace 36,121 · E1 0 · E2 0 · E3 0 · corner 0
   535	worst |engine meet − probe meet| = 0.01574 m
   536	```
   537	
   538	Two separate defects, both mine and both at freeze time:
   539	
   540	1. **The population was mis-specified.** F2 predicted a fire for the closest
   541	   licensed body without conditioning on his ACTION, when the branch lives
   542	   inside `case 'MakeRun'`. `noTrace` is not a fidelity failure — it is the

   544	2. **72 unexplained meet mismatches**, worst 1.57 cm — and the diagnosis

   546	   every one of them with `phase: 'halftime'` and the ball state **frozen**
   547	   (`zBefore == zAfter`, velocity identical to the last digit). At half-time
   548	   `Match.step` returns before `simTime += dt`, so nothing executes: the

   550	   `p.c4Trace` still holds the last *played* tick's value. The 1.57 cm is the
   551	   gap between those two instants, held across the pause. **A stale-read
   552	   artefact of the pause, in one match — not a fidelity failure.** I named
   553	   E1, E2 and E3; I did not name *the world is stopped*.
   554	
   555	E1, E2, E3 and the corner-precedence counter came back **exactly empty**, as
